lenses.lens: PROCESS ANATOMY: how the explore -> design -> review -> refine -> authorize -> lock -> three cycles -> official run -> audit -> report -> next design -> publish -> pointer loop is actually executed, reconstructed from artifacts in about 20 deliveries dated 2026-10-06 to 10-24 (Codex on the consolidated branch; Claude on origin/charming-head)
lenses.summary:
The loop is real and heavily documented, but almost every gate is written and judged by the same agent that designed the experiment. The discipline that exists is enforced by habit, not by machines.

Codex deliveries are strong on engineering integrity: hash locks, tamper tests, preserved failures, no-rescue rules, and gates that are never lowered after results. The best example is the SAMPLE-GEN selection lock: the confirmation seeds did not exist until after the candidate was chosen. Claude's work is lighter: a REPORT plus code, with no locks or authorization records.

The weak points cluster in five places:
1. **Auditors that share code with the implementation.** In MiniFly Package B the auditor reused the same function as the code it checked, so it could not see that the relation-control arms were never disabled. E3 was void across all 832 receipts.
2. **"Three cycles" has no fixed meaning.** It has been (a) iterative revision driven by held-out results, (b) technical checks only, with performance barred from tuning, (c) two technical cycles plus a 34k–56k-record pilot, and (d) tuning on development worlds, including swapping the task and the endpoint.
3. **Qualification checks that cannot fail.** Purely technical qualification let large runs go ahead (NATIVE-BIND 147k records, VALUE-INTERACT 240 jobs) even though taught acquisition was near zero. Behavioral admission gates appeared only from 10-14 on.
4. **Authorization and scope are agent-authored.** The user's words are short ("Run it in the background", "Do the 3-cycle exercise"). The agent writes the scope, judges conditional grants itself ("If yes…" became "The audit helped."), and presents options with a "(Recommended)" label. 14 of 39 cycle deliveries have no AUTHORIZATION file.
5. **Research-level memory is prose.** There are many CURRENT pointers with stale top-level fields, status files that contradict each other, design and results committed in the same git commit (so preregistration is self-attested), held-out item sets and dev worlds reused across experiments, and standing agent rules (AGENTS.md) that live only on the user's machine.

Cross-agent review is the strongest safeguard observed. Claude audited Codex v5.1, and Codex reconciled each finding as confirmed or corrected, including correcting Claude's own overstatement. Codex in turn removed unsupported claims from Claude's v6 memo, such as calling a step "approved".

Recommended skills: a stage-gate package validator, a spec-derived independent auditor that runs a control-arm difference test, a typed cycle contract, an endpoint-change protocol, a held-out and seed registry that marks sets as "spent", an authorization recorder, mutation-tested admission gates, cross-agent adversarial review, and a lessons register that is checked by machine.

findings.title: Receipt auditor shared implementation code, so a broken causal control went undetected through a full 832-receipt run
findings.description: In MiniFly Package B, platform function branch_allows compared branch names against 'N_old_relation' while arms were named 'N_old_rel', so the relation-write controls never disabled writes. W, N_old_rel and N_new_rel end states were bit-identical in 832/832 receipts and E3 was identically 0 by construction. The receipt auditor derived its expected write ledger from the same function, so every receipt 'passed'. It was only found post-analysis when the final audit re-derived the ledger from the protocol's stated semantics, after about 28,885 s of driver time. Documents state this directly; the inference is that any auditor importing implementation helpers is subject to the same common-mode blindness.
evidence: minifly_b/REPORT.md:17-26 (headline: E3 axis invalid; 'The receipt auditor did not catch this because it derives the expected write ledger from the same branch_allows')
findings.how_detected: Final audit after the full science run, by re-deriving expectations from the protocol text instead of the shared function. Not caught by technical qualification or receipt audits.
findings.generic_safeguard: Auditors must compute expected ledgers and endpoints from SPEC.json alone and may not import implementation modules. Before any roster, run a mandatory 'control-arm differential' smoke test: for every control arm, assert that its realized write ledger and end-state differ from W exactly as the spec says (for example N_old_rel old_relation writes == 0). Fail closed.

findings.title: 'Three cycles' has no stable definition; what may be revised and which data may be read varies by delivery
findings.description: The same user phrase ('Do the 3-cycle exercise: design, audit, test run, revise') was executed in incompatible ways. (a) 10-07 addition_rule: three DEV-world test-revise iterations; after held-out 0% in cycles 1 and 2 the agent changed PN->KC wiring, then switched to a scalar ordinal output prior, and cycle 3 scored 87.5% held-out. The rule allowed 'revise one explicit structure after a documented failure'. (b) 10-11 SAMPLE-GEN: technical worlds only, and 'performance ... cannot select a candidate or tune a recipe'. (c) 10-11 multimechanism hostile audit: no candidate score may tune the operation. (d) 10-22/23 RECOVERABILITY-R2, V6-R1, ADDRESS-CAPACITY: cycles 1-2 were technical qualification and cycle 3 was the full bounded pilot. (e) 10-24 Claude LEARNED-BANK: tuning on DEV worlds, including task, metric and learning-rate changes. Attempts within a cycle are uncapped: v4 cycle 3 kept five failed-attempt directories. My inference: the cycle is the main channel through which outcome-driven model search enters, and its rules are re-invented each time.
evidence: addition_rule_dev_v1_20261007/EXPERIMENT.md:21 ('Cycles may revise one explicit common structure or content operation after a documented failure')
findings.how_detected: Not caught as a process issue. The route retrospective flagged the consequences (A03 engineered priors entering via cycles) but not the definition gap.
findings.generic_safeguard: Use a typed CYCLE_PLAN.json, locked before each cycle runs. Fields: cycle_kind (technical | dev_tuning | pilot); data_visible (synthetic | technical | DEV ids); outcome_metrics_readable (bool); revision_class_allowed (engineering_only | hyperparameter | architecture | endpoint); max_attempts; record/CPU cap. A validator rejects revisions outside the declared class. Any architecture or endpoint change after reading held-out scores spends that held-out set (see PA-04).

findings.title: Mid-cycle task and endpoint substitution, threshold picked after DEV results, and a DEV world labeled 'confirmation' (Claude LEARNED-BANK V1)
findings.description: The design's primary task was T-MOD (last digit of a+b). In cycle 2, LEARN scored 0.000 held-out on T-MOD. The agent then: ran an evaluator-side BP/DFA testbed showing MOD was not learnable from the input code (a good solvability check); switched the primary task to T-PAR (parity of a+b, a binary task); raised eta0 tenfold and lengthened training; changed the primary metric to balanced accuracy; redesigned SHUF; and, after seeing LEARN 0.824 vs FROZEN 0.331 on D2, proposed a decision rule of LEARN >= FROZEN + 0.20. The section is headed 'Native confirmation' even though D2 was a tuning world, and the commit message says 'native confirmation on D2'. Mitigations stated in the documents: main worlds M1-M4 not generated, provisional settings declared. My inference: the endpoint moved from an addition-relevant function to a 1-bit task chosen because the candidate works on it. That is objective drift relative to the contract's E3 unseen-addition goal, and nothing in the process requires user re-authorization or an objective-distance check.
evidence: same file:30 ('T-MOD tells us nothing about local learning'), :39 ('Primary task becomes T-PAR'), :59 ('Settings chosen: eta0 = 0.03 ... 10 times the provisional'), :61 ('Native confirmation (T-PAR, D2 ...)'), section 9 (proposed rule +0.20)
git log origin/charming-head: 3d5a136a 'LEARNED-BANK V1 cycle 2: testbed audit, PAR task, tuning, native confirmation on D2'
minifly_b/package/DOCS/MINIFLY_OBJECTIVE_CONTRACT.md:23-33 (required block: claim level, recitation countermodel, promotion rule)
findings.how_detected: Not yet caught. The work is pending on a branch, with no recorded review or authorization artifact.
findings.generic_safeguard: Endpoint-change protocol. Any change to primary task, metric, control or threshold after seeing candidate outcomes must log the reason, state the new endpoint's E-level and its distance from the standing objective (same relation family toward unseen addition?), and get explicit user re-authorization. Thresholds must be fixed before candidate DEV values are seen, or derived from a stated power or effect rule. The words 'confirm' or 'confirmation' are reserved for fresh, untouched worlds.

findings.title: Held-out items and development worlds are reused across design iterations, later experiments and the confirmation
findings.description: In the engineered addition lineage the same five held-out orbits (1,1),(1,2),(0,4),(2,3),(3,3), eight ordered questions, were: scored in all three addition_rule cycles that drove architecture revisions; reused in value_retention DEV; and reused in the 64-world STABLE confirmation, where only noise, order and missingness seeds were fresh. The DEV protocol itself discloses these items 'are fixed targets of the existing protocol, not claimed to be unseen by the researcher'. Separately, technical worlds 202610143901-03 are reused across lineage comparison, the addition-difficulty diagnosis, CLS v0 and v3. No global registry records which held-out sets have been 'spent' by outcome-driven decisions. The 10-06 WORLD_EXCLUSION_REGISTRY was a one-off and was not maintained. Inference: confirmation evidence is valid for these exact items but carries researcher-selection risk, and findings carried across experiments are partly re-measured on the same data.
evidence: addition_value_retention_dev_v1_20261011/EXPERIMENT.md:55 ('不伪称为对研究者从未见过的任务')
minifly_cls_dev_20261017/REPORT.md:3 ('same single-digit split as the lineage comparison and the addition diagnosis')
findings.how_detected: Disclosed by the author in the DEV protocol, but no process response followed. Cross-experiment world reuse was not flagged anywhere.
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a project-level HOLDOUT_AND_SEED_REGISTRY.json: each held-out set or world ID, its generator hash, and every delivery that read its scores, with a 'spent_by_design_decision' flag. Confirmations must draw researcher-unseen held-out relations or items where the task space allows. Otherwise the claim is capped and labeled 'held-out items previously inspected'.

findings.title: Design review and final audit are mostly self-review; independence is claimed inconsistently and agent identity is not recorded
findings.description: Most design reviews are written by the designing agent, often as self-posed question-and-answer tables. value_retention's DESIGN_AUDIT is titled '设计自审' (design self-review). native_next REVIEW.md says 'Author's document review only; no independent agent'. GATED-FEEDBACK DESIGN_REVIEW is a self-answered list of questions. Before 10-22, FINAL_AUDIT files say things like 'all_committed_jobs_independently_audited: true', meaning a separate script, not a separate reviewer. Only from 10-22 do Codex audits state 'independent_process_not_independent_reviewer'. Git does not separate agents: Codex commits are authored by the user's identity 'Pencilbard' (54 commits), next to 48 by 'Claude'. Genuine independent review exists only sporadically: a separate Codex 'mechanism-audit thread' for MULTIMECHANISM; Codex reviewing Claude v5 and v6; Claude auditing Codex v5.1; and user-relayed external reviews (RECEIVED_REVIEW.md, FEEDBACK_INTAKE) without reviewer identity metadata.
evidence: native_next_v1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:58 ('author-run bounded engineering exercise, not independent human or multi-agent review')
findings.how_detected: Partly self-disclosed in late deliveries (10-22 onward). Not treated as a blocking condition anywhere.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every REVIEW.md and FINAL_AUDIT.json carries reviewer_identity {agent, model, session/thread id} and author_identity. The stage-gate validator blocks science, confirmation and adoption when reviewer == author. Received external reviews are stored with a source field. Commits record the acting agent via a trailer.

findings.title: STRENGTH: cross-agent adversarial audit with item-by-item reconciliation (Claude audit of Codex v5.1)
findings.description: Claude re-ran parts of Codex's v5.1 code. Findings: the output-port test 'passes, but it can't fail'; byte partitions were fixed by initialization, not learning; and Codex's revised design R1 would collapse at the next stage. Codex then reproduced each item and labeled it CONFIRMED_WITH_QUANTITATIVE_CORRECTION, COUNTERFACTUAL_FAILURE_REPRODUCED, SPECIFICATION_IMPLEMENTATION_MISMATCH, LATENT_INTEGRATION_DEFECT or CLAUDE_HISTORY_STATEMENT_CORRECTED. The last one corrected Claude's claim that v3, v4 and v5.1 all stopped before arithmetic was tested. The process-level verdict was that artifact reproducibility checks had been insufficient as design and integration validation. Codex review of Claude's v5 and v6 designs works the same way (REVIEW_RESOLUTION.md; V6 REVIEW.md removed unsupported forecasts and the false 'approved'). This is the strongest guard against blind spots in self-generated next designs.
findings.how_detected: User-mediated hand-off between agents (Claude audit text pasted into the Codex workflow).
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep and formalize: after each three-cycle exercise, and before the next design is authorized, a different agent runs a hostile audit with permission to re-execute bounded diagnostics. The author must reconcile every finding with a status enum and evidence hashes.

findings.title: Technical qualification is mistaken for behavioral readiness; large science runs produce predictable near-zero results
findings.description: Three technical cycles certify equations, gradients, tamper rejection and checkpoints, but often not whether the learner acquires taught items at all. NATIVE-BIND V2.1 passed three technical cycles, then ran 72 DEV jobs (147,456 records) in which even taught OLD/NEW stayed at 0-8.3%. VALUE-INTERACT passed qualification, then ran 240 science jobs (368,640 records) with roughly 0% unseen accuracy in every new configuration. The Claude audit found the v5.1 port test 'can't fail'. The process learned from this: from 10-14, MODEL-FEEDBACK has a pre-fixed SCIENCE_ADMISSION gate and halted with NO_SCIENCE_ADMISSION; native_next B used an input-state admission gate before opening held-out outcomes; V6-R1 profiled the first complete history. Admission gates are still not mandatory or standardized.
evidence: native_next_v1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md ('The decisive arithmetic result' table; stopped before opening HELD)
findings.how_detected: Partly by the Claude audit (10-20) and by the agents' own later redesigns (admission gates from 10-14). Earlier runs were not flagged as preventable.
findings.generic_safeguard: Mandatory BEHAVIORAL_ADMISSION.json before any science or confirmation roster. Required: taught acquisition strictly above the frequency and exact-key countermodels on DEV; a positive control (oracle or solvability witness) that passes; control arms that differ from W; and a cost projection from one complete history. Every qualification check must be mutation-tested: show it fails on at least one seeded defect, otherwise it is labeled 'non-discriminating'.

findings.title: Authorization is a short user quote plus agent-written scope; the schema is inconsistent, often missing, and conditional grants are self-evaluated
findings.description: AUTHORIZATION files quote one user sentence ('Run it in the background.', 'Do the 3-cycle exercise on X', 'Good. Run it.') and the agent fills in rosters, caps and allowed stages. Key names vary (user_request, human_request, user_instruction, request, authorized_by, user, instruction). Only one file records a thread id. 14 of 39 cycle deliveries have no AUTHORIZATION file; some keep it in prose or in SPEC.json. Conditional grants are judged by the agent: 'See if this helps. If yes, revise the design and run the 3 cycle exercise' led to the report's opening line 'The audit helped.' with no predicate defined. The official STOP-ONLY confirmation records 'User: Confirm STOP-ONLY only (Recommended)', meaning the agent framed and recommended the option the user clicked. 'Keep going' and 'Stuck is not allowed' were converted into a resource-policy amendment. Strength worth keeping: stage booleans (implementation, three_cycles, formal_pilot, confirmation, push, adoption), the 'supersedes' flag in v5.1 dev, and the gated-feedback allowed and forbidden lists.
evidence: no AUTHORIZATION file: addition_rule_dev_v1_20261007, arithmetic_kernel_no_attention_dev_v3_20261013, minifly_v4_dev_20261020, native_next_v1_dev_20261023, minifly_memory_channel_v2_dev_20261022, and 9 others
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Codex once rejected a prior memo's 'approved' wording as non-authorization (minifly_v6_revised_design_20261023/REVIEW.md:12).
findings.generic_safeguard: Standard AUTHORIZATION.json schema with: verbatim user text; timestamp; session/thread id; the options and recommendation the agent presented; enumerated stage booleans; numeric caps (records, CPU, wall, worlds); and any conditional as a machine-evaluable predicate over named artifacts, with a different agent evaluating it. The launcher refuses to start without a valid record whose stage covers the action.

findings.title: Scope creep: the '3-cycle exercise' grant grew from technical caps of about 100 records to pilot-scale runs
findings.description: Technical caps under the same kind of grant: 96 records (schedule-context, 10-15) and 512 (NATIVE-BIND V2.1, 10-17). Later, the '3-cycle exercise' carried a 54,432-record native pilot (RECOVERABILITY V1), up to 46,368 (R2), 56,448 (ADDRESS-CAPACITY cycle 3), 34,816 (V6-R1), and 793,600 'technical' records (MODEL-FEEDBACK). The exercise has become the vehicle for real pilots whose results feed the catalog (for example P030 'E1 positive component'), while 'official' runs are reserved for separate grants. Labels like technical, exercise and pilot do not bound cost or evidential weight.
evidence: minifly_recoverability_v1_dev_20261022/AUTHORIZATION.json (native_records_planned 54432; 'Full declared bounded pilot as the test payload of three development cycles')
findings.how_detected: Not caught.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every authorization must carry explicit numeric caps copied from SPEC and shown to the user. A three-cycle grant without a stated cap defaults to a small fixed budget. Any cycle payload above it needs a separate user-approved number.

findings.title: Preregistration is self-attested: locks and results are committed together, and some locks post-date the first tests
findings.description: For recent deliveries, the design directory and the results directory first appear in the same publication commit: V6 revised design and V6-R1 dev in 43d04b5e; native-next in 43b07e89; address capacity in 16550151; RECOVERABILITY-R2 design and STOP-ONLY confirm in 3065bb1a; NATIVE-BIND V2.1 in 47e72101. The value_retention design directory was committed on 10-14, after its confirmation was committed on 10-12. SOURCE_LOCK and SELECTION_LOCK hashes live inside the same bundle they protect, so a third party cannot verify that locks preceded outcomes. native_next states no complete source lock covered the first fixtures. ADDRESS-CAPACITY needed a SOURCE_LOCK_AMENDMENT. By contrast, Claude's LEARNED-BANK committed DESIGN.md (4d8952c3) before any code or cycle, which gives an external timestamp.
evidence: git log --format='%h %ad' -- <dir> | tail -1 for the listed directories (same SHA for design and dev)
findings.how_detected: Partly self-disclosed (native_next). Commit-order evidence found by this audit.
findings.generic_safeguard: Push (or append to a timestamped log) SPEC.json, SOURCE_LOCK.json, the selection rule and the held-out manifest hash before the first scored value is produced. The validator compares the lock's commit time with the first result artifact's time and downgrades the claim if the lock is not earlier.

findings.title: STRENGTH: confirmation seeds generated only after selection, with DEV-only selection locks
findings.description: SAMPLE-GEN V2 selection lock records 'confirm_entropy_created': false and 'selection_uses_only_DEV': true. CONFIRM_ADMISSION records 'private_roots_drawn_after_selection': true. Value-retention keeps a DEV_SELECTION_LOCK (formal_launch_authorized false) and a separate formal SELECTION_LOCK with the fixed 64-world roster and 'additional_candidates_allowed': false. next_core_budget scanned 428,670 local files to exclude historical world IDs. addition_rule rejects unapproved world IDs in code. These choices make selection leakage into confirmation hard.
evidence: addition_rule_dev_v1_20261007/EXPERIMENT.md:33 (scientific and extra DEV IDs rejected by code)
findings.how_detected: Designed in by the Codex agent.
findings.generic_safeguard: Make it mandatory: confirmation entropy is drawn only after a hashed selection lock exists. The registry (PA-04) enforces no reuse of world IDs.

findings.title: Pointer sprawl, stale top-level fields and conflicting status files obscure the true current state
findings.description: CURRENT_ARITHMETIC_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.json still has top-level date 2026-10-15 and native_interface_transfer as its design and implementation. Its nested next_design is v5.1-R2 (planning_updated 10-20) and last_completed_native_experiment is NATIVE-BIND (10-17). V6-R1, an unseen-addition E3 attempt, is tracked under a new CURRENT_PROCEDURAL pointer, so the invariant 'arithmetic pointer unchanged' (sha 79c74951) stays formally true. native_next B's arithmetic admission test appears in no pointer. Pointers use absolute /Users/pencilbard paths. The route retrospective warned that multiple CURRENT pointers must not imply a merged system. Status files contradict each other: the root STATUS.json of addition_feedback_efficiency says TECHNICAL_QUALIFIED_SCIENCE_NOT_AUTHORIZED while results/STATUS.json says COMPLETE (456 jobs), and the census memo had to warn readers about this. Design directories are mutated into status trackers (value-interact DESIGN.json became 'QUALIFIED...' with the original kept as DESIGN_AS_DELIVERED.json; v4 DESIGN.md was overwritten by Codex's outcome and Claude's original kept as CLAUDE_BRANCH_ORIGINAL_DESIGN.md).
findings.how_detected: Partly noted by the retrospective (10-14) and the census memo (10-23). The pointer staleness was found by this audit.
findings.generic_safeguard: One append-only RESEARCH_LEDGER.jsonl (one row per delivery: id, stage reached, evidence level earned, objective hash, parent lineage, status authority path, supersedes). CURRENT pointers become generated views, never hand-edited. Design directories are immutable after delivery, and status lives only in the ledger. Paths are repo-relative.

findings.title: The objective contract's required design block is not machine-enforced; schemas are ad hoc and validators check bookkeeping, not science
findings.description: The contract requires five items in every design: claim and level, exposure audit, recitation countermodel, causal controls, and promotion and cost rule. Nothing enforces this. Each SPEC or DESIGN json invents its own schema name (about 40 distinct names). Claude-authored designs v2, v5 and the v6 memo contain no E-level, exposure or countermodel content; a keyword scan (English and Chinese) found zero hits. Validators check arithmetic, hashes, links and declared booleans: verify_design.py says 'Document integrity and count checks only', and gated-feedback's validate_design.py checks DESIGN.json flags such as attention false rather than scanning code. Banned-architecture and no-backprop constraints are therefore self-declared. Native-bind kernels used torch autograd at a time when that was allowed, and later SPECs declare 'backpropagation': false without a code check.
evidence: schema field survey across */SPEC.json and */DESIGN.json (for example ADDRESS_CAPACITY_V1, NATIVE_NEXT_V1, MINIFLY_PROCEDURAL_DESIGN, NO_SCHEMA in 3 files)
findings.how_detected: Not caught as a process gap. Codex reviews of Claude designs fixed content case by case.
findings.generic_safeguard: A shared EXPERIMENT_SPEC schema whose required fields encode contract items 1-5. Semantic validators: held-out vs exposure disjointness computed from the actual stream manifests; countermodel scores computed from permitted exposures; control-arm differential (PA-01); a static import and AST scan for banned components (attention, ELM, autograd in native modules). Static checks may not be labeled PASS unless the semantic checks ran.

findings.title: Research-level lessons are carried in prose and repeatedly re-learned or misremembered across agents
findings.description: The route retrospective (10-14) states that limits correctly written in local reports were not kept in the next design and in oral summaries. It prescribed seven continuity rules. Ten days later the census memo restates the same separations: learner identity changes and representation changes. On 10-23 Claude's v6 memo claimed the fly 'is a fixed random expansion plus a learned linear vote' and that the 254-entry register 'has no entries for sequential state'; Codex's review corrected both from the register. On 10-20 Claude's audit claimed v3, v4 and v5.1 all stopped before arithmetic was tested; Codex corrected it. EVIDENCE.json files hash the documents consulted but do not record which lessons or claims were checked. Few lessons became machine checks; the arithmetic pointer hash invariant is one exception.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014/REPORT.md:7 and the closing list of seven rules
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent review and retrospectives requested by the user.
findings.generic_safeguard: A LESSONS.jsonl register: id, trigger condition, the required check (ideally executable), source incident and evidence hash. Designs list the applicable lesson IDs and the validator runs their checks. Historical claims in designs must cite catalog row IDs (PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/FULL151_VERSION_CENSUS_20261023/EXPERIMENT_CATALOG.json) or be flagged as unsupported.

findings.title: Lineage and capability-inheritance drift: learner changes are hidden under shared names, assets and pointers
findings.description: The documents (the retrospective, A03/A06/A07/A08) show learners being replaced, or engineered priors added, while names, coordinates and pointers stayed the same. addition_rule's cycle 3 replaced native writing with a scalar ordinal readout. U042 'into the core' was packaged as a standalone ByteLearner. Generic IO built a new hash bank. KERNEL V3 changed the GRU equations, initialization, optimizer and dose at once, and its own lineage review admits it 'is not a controlled upgrade of the old core'. Later Codex deliveries partially fixed this with MODEL_MANIFEST.json, PARENT_ASSET_AUDIT.json, PARENT_CLOSURE.json and UNCHANGED_TRACK_LOCK.json, but lineage fields are not uniform. A survey of SPEC/DESIGN json found no lineage, parent or inherit keys in ADDRESS-CAPACITY, NATIVE-NEXT, RECOVERABILITY-R2 or V6-R1.
evidence: SPEC/DESIGN json key survey (minifly_address_capacity_design_v1_20261023/SPEC.json, minifly_native_next_design_v1_20261023/SPEC.json: no lineage keys)
findings.how_detected: User questioning, followed by the route retrospective (10-14). Partial structural fix afterwards.
findings.generic_safeguard: A required LINEAGE block in SPEC.json: executable parent (path + hash); retained state, write, read and feedback operations; replaced operations; added engineered priors; and inheritance_status defaulting to 'not_demonstrated'. The ledger refuses to carry a parent's E-level to a child unless an integrated test is linked.

findings.title: STRENGTH with a caveat: strong failure preservation and no-rescue rules, but a high rate of small engineering errors
findings.description: Strengths: receipt and checkpoint tamper tests (addition_rule rejected 15 receipt and 5 checkpoint manipulations); failed attempts preserved as directories; explicit no-rescue rules (V6-R1: no replay, larger readout, capacity expansion or goal change as a rescue); guards not lowered (addition_rule HOLD at 69.23% old retention against a 75% guard despite 87.5% held-out); count corrections disclosed rather than rewritten. Caveat: engineering defects recur in almost every delivery. A reversed teaching sign produced six invalid histories (v4). Import or module-name collisions hit addition_rule, value-retention confirm and V6 cycle 1. V6 had an unenforced API cap. NATIVE-BIND had a checkpoint digest that missed the cursor. native_next had a wrong test assumption and an unsaved raw support array. Seven vendor configs were silently overwritten and caught by a working-tree audit.
findings.how_detected: Mostly self-detected by tests and code review within cycles. Some only post-run (V6 API cap found while the roster was running).
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep failure preservation and no-rescue clauses. Add a standard PREFLIGHT_CHECKLIST that runs before every cycle: unique module namespace, teaching sign per output channel, API caps enforced at input, checkpoint digest covers all mutable state including cursor and RNG, raw arrays saved for every gate metric, and a clean working tree for vendored dependencies.

findings.title: Tests and gates are edited during cycles without an independent loosen/tighten classification
findings.description: native_next corrected a failing assertion ('incorrectly assumed gated=False implies zero slow-state writes') and the fixture then passed. MODEL-FEEDBACK's science-admission gate text changed between cycle 2 and cycle 3 to specify the frequency countermodel and to excuse the taught lookup upper bound, under an ops 'cycle2_gate_review'. Both look legitimate and both are documented. Still, an edit that makes a failing check pass is the canonical reward-hacking vector, and here the same agent decides whether the edit is a fix or a loosening.
findings.how_detected: Self-documented. No independent verification.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every change to an assertion, gate or threshold produces a GATE_DIFF record (old, new, classification tighten/loosen/clarify, and the triggering failure). A loosen or clarify-after-failure needs sign-off from another agent or the user before re-execution. The validator diffs gate text between the cycle snapshot and the final package.

findings.title: Results-only publication and local-only standing rules block cross-agent re-verification
findings.description: Recent publications deliberately omit raw data. The documents say the artifact-audit scripts require the omitted local evidence. A different agent, for example Claude in a cloud container, therefore cannot re-run Codex's final audits from the repository. The standing agent rules referenced by hash (/Users/pencilbard/Downloads/second_try_copy/AGENTS.md, PERSISTENT_CORE_REQUIREMENTS.md) are not in the repository, so only the local agent can read the operative rules. CURRENT pointers point to absolute local paths.
evidence: minifly_v6_r1_dev_20261023/PUBLICATION.md ('Artifact-audit scripts require the omitted local evidence')
findings.how_detected: Found by this audit. Publication scope is disclosed but its effect on auditability is not discussed.
findings.generic_safeguard: Publish a minimal verification subset: per-item held-out outputs, the exposure manifest hash and the manifest itself, and the reducer inputs for primary endpoints. Version all standing agent rules in the repo (or a synced rules package) and reference them by repo path. Use repo-relative paths only.

findings.title: 'Confirmation' passes accumulate on proxy or component endpoints far from the objective
findings.description: The only official run in the late period confirmed an evaluator-only conditional-stopping gain (+22.10pp, 32/32 pairs). Complete NEW own-output was 11.26% and OLD 0.33%, and the run is explicitly E1. The option was the agent's '(Recommended)' choice. CURRENT_EXTERNAL_MEMORY records 'confirmation_passes': true. The documents disclose the scope well. Inference: without a distance-to-objective field, pointers, catalogs and later agents can read a growing list of 'confirmed' components as progress toward E3 unseen addition. The objective contract warns explicitly against letting such scores expand silently.
findings.how_detected: Self-disclosed in the report, but no structural safeguard.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every PASS or confirmation record must carry: earned E-level; the objective metric value (retained exact own-EOS unseen addition per sample and compute) measured in the same run, or 'not measured'; and objective_distance (component, E1, E2 or E3). Ledger and pointer views display the objective metric next to any pass. Spending confirmation budget on an E1 component requires a user choice that was not framed with a recommendation, or a written rationale linking it to the E3 path.

findings.title: STRENGTH: user constraints encoded as machine invariants and explicit non-execution receipts
findings.description: 'Keep the arithmetic track unchanged' was turned into arithmetic_pointer_sha256 = 79c74951..., checked in RECOVERABILITY, STOP-ONLY, ADDRESS-CAPACITY and the V6 EVIDENCE files. Designs carry 'executed_by_delivery' zero counters and authorization booleans. verify_design.py asserts that every authorization flag except 'design' is false, and that Claude's original blob SHA matches the preserved copy. Received designs and reviews are stored verbatim with hashes (CLAUDE_RECEIVED.md, DESIGN_RECEIVED.md, RECEIVED_REVIEW.md). The census has an executable verify_catalog.py. These are the most reusable, already machine-checkable parts of the loop.
findings.how_detected: Designed in by the Codex agent.
findings.generic_safeguard: Generalize: every standing user constraint gets an invariant ID with a check (a hash, an AST scan or a state assertion) evaluated at lock time and at final audit.

process_observations: STAGE ANATOMY. Explore/search lives in PROJECT_DOCUMENTS memos and screens (MECHANISM_SCREEN_20261007/*, NEXT_ROUND_PRIORITY*, FEEDBACK_INTAKE_20261015, FULL151 census MEMO/CATALOG/MECHANISMS_254) and in Claude memos and catalogs (minifly_cls_dev_20261017/MEMO_NEXT_STEPS.md; human_learning_mechanisms_20261023 on origin/charming-head). Recent designs record what was consulted only as EVIDENCE.json hashes. This stage is judgment-only and is often done by the agent who will run the experiment.

DESIGN files changed over time. 10-06..10-17: EXPERIMENT.md plus DESIGN.json (Chinese/English) plus DESIGN_REVIEW.md or STATIC_REVIEW.md plus DESIGN_STATIC_CHECKS.json. From 10-20: DESIGN.md plus SPEC.json plus EVIDENCE.json plus REVIEW.md or STATIC_REVIEW.md plus STATIC_CHECK(S).json plus verify_design.py. Claude designs are DESIGN.md only, with no SPEC, lock or authorization. There is no shared schema: about 40 distinct schema names.

REVIEW / HOSTILE AUDIT: true hostile audit by a separate thread appears once (addition_multimechanism_v1_design_20261011/HOSTILE_AUDIT.md). Cross-agent review happens on the Claude<->Codex v4/v5/v6 hand-offs and the V51 audit. User-relayed external reviews are kept verbatim (RECEIVED_REVIEW.md, FEEDBACK_INTAKE). Everything else is author self-review, usually in self-answered 'question | handling' tables.

REFINEMENT shows up as amendments and resolutions: AMENDMENT_01.md (pre-cycle, before endpoints), REVIEW_RESOLUTION.md (v5 to v5.1, findings F01-F10), REVISED_DESIGN.md / NEXT_DESIGN.md in dev directories, and SOURCE_LOCK_AMENDMENT.json. Refinement before implementation is common. Refinement after results is folded into 'cycles'.

AUTHORIZATION: the user speaks at four kinds of points. (1) Approve a design or ask for a three-cycle exercise. (2) Launch science or confirmation ('Run it in the background'). (3) Publish ('Push the results, not the raw data'). (4) Adopt, park or redirect: the U042 adoption in CURRENT_ADDITION_CORE.json; '保持加法主任务，语言方案暂存' (keep addition as the main task, park the language plan) in native_interface_transfer_dev_v1_20261015/ops/AUTHORIZATION.json; the noise-direction correction recorded in the retrospective, A05. Scope is always written by the agent. GitHub push is separately authorized in most Codex runs, a good pattern.

LOCKS: SOURCE_LOCK.json in 36 of 39 cycle deliveries. RUNTIME_MODULE_CLOSURE.json, PRE_VALUE_ASSET_LOCK.json, PARAMETER_LOCK.json, SELECTION_LOCK.json, HEAD_FREEZE.json and KEY_AUDIT.json appear only in some, mostly 10-20 onward. All are hash lists, machine-checkable for integrity but not for timing (PA-10).

THREE CYCLES: 39 deliveries have cycles/. File layout varies: cycle{n}/DESIGN.md, AUDIT_BEFORE_TEST.md and AUDIT_AND_REVISION.md (10-07); cycle{n}/AUDIT.md and REVIEW.md (10-17/20); CYCLE{n}_PLAN.json, RESULT.json and REVIEW.md (10-22); 01_..03_ prefixed files (V6-R1); CYCLE{n}.md (Claude). The best variant is minifly_transformer_external_memory_v1_r1_20261022/SPEC.json, where each cycle has status PLAN_LOCKED_BEFORE_EXECUTION plus runner_sha256 plus design_sha256 plus CPU ceiling plus seed. Its self_audit booleans are still self-asserted.

OFFICIAL/SCIENCE RUN: results/ holds LAUNCH.json, AUTHORIZATION.json, SELECTION_LOCK.json, CONFIRM_ADMISSION.json, STATUS.json, DEV/CONFIRM subdirectories and bundle parts. Conditional confirmation chains exist (DEV -> lock -> fresh roots -> CONFIRM). Behavioral admission gates exist only from 10-14 (MODEL-FEEDBACK SCIENCE_ADMISSION.json).

FINAL AUDIT: FINAL_AUDIT.json is a separate reducer or auditor process by the same agent. Contents range from about 180 bytes (a status line) to 333 KB (minifly_a_v3, independent score arithmetic over 1.15M rows). Explicit 'not independent reviewer' language appears only from 10-22.

REPORT and NEXT DESIGN: REPORT.md consistently states the earned evidence level and keeps negative results. NEXT_DESIGN / REVISED_DESIGN are always self-authored proposals flagged 'not authorized'. The V51 audit showed they can encode the same blind spot (R1 would collapse again).

PUBLICATION / POINTER: PUBLICATION.json or PUBLICATION.md plus PUBLICATION_MANIFEST.json, a pre-change pointer snapshot in *_POINTER_HISTORY/ (38 snapshots for arithmetic alone), then a hand-edited CURRENT_*.json. Pointer history is preserved (good), but pointers mix stale top-level fields with nested updates (PA-12).

STAGES MOST OFTEN MERGED OR SKIPPED: independent design review (merged into author review); behavioral admission (skipped before 10-14); authorization file (14/39 missing); final audit by another party (almost always skipped); preregistration push before outcomes (design and results committed together); for Claude deliveries, every lock, authorization and final-audit artifact.

MACHINE-CHECKABLE TODAY: hashes and source closure, roster counts, tamper rejection, read-only probe parity, pointer-hash invariants, catalog evidence hashes (verify_catalog.py), document links and arithmetic. JUDGMENT-ONLY TODAY: claim level, exposure audit, countermodel adequacy, whether a revision was allowed, whether a conditional authorization was met, objective distance, lineage and inheritance.

IDEAL MINIMAL MACHINE-CHECKABLE PACKAGE, built from the best existing parts: (1) SPEC.json on a shared schema with required contract fields: claim_level_target, task and split generator hash, held-out manifest hash, exposure ledger definition, countermodels, control arms with expected ledger differences, primary endpoint formula, gates, stopping rules, resource caps, DEV vs main roster, constraint invariants, LINEAGE block (pattern: minifly_v6_revised_design_20261023/SPEC.json plus verify_design.py). (2) EVIDENCE.json: consulted reports by hash plus applicable LESSON ids. (3) AUTHORIZATION.json: verbatim quote, timestamp, session id, options presented, stage booleans, numeric caps, machine predicates for conditionals (pattern: minifly_v5_1_dev_20261020/AUTHORIZATION.json plus arithmetic_gated_feedback_dev_v2_20261014/AUTHORIZATION.json). (4) REVIEW.md plus REVIEW_RESOLUTION.json written by a different agent, with a per-finding status enum (pattern: V51 AUDIT.json). (5) SOURCE_LOCK.json plus RUNTIME_MODULE_CLOSURE.json plus PRE_VALUE_ASSET_LOCK.json, pushed before the first scored value. (6) cycles/CYCLE{n}_PLAN.json (locked: kind, data visibility, revision class, attempt cap, runner sha), CYCLE{n}_RESULT.json, CYCLE{n}_REVIEW.md, GATE_DIFF.json. (7) CONTROL_DIFFERENTIAL.json (each control's realized ledger vs W, derived from SPEC). (8) BEHAVIORAL_ADMISSION.json (taught acquisition above countermodels, positive control or solvability witness, mutation-tested checks). (9) KEY_AUDIT / EXPOSURE_AUDIT.json (held-out never in any teaching, calibration or listening stream) plus a HOLDOUT_REGISTRY entry. (10) SELECTION_LOCK.json with confirm_entropy_created=false, then CONFIRM_ADMISSION.json with private_roots_drawn_after_selection (pattern: addition_sample_generalization_dev_v2_20261011/results). (11) RESOURCE_LEDGER.json including failed attempts. (12) FINAL_AUDIT.json from an auditor that imports no implementation code, with reviewer_identity. (13) REPORT.md plus SUMMARY.json with earned E-level, objective metric value and objective_distance. (14) NEXT_DESIGN.md flagged as a proposal. (15) PUBLICATION_MANIFEST.json plus a minimal verification subset. (16) A ledger row appended; pointers regenerated. A single validator script checks presence, schema, timing order and the semantic checks, and refuses launch, confirmation, adoption or pointer update on failure.

CROSS-BRANCH NOTE: origin/charming-head (Claude) follows a lighter loop: DESIGN.md committed first, then cycle notes with unit checks (34/34) and solvability testbeds, which are good habits. It has no lock, authorization, selection lock or independent review artifacts, and it tunes and changes endpoints within cycles (PA-03). Codex and Claude conventions are not unified, and consolidation produced path collisions (minifly_v4_design_20261020/DESIGN.md).

skill_recommendations.name: experiment-package-validator (stage gate)
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any implementation, cycle, science launch, confirmation, adoption, push or pointer update, run a validator on the delivery. It requires the stage-appropriate files on a shared schema (SPEC.json with contract fields 1-5 plus LINEAGE, EVIDENCE.json, AUTHORIZATION.json covering the stage, SOURCE_LOCK pushed earlier than any result, CYCLE_PLAN locks, SELECTION_LOCK before confirmation entropy, FINAL_AUDIT with reviewer_identity != author). It refuses the action on any failure.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Required stages are skipped or merged in many deliveries (14/39 missing authorization; same-commit preregistration; ad hoc schemas). Habits differ between Codex and Claude, so only a machine gate makes the loop's discipline survive agent turnover (PA-05, PA-08, PA-10, PA-13).

skill_recommendations.name: spec-derived-independent-auditor
skill_recommendations.rule: Audit code may read only SPEC.json, manifests and raw outputs; importing implementation modules is forbidden. Before any roster, run a control-arm differential smoke test asserting that every control's realized write ledger and end-state differ from W exactly as the spec predicts, and that each held-out key never appears in any teaching, calibration, listening or replay stream.
skill_recommendations.rationale: MiniFly Package B's auditor shared branch_allows with the implementation, so a dead E3 control passed 832 receipt audits (PA-01). The same common-mode pattern applies to any shared helper.

skill_recommendations.name: typed-cycle-contract
skill_recommendations.rule: Each cycle starts with a locked CYCLE_PLAN.json declaring kind (technical / dev_tuning / pilot), visible data, whether outcome metrics may be read, allowed revision class, attempt cap and record/CPU cap. Revisions outside the class are rejected. Any revision made after reading held-out scores marks that held-out set as spent.
skill_recommendations.rationale: 'Three cycles' has meant everything from technical checks to outcome-driven architecture search (PA-02, PA-03, PA-09). This is the main entry point for researcher degrees of freedom and reward hacking.

skill_recommendations.name: endpoint-change-and-objective-distance-protocol
skill_recommendations.rule: Any change to primary task, metric, control or threshold after candidate outcomes are visible must log the trigger, the new E-level and its objective_distance from 'retained exact own-EOS unseen addition per sample and compute', and get explicit user re-authorization. Thresholds are frozen before candidate DEV values are seen. 'Confirm' is reserved for untouched worlds. Every PASS displays the objective metric next to it.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Prevents silent drift to easier proxies (T-MOD to T-PAR; conditional stopping 'confirmed' while complete recall is 11%), as in PA-03 and PA-19, and the retrospective's A01/A05 history.

skill_recommendations.name: holdout-and-seed-registry
skill_recommendations.rule: Keep PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/HOLDOUT_REGISTRY.json listing every held-out set and world ID with its generator hash and every delivery that read its scores or used it for a decision. New designs must draw unused IDs. Confirmations must use researcher-unseen held-out relations or items where possible; otherwise the claim carries an 'items previously inspected' cap.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The same eight held-out addition questions guided the revisions and then served as the 64-world confirmation. Technical worlds 202610143901-03 were reused across four experiments. The 10-06 world-exclusion registry was never maintained (PA-04, PA-11).

skill_recommendations.name: authorization-recorder
skill_recommendations.rule: Record every user grant as AUTHORIZATION.json with: verbatim text; timestamp; session or thread id; the exact options and recommendation the agent showed; stage booleans; numeric caps; and conditionals written as machine predicates that a different agent evaluates. Never infer authorization from memo wording such as 'approved'. Turn pressure phrases ('keep going') into scoped amendments only with the caps restated to the user.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Scope is currently written by the agent being authorized. 'If yes' conditions were self-judged, and recommended-option framing steered the confirmation choice (PA-08, PA-09).

skill_recommendations.name: behavioral-admission-with-mutation-tested-qualification
skill_recommendations.rule: No science or confirmation roster runs without BEHAVIORAL_ADMISSION.json. Required: taught acquisition strictly above the frequency and exact-key countermodels on DEV, a passing positive control or solvability witness (oracle, learned-linear, BP/DFA testbed), and a passing control differential. Every qualification check must be shown to fail on a seeded defect, or it is reported as non-discriminating.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Technical-only qualification let large runs proceed with near-zero taught acquisition (NATIVE-BIND V2.1, VALUE-INTERACT). A port test that 'can't fail' was counted as qualified (PA-07). The fix already exists in MODEL-FEEDBACK and native-next; this rule makes it standard.

skill_recommendations.name: cross-agent-hostile-audit-and-reconciliation
skill_recommendations.rule: After each three-cycle exercise and before the next design is authorized, a different agent audits code, artifacts and the proposed next design, with permission to run bounded diagnostics. The author reconciles each finding with a status enum and evidence hashes in AUDIT.json. Historical claims by either side must cite catalog rows.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The V51 Claude audit plus Codex reconciliation caught design-blocking defects and corrected overstatements in both directions. Self-authored next designs repeat blind spots (PA-06, PA-14).

skill_recommendations.name: lessons-register-as-executable-checks
skill_recommendations.rule: Maintain LESSONS.jsonl: id, trigger, check (script or assertion), source incident and evidence hash. Each design lists the applicable lesson ids and the validator runs their checks. When a post-mortem finds a defect class, add a lesson with an executable check before closing the incident.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The retrospective's continuity rules and the census's separations had to be restated repeatedly. Only a few lessons, such as the arithmetic pointer hash, became machine invariants (PA-14, PA-15, PA-20). This is the main way findings transfer from one experiment to the next.

skill_recommendations.name: single-ledger-derived-pointers
skill_recommendations.rule: Append one row per delivery to RESEARCH_LEDGER.jsonl (stage, earned E-level, objective metric, parent lineage, status-authority path, supersedes). Generate CURRENT_* views from it. Never edit design directories after delivery. Use repo-relative paths, version the standing agent rules in-repo, and publish a minimal verification subset.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Stale pointer top-level fields, conflicting STATUS files, design files reused as status trackers, local-only AGENTS.md and raw-data-free publications prevent other agents from verifying the true state (PA-12, PA-18).

skill_recommendations.name: gate-diff-guard
skill_recommendations.rule: Any edit to an assertion, gate or threshold after it has failed produces GATE_DIFF.json classified as tighten, loosen or clarify. Loosen or clarify-after-failure needs sign-off from another agent or the user before re-running.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Editing a failing check to make it pass is the canonical specification-gaming move. Current cases (native-next assertion, MODEL-FEEDBACK gate wording) were self-classified (PA-17).

skill_recommendations.name: preflight-engineering-checklist
skill_recommendations.rule: Before every cycle, run a standard preflight: unique module namespace and import-path isolation; teaching-sign check per output channel; API input and output caps enforced at entry; checkpoint digest covering all mutable state (cursor, RNG, resources); raw arrays saved for every gate metric; clean working tree for vendored dependencies; resource profile from one complete history.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Small engineering errors recur in nearly every delivery: sign reversal, import collisions, API cap gaps, checkpoint cursor gaps, missing raw supports, overwritten vendor configs. They cost cycles and sometimes whole histories (PA-16).

lenses.lens: INCIDENT CATALOG: documented things that went wrong or nearly went wrong in the MiniFly research loop (explore -> design -> refine/audit -> 3 test cycles -> official run -> audit/search), with origin stage, catching stage, detector, verdict impact and a reusable safeguard
lenses.summary:
I catalogued 39 incidents from the repository docs, the cycle folders and git state. Labels in the descriptions: "Documented" means the files say it; "Inference" is my own reading. The culture is strong on disclosure: failed attempts are kept in cycles/, verdicts are not quietly rewritten, and posthoc work is labelled as posthoc. Prevention is weak. The same failure classes keep coming back across deliveries: import/module collisions (4 times), missing dependencies or environment drift (at least 6), calls and cost undercounted (at least 5), raw evidence lost when an assertion fails (4), and gates that cannot fail or cannot pass (4).

The expensive incidents were almost all caught late:
- **Package B (minifly_b):** the relation no-write branch was never instantiated, so E3 is void after 832 receipts and 80 core-hours. The final audit found it after the analysis; the receipt auditor reused the faulty function.
- **v4:** a reversed teaching sign was found only after 6 complete histories had run.
- **V6-R1:** the cue-vs-noise scale problem (about 0.0027 vs 0.1) was found only after the whole roster had run.
- **STOP-ONLY:** the "confirmed" +22pp gain was measured against a decoder that scores zero. The next delivery showed that a fixed always-stop-after-1-byte rule gets 10.6% against STOP's 11.3% on NEW, and beats STOP on OLD.
- **R2:** stopped at its resource limit with birth-2 controls missing, so it gave no efficacy verdict.

Cross-agent review caught a large share of errors in both directions:
- Codex corrected Claude's analytic claims: the running-mean reference, the dose read from attenuated writes, the decay sign-invariance argument, and mixing numbers from different decoders.
- Claude found that the v5.1 port gate could not fail, that the v5.1 byte-stage outcome was fixed by the starting values, and that Codex's revision would fail at the next stage.
- Codex in turn corrected a false history claim in Claude's audit.

The causes at research level are the ones the Route Retrospective names (A01–A10): the objective shrinking to taught-association retention, engineered or independent learners credited to "the core", user adoption read as confirmation, and mechanism-name aliasing. These recur because the limits written in each local report do not carry into the next design. Newer incidents of the same kind are softened gate labels ("largely met"), a "confirmation" run on a tuning world, a mid-cycle task switch to parity, and proxy metrics (loss, teacher-forced bit accuracy) that improve through marginal byte statistics alone.

The safeguards proposed below are mechanical:
- an arm-distinctness check against an oracle written from the spec
- a falsifiability and satisfiability check on every gate
- a ladder of trivial-heuristic baselines
- a cheap pre-run check that inputs produce distinct codes (E0 discrimination)
- results written to disk before any assertion runs
- import and environment closure locks
- a claim-label linter
- a lineage/inheritance contract
- task-substitution sign-off

findings.title: Package B relation no-write branch never instantiated (branch-name mismatch) -> W and N_old_rel identical, E3 void
findings.description: Documented: shared locked platform function branch_allows compared against 'N_old_relation'/'N_new_relation' while branches were named 'N_old_rel'/'N_new_rel', so relation writes were never disabled; end-state digests of W, N_old_rel, N_new_rel identical in 832/832 receipts and all 8,320 relation probe blocks bit-identical; E3=0 by construction for all six variants (80.3 learner core-hours). The receipt auditor derived its expected ledger from the same branch_allows, so it could not detect the defect; found only post-analysis when the (unlocked) final audit re-derived the ledger from the protocol's stated semantics. Origin: implementation inherited from REFERENCE_SOURCE (design). Should have been caught: refine/audit or technical qualification (a single technical receipt shows N_old_rel performing 288 old-relation writes; the later corrected scaffold's causal_branch_gate rejects exactly that receipt). Verdict impact: E3 axis declared INVALID (not a null); E1 retained; mechanism register marks T/S E3 'invalid, family not excluded'; Package A v3 rebuilt with explicit five-branch map and a causal_branch_gate.
findings.how_detected: Post-science final audit re-deriving write ledger from protocol text, after the full 832-receipt roster; the in-loop receipt auditor missed it because it shared code with the system under test
findings.generic_safeguard: Arm-distinctness preflight on the first technical receipt: for every causal/no-write arm, assert (a) its write ledger equals counts derived independently from the spec text (oracle not importing learner/platform code) and (b) its end-state digest differs from W where the spec says it must. Auditors must never reuse the predicate they audit.

findings.title: v5.1 isolated output-port gate could not fail; fixture density did not match the candidate
findings.description: Documented: the port passed exactly from the first round (8 records, strength 0.004); with the zero-value reference and non-overlapping activity patterns, any write with the right sign gives the right bit and decay cannot flip a sign, so pass and 1-hour retention were guaranteed by construction (Claude audit). Codex reconciliation found the port lock claimed 'same native active fraction' while the fixture hard-codes 0.02 vs native 0.0354 (cycle2.py:8-12). Origin: design of the qualification fixture. Should have been caught: design review/refine_audit by asking 'what learner would fail this gate?'. Caught: Claude cross-agent audit after publication; confirmed by Codex. Verdict impact: port reinterpreted as narrow disjoint-frame wiring/sign E1, not dose qualification; overlapping-memory interference untested.
findings.how_detected: Claude cross-agent audit of Codex commit b01df0d6, after the three cycles were published; reconciled by Codex with source line evidence
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate falsifiability check: every gate must be run against at least one known-bad learner (random-sign writes, shuffled targets, overlapping patterns at the real activity density) that must FAIL, and fixture parameters must be read from the candidate's locked config, not hard-coded.

findings.title: v5.1 learned byte identity aliased 12 byte types into 8 units, fixed at birth by random init; revision fixed only one of two competitive layers
findings.description: Documented: winner-only competitive Hebbian learning kept the birth partition (6-7 of 8 settings identical to pre-listening partition); usage bias thousands of times too weak; 200k listening bytes changed nothing. Claude ran Codex's next-stage context-class code on a perfect byte stage and it collapsed to one class (same dead-unit problem plus prototype scale mismatch), so the R1 revision 'guarantees another NO_ADVANCE'. The v5 design review (F03) had already warned that stability can let collapsed codes pass. Origin: design (generic competitive-layer defect). Caught: the v5.1 identity gate failed correctly in cycle 3; Claude's audit diagnosed cause in about a second and showed R1 incomplete. Verdict: NO_ADVANCE; R1 not executed unchanged; R2 used farthest-first initialization in both layers and reached 0 aliases.
findings.how_detected: Written gate failed in test cycle 3 (good); root cause and next-stage failure found by Claude cross-agent audit with seconds of compute
findings.generic_safeguard: Birth-state diagnostic before any cycle: for every competitive/clustering layer report initial-vs-final partition, dead units, occupancy and scale of prototypes vs inputs; when a generic defect is found, apply the fix to all layers of the same type and run the whole chain once in a fast harness before formal qualification.

findings.title: v5.1 threshold calibration omitted the REPLY transition and used frames not matching training/prediction frames
findings.description: Documented: calibration skipped REPLY so the reply-step bank was absent during calibration (latent, not executed because M2 failed); calibrating on actual prefeedback frames reduced massive cutoff ties; first-answer KC codes shared ~70% of active cells across unrelated prompts. Origin: implementation during refinement. Should have been caught: refine_audit frame-equivalence test. Caught: Codex reconciliation diagnostics prompted by Claude audit. Verdict: no published verdict change (branch unexecuted) but recommended next work changed; R2 calibrated on the same passive/REPLY/pre-answer/EOS frames.
findings.how_detected: Post-publication reconciliation audit using counterfactual diagnostics (21 CPU-s)
findings.generic_safeguard: Frame-equivalence test: any calibration/normalization statistic must be computed on frames produced by the exact same code path and event types as training and query, asserted by digesting frame-type sequences.

findings.title: v4 teaching coefficient sign reversed; six complete histories and a seventh partial run with wrong sign; zero-replay slice bug invalidated a B0 history
findings.description: Documented: port residual negated relative to the native signed-write convention; 6 complete invalid jobs (432 record applications) plus 16 records of a seventh; detected by a new directional source-to-port audit; a zero-replay slice bug also produced an invalid B0 history; the run was stopped by a read-only admission fence. Also v3: 'an initial readout projection error was corrected before comparisons'. Origin: implementation in test cycle 3. Should have been caught: cycle-1 refine_audit with a directional fixture and positive control. Verdict: histories marked valid_for_model_efficacy=false and excluded; corrected runs on fresh technical worlds; Codex acknowledges 'my implementation's reversed sign and replay defect must be excluded from efficacy'.
findings.how_detected: Codex self-audit (new directional fixture) during cycle 3, after invalid histories had already run
findings.generic_safeguard: Mandatory directional sign test before any history: one write per output class must move the matched-control margin toward the target versus a passive branch, plus a generic positive control that must learn; this test is part of the source lock and re-run whenever the port code changes.

findings.title: v4 'strict' no-early-commitment gate was not strict, and its G0 coverage gate ordering was circular
findings.description: Documented: the recurrence-gate sigmoid permits 0.899% slow allocation at q=0, so it is not a strict 'nothing permanent before confirmation' rule; the pre-learning G0 coverage gate is circular if useful segment codes require learned boundaries; v4 also changed input encoding, output ports, population, commitment, segmentation, task length and repetition at once. Origin: design. Should have been caught: design review (static check of the spec's claimed invariant). Caught: Codex self-report at end of v4; v5 design added a strict slow floor. Verdict: interpretation narrowed; no efficacy claim.
findings.how_detected: Codex end-of-exercise report
findings.generic_safeguard: For every invariant stated in prose (strict, zero, read-only, identical), add an executable assertion that checks the boundary case numerically (e.g. allocation at q=0 == 0.0), and check that gate ordering does not require a capability produced by a later stage.

findings.title: V6-R1 cue signal ~37x weaker than sampling noise by design; full roster run before checking input-dependent addressing
findings.description: Documented: birth weights SD 0.05/sqrt(348)≈0.00268 per active symbol column versus content-proposal noise SD 0.1; posthoc fixed-tape diagnostic: same-prompt/different-tape KC Jaccard ~0.01-0.02 versus different-prompt/same-tape ~0.98-0.99 (input effect 1/70-1/87 of noise). All 8 histories (34,816 records, ~3,060 CPU-s) scored 0% OLD/NEW/held exact, own EOS 0%, truncation 100%. Origin: design (LEARNING_RULE.md lines 9,17 contain both numbers). Should have been caught: design static check or a 1-second E0 input-identity check before the roster. Caught: Codex posthoc localization after the roster. Verdict: NO_DEMONSTRATED_UNSEEN_ADDITION_GAIN; follow-up native_next tested rescaled births which still failed support admission before training. Claude's later learned-bank design adopted an 'Input-identity gate at birth (V6 lesson)'.
findings.how_detected: Codex posthoc saved-state diagnostic after the full bounded roster
findings.generic_safeguard: E0 discrimination preflight before any learning roster: compute same-input/different-noise vs different-input/same-noise code similarity (and an analytic signal/noise ratio from the init formulas) and require a prespecified separation; failure stops the roster.

findings.title: Proxy metrics improved through marginal output statistics while exact own-output stayed at zero
findings.description: Documented: in V6-R1, final outputs were 98.6-99.9% identical to a repeated mode byte 0x31 predicted from observed bit priors plus truncation, explaining the 'apparent loss improvement'; in v5.1-R2, teacher-prefix bit/loss improvements 'can reflect common output statistics while free answers remain wrong' (e.g. 7+7= -> 1125); v4 directional fixture lowered residual loss 0.131655 -> 0.129958 while exact reply stayed 0%. Origin: metric choice during test cycles. Caught: Codex posthoc; primary exact own-output endpoint protected the verdict. Inference: if any gate had been defined on loss or teacher-forced bit accuracy this would have been a reward-hacking pass.
findings.how_detected: Codex posthoc localization; locked exact-output endpoint prevented a false pass
findings.generic_safeguard: Any proxy metric (loss, bit accuracy, teacher-forced accuracy, rank separation) must be reported next to marginal/mode/frequency countermodels and an input-shuffled control; proxies may never be gate endpoints for E1/E3 claims.

findings.title: V6-R1 independent reducer and diagnostics written after baseline probes; audit assertions added while roster active
findings.description: Documented: the artifact reducer was implemented during the pilot, after baseline queries, before probe scores were inspected; saved-output/address localization scripts added after first OLD_END inspection; marginal diagnostic added after first-world outputs showed repeated ASCII '1'; roster-uniqueness assertions added while roster active. Main scoring/gates frozen beforehand; disclosed in AUDIT_SOURCE_LOCK.json. Related: native_next had no prospective complete source lock for first fixtures; Package B final audit not in SOURCE_LOCK. Origin: test_cycle process. Verdict: none changed; strongest 'all reduction code before probes' contract not met.
findings.how_detected: Self-disclosure by Codex in the audit lock
findings.generic_safeguard: Lock scoring, reducer and gate code before the first probe; anything added later is automatically tagged POSTHOC by file timestamp vs lock and cannot feed a gate. Keep allowing extra posthoc audits (Package B shows they find real bugs) but label them.

findings.title: Recurring import/module-name collisions across deliveries
findings.description: Documented: v4's first launch failed through a cross-delivery import chain (v4 common -> v3 bootstrap -> minifly_a_v3/src/stores -> z1_model -> bytecore native); v5.1 'early module-name collisions and overly literal pickle hashing'; recoverability v1 cycle 1 'import namespace collision'; V6-R1 cycle 1 evaluator 'import data' resolved to an inherited module after the native bootstrap modified sys.path; ERROR study needed an analysis-only import-path repair before final calculation. Each cost a failed technical attempt; no science contaminated. Origin: cross-cutting engineering (sibling delivery folders on sys.path, generic module names). Should have been caught: preflight import-closure check.
findings.how_detected: Runtime failures in technical cycles (each time after compute was spent)
findings.generic_safeguard: Import-closure preflight: run with an isolated interpreter (-I), explicit import roots, delivery-prefixed module names, and assert every imported module's __file__ is inside the locked closure before any record.

findings.title: Dependency, asset and environment restoration problems (missing files, silent config drift, unhashed runtime closure)
findings.description: Documented: native_next bootstrap failed on a missing canonical config and an environment without numba; filling absent upstream files from the vendor package silently changed 7 later-iteration configs, caught by a working-tree audit and restored to HEAD bytes; v5.1-R2 first startup failed because psutil was absent; ADDRESS-CAPACITY found incompatible NumPy/Numba and used a cached runtime; CLS imports the native fly from minifly_a_v3/src and an extracted package/ not in git; V6-R1 source lock covered vendor copies rather than actual upstream birth-asset locations; recoverability V1/R2 did not prospectively hash the full runtime dependency closure. Verdicts unchanged but reproducibility weakened.
findings.how_detected: Launch failures and working-tree audits by the executing agent
findings.generic_safeguard: Environment/asset manifest (package versions + content hashes of every runtime file and birth asset) verified at process entry; restoring files from a vendor copy requires a byte diff against the tracked version; runtime import closure snapshot saved before first value.

findings.title: Cross-platform non-determinism of the Full151 newborn PN->KC matrix
findings.description: Documented: remote agents (Muse and Claude Code) found a raw Linux-built newborn had the correct Q digest but a different B data digest; the source Mac reproduces the original; fix was to ship a canonical B asset and verify a 30-field birth fingerprint; Package B recorded raw_B_match:false and installed canonical B. Origin: birth formula (seeded Gaussian jitter + numeric exponential). Caught: remote verification gate before science. Verdict: none (caught before science).
findings.how_detected: Remote bundle verification by two independent agents before science
findings.generic_safeguard: Content-addressed birth assets plus a birth fingerprint check on every host; never rebuild stochastic assets on a new platform without digest comparison.

findings.title: NATIVE-NEXT EOS fixture used BASE's residual for every arm and omitted BEGIN/end boundaries
findings.description: Documented: the initial EOS fixture did not exercise each arm's own native residual and lacked record boundaries, so its observations were 'provisional, not evidence for the proposed EOS learner'; cycle 3 corrected fixtures to use each arm's own residual and boundaries. Origin: fixture authoring (refine_audit). Caught: cycle-2 audit by the same agent. Verdict: initial component pass withdrawn, then re-earned on corrected fixture.
findings.how_detected: Within-delivery cycle-2 audit
findings.generic_safeguard: Fixtures must call each arm's own code path; add an assertion that arm-specific intermediate quantities (residuals, margins) differ across arms where the design says they should, otherwise the fixture is flagged as non-discriminating.

findings.title: False test assertion (gated=False implies zero slow writes) corrected after it failed
findings.description: Documented: an expanded fixture failed an assertion that slow writes must be zero; the agent classified it as an erroneous test assumption, corrected the assertion, kept the native allocation and states 'no native equations or allocation fraction were changed to make the fixture pass'; the failed attempt and assertion log are preserved. Inference: this was a legitimate correction, but 'edit the assertion after it fails' is exactly the path that reward hacking would take, and the only safeguard here was self-attestation in an author-run exercise ('not independent human or multi-agent review').
findings.how_detected: Assertion failure in cycle 3; reclassified by the authoring agent
findings.generic_safeguard: Assertion-change protocol: any change to a failing test requires (1) a written derivation from the spec showing the old assertion was wrong, (2) a new negative test showing the corrected assertion still fails on a known-bad implementation, (3) both versions preserved, (4) review by a different agent before results count.

findings.title: Undercounted calls, costs and parameters; count caches out of sync
findings.description: Documented: NATIVE-NEXT's original SUMMARY omitted passive reference calls (preserved, corrected in REPORT); failed-import and failed-revision CPU/RSS not captured; V6-R1 technical private-generation calls timed but not individually counted (bounded at 300) and stage-1 import CPU not timestamped; v4/v5.1 failed-attempt CPU not itemized; Package A ledger persisted_receipts cache stayed at 829 vs 832; RECOVERABILITY R2 head.py header says 5,801 parameters vs actual 5,537. Because the objective is per-sample and per-actual-compute efficiency, undercounting biases the target metric itself.
findings.how_detected: Self-audits at report time; not by an automated reconciliation
findings.generic_safeguard: Two-source accounting: count events from the learner's own counters AND independently from saved receipts/telemetry and require equality; record process-tree CPU/RSS/wall from process entry through failure; documentation constants (parameter counts) generated from code, never typed.

findings.title: Evidence not persisted before gates/assertions, so failures could not be rebuilt
findings.description: Documented: NATIVE-NEXT raw support arrays were not saved in the initial gate run, so CYCLE2 metrics cannot be independently rebuilt; R_center cycle-3 assertion aborted before writing its qualification receipt (repair: 'save the measured values before an assertion can discard them'); RECOVERABILITY V1 first/fourth-pass training probes omitted and cannot be recovered; v5.1-R2 per-event mixed-sign/spacing telemetry not retained; ADDRESS-CAPACITY lacks per-event L2/clipping diagnostics.
findings.how_detected: Post-run audits found gaps that could not be filled
findings.generic_safeguard: Write-before-assert: every gate computation persists its raw inputs and outputs to an append-only file before evaluating pass/fail; the auditor checks that every gate decision has a matching raw artifact.

findings.title: R_center operations test failed because ru_maxrss inherited parent/fork history (measurement instrument error)
findings.description: Documented: the cycle-3 operations attempt exited at a 'ru_maxrss < 128 MiB' assertion; independent reproduction showed the child's ru_maxrss equalled the parent's (188 MB) while its own VmHWM was ~21 MB; classified as infrastructure/test-instrumentation failure; repair measures the child's VmHWM without raising the threshold; failed attempt kept charged. Origin: test instrumentation (refine_audit).
findings.how_detected: Independent failure classification review with a synthetic reproduction
findings.generic_safeguard: Validate every measurement instrument on a synthetic case with known value (large-parent/small-child) before using it in a gate; repairs must not relax thresholds.

findings.title: v5.1-R2 stopped at resource limit: controls of birth 2 missing, dose never reached intended strength
findings.description: Documented: RESOURCE_LIMIT_NO_EFFICACY_VERDICT; arms were processed sequentially (R-W, A-W, R-N_OLD, R-SH_OLD), so birth-2 R-N_OLD reached 463 records and R-SH_OLD 0, i.e. the causal controls were what got cut; the 16-record profile projected 539.1 CPU-s of production but evaluation added ~409 s and the controller stopped at 900.07 CPU-s; the schedule only rose to strength ~0.040 by record 640, below the 1/16 ceiling, so 'this is not a full-strength acquisition test'. Missing endpoints were correctly not filled. Origin: test_cycle planning. Should have been caught: cycle-2 resource profiling including evaluation, and a dose-reachability check.
findings.how_detected: Resource bound triggered during the bounded addition chain; reported honestly
findings.generic_safeguard: Budget-robust roster: profile full per-history cost including evaluation; order execution so each paired world (W plus all controls) completes before the next starts; check analytically that the warmup schedule reaches its intended strength within the planned records.

findings.title: Official runs interrupted by workspace loss and host-budget rules; caps amended mid-run
findings.description: Documented: ERROR-vs-R_center was blocked at 26/64 worlds after a workspace loss (world 320027 finished but its output was not preserved), the conservative recovery charge projected over the 18 h host cap; a later approved 24 h allowance permitted continuation, plus an analysis-only import-path repair. RESPONSE_MECHANISMS lost 202 observed lives and recomputed 217; worker cap amended 8 -> 12 h and concurrency 1 -> 2. Package B ran across two agent sessions with container restarts, in-flight world-arms rerun from scratch. Science settings unchanged; amendments disclosed.
findings.how_detected: Durable checkpoints/recovery verification; disclosed in blocker and final reports
findings.generic_safeguard: Pre-register contingency rules for infrastructure loss (allowed cap extension, rerun-from-scratch policy) before launch; write-ahead durable receipts per world; amendments may touch only operations and must be separately approved and logged.

findings.title: STOP-ONLY official confirmation measured against a weak comparator; trivial fixed-length stopping nearly matched it
findings.description: Documented: the confirmation (32 pairs, 225,792 records) reported +22.10pp conditional stopping gain over DIRECT, a decoder that scores 0% complete recall. Codex's review of Claude's memo noted the direct decoder is 'a very weak stopping baseline' and an always-stop-after-one-byte rule could reach up to 12.5%. The next delivery measured fixed endpoint-1 = 10.645% vs STOP 11.263% on NEW, and fixed endpoint-1 beat STOP on OLD (0.977% vs 0.326%): 'most of the benefit over zero-scoring DIRECT is generic stopping calibration'. Origin: comparator choice at design (recoverability R2 / STOP confirmation). Should have been caught: design review before the official run. Verdict: official confirmation left formally unchanged but its interpretation was substantially downgraded.
findings.how_detected: Codex design review after the confirmation, then measured from saved responses in ADDRESS-CAPACITY cycle 1
findings.generic_safeguard: Trivial-heuristic baseline ladder required before any confirmation: constant, frequency/mode, fixed-length, position-only and input-scrambled variants must be computed on the same saved states; a component gain counts only over the strongest of them.

findings.title: ZERO/FOREIGN lesion controls changed both payload and stopping inputs, so they could not isolate memory-dependent stopping
findings.description: Documented: 'the current ZERO/FOREIGN implementation changes the response tensor used for both payload and stopping, so it tests the whole memory contribution rather than isolating memory-dependent stopping'; ADDRESS-CAPACITY cycle 1 revised it so 'foreign input changes EOS only' and measured 4.85% for foreign EOS input. Origin: control design. Caught: Codex review after confirmation.
findings.how_detected: Codex review of Claude's next-step memo
findings.generic_safeguard: For each control, write the single causal path it is meant to cut and assert, with a dataflow check, that all other inputs to the scored decision are unchanged.

findings.title: CREDIT protection treatment barely applied (0.3-1.3% attenuation) and its matched control failed literal matching
findings.description: Documented: measured CREDIT plastic-increment attenuation 0.312% (OLD) and 1.335% (NEW), mean active gate 0.9952 ('this particular gate barely reduced most updates'); UNIFORM matched control had 88 unmatched compartment-events; every-pair protection gate False.
