The null therefore says almost nothing about protection. Origin: design (dose of intervention). Should have been caught: qualification (realized-dose manipulation check). Caught: report-time analysis. Verdict: 'native CREDIT protection null' entered the census as a failed recipe.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/FULL151_VERSION_CENSUS_20261023/MEMO.md (priority 3 row: CREDIT recipe does not work)
findings.how_detected: Codex write-ledger analysis after the roster
findings.generic_safeguard: Manipulation check: in qualification, measure the realized magnitude of the intervention (e.g. fraction of update mass changed) and require a prespecified minimum effect before running the roster; record 'treatment not delivered' distinctly from 'treatment failed'.

findings.title: 'Population size' intervention also changed wiring and self-write gain; existing helper did not implement the proposed experiment
findings.description: Documented: Codex found Claude's proposed '5177 -> 20000 cells, same active count' was not what fresh_bank() did (same fraction, rescaled Q, B not enlarged); in the implemented EXPAND, self-write gain differed ~6.9% and cross-write 0.046 vs 0.020, 'ruling out describing the experiment as population size alone'; EXPAND cost ~3.15x CPU and 4x state. Census: 'expansion also changes wiring/self-gain, cannot attribute to pure N, does not prove compute efficiency'.
findings.how_detected: Codex source reading before implementation, then cycle-2 fixture measurement
findings.generic_safeguard: Implementation-vs-hypothesis check: list which quantities the hypothesis says change and which must stay fixed, and measure all of them on fixtures before the run; label multi-factor interventions as such.

findings.title: Tempting posthoc metrics and cross-model number mixing (payload bypass, evaluator-chosen threshold, 99% rank)
findings.description: Documented: RECOVERABILITY V1's posthoc recombination (native payload signs + frozen head EOS) gave 13.28-13.80% NEW complete exact against a negative primary, explicitly 'not a preregistered candidate' and not substituted; its 99.22% EOS rank separation relies on an evaluator-chosen per-query threshold (fixed-threshold decisions valid only 21.88%). Claude's later memo cited the 99% number as if it described the STOP-ONLY model; Codex: 'it should not be combined casually'. Verdict: primary negative retained.
findings.how_detected: Self-labelling by Codex; cross-agent correction of Claude's reuse
findings.generic_safeguard: Every reported number carries provenance tags (model/decoder version, preregistered vs posthoc, oracle-assisted vs not); a claim linter rejects sentences combining numbers with different provenance tags.

findings.title: Significance tests computed on floating-point residuals of algebraically zero effects (p≈0.032 artifact)
findings.description: Documented: in RESPONSE_MECHANISMS, H-FE0 F/G/interaction components are algebraically invariant; observed differences were cancellation residuals (~1e-17), yet the locked analysis produced p=0.032 for g12/g1 with a nominal interval below zero; the independent auditor mismatched four p-values only because of subtraction order. Disclosed as 'numerical artifacts, not evidence for an H effect'; no primary result affected.
findings.how_detected: Independent auditor reproduction failure, then supplemental review
findings.generic_safeguard: Before any statistical test, compare the effect magnitude with a numerical-noise floor (for example 1e3 x machine epsilon x scale) and with known algebraic invariances; invariant quantities are checked as implementation identities, never significance-tested.

findings.title: Tautological equality interpreted as causal evidence (teacher-forced vs own-output exactness)
findings.description: Documented: RAW-RULE findings treated 41/199 teacher-forced complete = 41/199 own-output complete as showing teacher forcing does not rescue compounding; correction: for deterministic greedy decoding they are necessarily equivalent, so it is only a consistency check; the informative evidence is per-position (137 of 158 failures are first-byte errors).
findings.how_detected: Read-only interpretation review by Codex
findings.generic_safeguard: Tautology check in review: for each claimed comparison ask whether the two quantities could differ under the model's own definition; if not, demote to a consistency check.

findings.title: Gate that could not be passed: strict improvement required over exact taught-key lookup
findings.description: Documented: MODEL-FEEDBACK warm acquisition sanity used the maximum of exact/canonical lookup and frequency controls; exact taught-key recall has upper bound 1, so a strict improvement gate over it is impossible; corrected before cycle 3/formal science by comparing E1 acquisition only with the global answer-frequency baseline, all E3 gates unchanged. The design's 'same real 0/1' wording also had to be reinterpreted as 'same judging rule'.
findings.how_detected: Codex cycle-2 gate review
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate satisfiability check: an oracle/positive-control learner must be able to pass every gate and a null learner must fail it, both computed before the first cycle; a gate changed in cycles must keep all E3 gates fixed and be logged with reason.

findings.title: Capability attributed across different learners: native Full151 -> residual -> COV-R/SUPPORT -> generic hash bank -> GRU kernels narrated as one 'MiniFly core'
findings.description: Documented (route retrospective): Full151's native addition test was replaced within one three-cycle exercise by role-partitioned input, a scalar ordinal readout and custom residual writes; later COV-R had 31 weights and a 31x31 matrix with no operative fast/slow/adapt; the generic byte IO was a new 4096x257 hashed bank; KERNEL V3 changed GRU equations, init, readout, precision, optimizer, credit window and dose at once, and was called 'based on the old design'. Old ANSWER-0 had ~280 presentations per problem vs 5.5-11.4 in the new tasks, so 'the same fly lost its intelligence' is unsupported. Reports disclosed locally; the drift happened in cross-round narration. Detected: user disputes and the Oct-14 retrospective. Verdict: no frozen verdict changed; inheritance contract required.
findings.how_detected: User challenge plus retrospective audit across many rounds (late)
findings.generic_safeguard: Lineage/inheritance contract in every design: name the executable parent, list each persistent state/write/readout/feedback path as retained/replaced, and attach every inherited result to its task, priors, dose and learner branch; inheritance of capability defaults to 'unproven' when the substrate changes.

findings.title: U042/COV-SUPPORT adopted 'into the core' without confirmation; adoption meant a separate package and the promised comparison anchor was not carried forward
findings.description: Documented: user instruction '我决定让它进入核心' adopted COV-SUPPORT although the frozen verdict was NO_ADVANCE_RETAIN_COV_R, confirmation worlds 0, scientifically confirmed incremental gain false; posthoc reanalysis gave BLURRY NEW −0.83pp [−3.79,+2.12]. Implementation was a standalone ByteLearner package, not a Full151/R_center transplant; generic byte work then used different learners and anchors (A06). The name U042 originally meant independent write and forget gates; SUPPORT has no forget gate (A10). Adoption itself was legitimate; the incident is ambiguous core identity and missing migration contract. Scope clarified on 2026-10-14.
findings.how_detected: Route retrospective and later scope clarification
findings.generic_safeguard: Separate record types: USER_ADOPTION, SCIENTIFIC_CONFIRMATION, ENGINEERING_REFERENCE, CANDIDATE; any CURRENT_* pointer must state executable identity and which later experiments actually use it; adoption never upgrades evidence level.

findings.title: Objective shrinkage: reusable learning narrowed to taught-association retention; noise handling became the main question
findings.description: Documented: Sept 21-26 FB1/PostV5-V9.7 concentrated on whether taught cues return after new writes; BYTE-CORE-1 claimed headline was not recitation although an exact key-to-consequence table was not excluded; all-256-pair ORDER task could not show rule discovery. The Sept-26 audit and MINIFLY_OBJECTIVE_CONTRACT (E0-E4) were created, yet the pattern recurred. A05: after SAMPLE-GEN the next question became better handling of wrong answers under blurry feedback, staying on the engineered addition specialist; the user corrected the priority. Old rationales such as 'E3 is only optional', '24 keys', '99.12% retention' were later explicitly retired.
findings.how_detected: Historical drift audit (Sept 26) and user correction; recurrence detected only by the Oct-14 retrospective
findings.generic_safeguard: Objective-contract check at every design and every next-step memo: the primary endpoint must be one that an exact-key/canonical-key table and frequency shortcuts fail; any reprioritization away from the stated objective requires explicit user sign-off recorded in the design.

findings.title: Mechanism identity aliasing and duplicate 'novel' proposals
findings.description: Documented: U055 was wrongly assigned to 'multi-observation joint re-estimation' and listed as a next direction; it actually maps to M094 KC-KC recurrence/DPM feedback; a previous direction ranking omitted already-tested REPLAY-P and TOPO-G; source code showed REPLAY-P already samples by cached absolute-residual priority, so proposing selective replay as new is 'insufficient novelty'. Overlapping 108/136/254/71/16 inventories must not be added. Caught by Codex rescreen and an assistant source audit.
findings.how_detected: Codex rescreen and source audit
findings.generic_safeguard: Before proposing a mechanism, query the register by operation signature (equation, substrate, task, feedback contract), not alias; a proposal must cite the nearest tested version and state the material difference.

findings.title: Cross-agent analytic overclaims (mostly Claude's design memos) corrected by the other agent
findings.description: Documented: Codex's v5 review found (F01) Claude's running-mean output reference would absorb a persistent learned bias; (F02) 'no answer information reaches M2/M3' was false because D0 listening includes correct answers; (F05) dose constants derived from v4 writes measured with attenuated coefficients; v4 retrospective overstatements ('no segments ever formed'). Codex's review of Claude's later memo: 'STOP-ONLY adds only 1-5 points' did not describe the confirmation; the sign-invariance argument under decay is incorrect (counterexample 2e^{-t/τf} − e^{-t/τs}); 'old traces ten times smaller' not established. Codex's v6 revision called Claude's 'only a fixed linear lookup' an overstatement. Reverse direction: Claude's v5.1 audit claim that v3/v4/v5.1 all stopped before any arithmetic test was corrected by Codex (v3 ran full addition histories). Claude accepted most v5 corrections in its v5.1 audit.
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent design review before implementation (good catch timing)
findings.generic_safeguard: Every quantitative or invariance claim in a memo must ship with a tiny executable check (counterexample search, source-line citation of the measured coefficient); a cross-agent review is mandatory before a design memo becomes a design lock.

findings.title: Gate outcomes softened and native credit over-attributed in Claude's CLS report
findings.description: Documented: G1 memory target was ≥95%, result 84-88%, reported as 'largely met'; G4 'met in part'; unseen sums reported with 'mean best during training 20%' (peak on held-out during training); 'the native mushroom body can now be the memory' although the gain depends on four new wrapper mechanisms (FE-PERM, one-sided homeostasis, adaptation reset, error-corrective delta) and a fixed C16 output codebook, with lineage native cores at 0-8%; an earlier causal explanation (homeostasis suppressed the operator byte) was wrong and self-corrected. Limits are disclosed (3 technical worlds, no statistics). Census memo later says CLS cannot be claimed as successful mechanism fusion. Inference: label softening on a failed gate is the reporting-level form of reward hacking.
findings.how_detected: Not caught at the time; later census memo bounded the claim
findings.generic_safeguard: Claim-label linter: gate results must be reported as PASS/FAIL against the prespecified threshold with no qualitative upgrades ('largely', 'in part'); held-out numbers must be at the prespecified checkpoint, never best-during-training; attributions must name every non-native component in the answer path.

findings.title: Learned-bank (charming-head) switched primary task from addition-digit to parity mid-cycle and called a tuning-world run 'native confirmation'
findings.description: Documented: after T-MOD (last digit of a+b) failed and even exact BP could not generalize from 74 prompts, cycle 2 made T-PAR (1-bit parity of a+b) the primary task, set the learning rate 10x the provisional value after surrogate tuning on D2/D3, and ran a 'Native confirmation' on D2, which was also a tuning world; the text says 'not yet a result; the main run decides'. Codex's same-day NATIVE-NEXT revision says a 'counting/parity curriculum... cannot stand in' for the arithmetic answer. The same cycle caught real flaws: a binary-label derangement teaches anti-parity (not a control) and a constant answer would score 0.68 plain accuracy (switched to balanced accuracy). Inference: risk of objective shrinkage and evidence-label inflation at lock time; not yet a completed incident because the main run has not been locked or executed.
findings.how_detected: Partly self-caught (controls); task substitution not flagged; identified in this review by comparing with the objective contract
findings.generic_safeguard: Task-substitution guard: changing the primary task or metric during cycles requires an explicit mapping to the objective contract (which E-level and which part of exact own-EOS unseen addition it supports) plus user sign-off; runs on worlds used for tuning can never be labelled confirmation.

findings.title: NATIVE-BIND: 24 then 72 science jobs on a learner that barely acquired taught facts; final report omitted planned diagnostics; auditor initially accepted a tamper
findings.description: Documented: V2.1 review records reporting_deficiency 'final-only report omitted planned immediate acquisition, delay losses and EOS diagnosis'; descriptive analysis of V1 shows W OLD taught exact 8.3% before rest and 1.25% after; V1 24 jobs and V2.1 72 jobs both NO_ADVANCE. During V2.1 qualification 'the initial tamper was wrongly accepted' (preserved) and an inherited checkpoint did not bind cursor/resource. Inference: scale escalated without first establishing taught acquisition, contrary to the contract's 'cheap preflight before costly run'.
findings.how_detected: Post-run read-only review; tamper false-accept caught by later auditor test
findings.generic_safeguard: Acquisition precondition: no multi-world E3 run until taught exact acquisition on the same pipeline exceeds a prespecified level in a cheap pilot; report template auto-fails if any planned diagnostic is missing.

findings.title: Package A V2 results existed only as conversation testimony; no runner, locks or receipts to audit
findings.description: Documented: Claude's intake found no Muse runner, source hashes, SPEC_LOCK/SOURCE_LOCK, receipts, stop record, P3 failure receipt or roster amendment, only 'Muse status as conversation testimony only'; V2 E1 not asserted valid and P3 failure not independently confirmed; a new, separately named Package A v3 was built from the corrected scaffold. P3 remains 'technically unqualified'.
findings.how_detected: Claude intake audit
findings.generic_safeguard: No-artifact-no-claim: a result enters the register only with a hashed bundle (source lock, receipts, status); agent testimony is recorded as testimony with zero evidence weight.

findings.title: Branch/publication hygiene: retired branch name reused after one-branch consolidation, colliding with a legacy tag, based on a stale tip
findings.description: Documented: consolidation retired 18 remote heads, set codex/minifly-consolidated-20261023 as the only branch (github_remote_head_count 1) and kept old names as immutable tags. Inference from git state: remote now has 4 heads; claude/charming-clarke-u9g850 exists both as a branch (3d5a136a, LEARNED-BANK work dated Oct 24) and as a legacy tag (19107b68), and that work is based on pre-consolidation 19107b68, not merged into HEAD, 76 commits behind. Earlier publication issues: GitHub 100 MiB limit forced split archive parts; git add/push failures on the U042 branch; a v4 design add/add conflict resolved by preserving both versions.
evidence: git log origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850 (3d5a136a); git log origin/charming-head..HEAD | wc -l = 76
findings.how_detected: Consolidation audit for the earlier issues; the post-consolidation collision is identified in this review (not caught yet)
findings.generic_safeguard: Publication preflight: new work must branch from the canonical head; refuse branch names equal to existing tags or retired names; verify after push that the head count and ancestry match the consolidation policy.

findings.title: Comparisons changed many factors at once, preventing attribution
findings.description: Documented: v4 vs v3 changed input encoding, output ports, cell population, commitment, segmentation, arithmetic length and repetition policy ('these tests do not isolate which change explains the difference'); KERNEL V3 changed 6+ implementation dimensions plus data range and dose at once; Claude's address-capacity memo proposed three fixes combined into a new version (Codex: test one controlled change). Route retrospective A09: comparisons mixed budgets and evidence stages.
findings.how_detected: Codex self-report and reviews, after the runs
findings.generic_safeguard: One-factor rule for attribution: a design that claims a mechanism effect must change one declared factor against an unchanged parent; multi-factor packages are labelled 'integrated intervention' and cannot support mechanism attribution.

findings.title: Held-out leakage through pretraining listening and through segment-closure timing (caught at design review)
findings.description: Documented: v5 D0 listening included correct answers, so 'no answer information reaches M2/M3' was false and sampled presentations could repeat held facts; segment closure using the expected digit's class would 'leak a future target'. Resolution in v5.1 design: globally partition semantic unordered operand pairs (both orientations) before any stream and count all heard answer bytes; R2 counted 18,329 correct answer bytes in D0 against sample efficiency. This is an example of the loop working: caught before implementation.
findings.how_detected: Codex design review before implementation
findings.generic_safeguard: Exposure audit as code: partition held orbits before generating any stream; assert at every learner input (listening, teaching, replay, calibration, fitting) that no held pair and answer co-occur; a before/after event-timing table for every state update.

process_observations: Disclosure is strong, prevention is weak. Nearly every incident is honestly preserved: cycles/*failure* folders, FAILURE.json, posthoc labels, verdicts not rewritten. But the same classes recur across deliveries: import collisions (v4, v5.1, recoverability v1, v6_r1, ERROR), missing dependencies/environment (native_next, R2, address capacity, CLS, v6_r1), undercounts (native_next, v6_r1, v4, v5.1, Package A ledger). Lessons stay in reports and are not turned into executable checks that travel with the next delivery.

Detection timing skews late and expensive. The highest-cost defects were caught after the full roster or official run: Package B E3 (after 832 receipts), v4 sign (after 6 histories), V6-R1 cue/noise (after 8 histories), STOP-ONLY comparator (after the 225,792-record confirmation), R2 resource stop. In most cases a cheap pre-run computation would have caught them: an arm-distinctness digest, a directional fixture, an analytic SNR or E0 discrimination check, a trivial-baseline ladder, or a cost profile that includes evaluation.

Auditors that share code or assumptions with the system under test are blind. Package B's receipt auditor reused branch_allows. NATIVE-NEXT and V6-R1 were 'author-run' with self-audit only. The bugs that were caught were mostly caught by (a) an audit that re-derived expectations from protocol text, (b) a different agent (Claude on v5.1; Codex on Claude's v5 and address-capacity memos), or (c) the user, for objective and lineage drift.

Cross-agent review is the most productive control and it works in both directions. Codex caught Claude's analytic overclaims: running mean, dose, decay sign, '1-5 points', mixing decoders. Claude caught Codex's gate that could not fail and its init-determined outcome. Codex corrected Claude's history claim. Reviews that happened before implementation (v5 F01-F06, address capacity) prevented runs; reviews after publication only reinterpreted them.

The 'three cycles' loop mostly produces engineering qualification. The catalog shows many deliveries ending in E0/E1 or NO_ADVANCE before any valid E3 test (v3/v4/v5.1/R2/V6-R1/native_next). The route retrospective's core diagnosis is that limitations recorded in local reports were not carried into the next design. That is the research-level failure of 'generalizing from unit knowledge': findings are not indexed by scope, so later rounds over-inherit them (A03-A09) or rediscover them (U047 vs REPLAY-P).

Gates show both failure modes: vacuous (v5.1 port, H invariants tested statistically, teacher-forcing tautology) and unsatisfiable (MODEL-FEEDBACK strict improvement over exact lookup). Neither was found by a systematic check. Each was found ad hoc by a reviewer.

Proxy metrics repeatedly look like progress without conditional learning: loss, teacher-forced bit accuracy, rank separation with an evaluator threshold, conditional stopping against a zero baseline. The exact own-output/own-EOS endpoint and countermodels (exact/canonical lookup, frequency, suffix) protected the verdicts every time they were locked as primary. This is the main existing anti-reward-hacking asset and should be mandatory.

Labels drift more than numbers. Wording incidents include 'largely met', 'met in part', 'native confirmation' on a tuning world, 'reward' for a dense byte-loss signal (flagged by Codex in v6 DESIGN.md:80), 'based on the old design', and 'entered the core'. The numbers underneath were usually correct. A claim-label linter tied to the E0-E4 ladder would address this cheaply.

Not every apparent change is drift. Narrowing to addition-only was an explicit user decision (addition_core_lineage_comparison_design_v1_20261014/EXPERIMENT.md:3). Model changes and backprop references were authorized. The retrospective is careful not to count authorized changes as violations. Skills should separate 'authorized scope change, recorded with date' from 'silent objective drift'.

Budget and infrastructure events are common: workspace loss, container restarts, host caps. They are handled conservatively (charges retained, no partial-cohort analysis). However, cap amendments were approved mid-run (ERROR 18->24 h; response_mechanisms 8->12 h). Pre-registered contingency rules would remove discretion at the moment of temptation.

skill_recommendations.name: arm-distinctness-and-manipulation-check
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any science, on the first technical receipt: (1) re-derive each arm's expected write ledger from the spec text with an oracle that imports no learner or platform code; (2) assert end-state digests differ between W and every no-write/lesion arm where the spec says so; (3) measure the realized magnitude of every intervention (fraction of update mass, gate attenuation) and require a prespecified minimum. Record 'treatment not delivered' separately from 'treatment failed'.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Would have caught the Package B branch mismatch (INC01) on one technical receipt instead of after 832. It also exposes the near-inert CREDIT gate (INC22) and unequal matched controls.

skill_recommendations.name: gate-falsifiability-and-satisfiability
skill_recommendations.rule: For every gate, run a known-bad learner (random-sign writes, shuffled labels, input-scrambled, constant/mode output) that must FAIL and an oracle/positive control that must PASS, at the candidate's real operating parameters read from its lock. Reject the gate if either check is violated. Reject tautological comparisons (quantities equal by definition) and significance tests on algebraic invariants or effects below a numerical-noise floor.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Covers the v5.1 port that could not fail (INC02), the unsatisfiable MODEL-FEEDBACK gate (INC27), the teacher-forcing tautology (INC26) and the floating-point p-value artifact (INC25).

skill_recommendations.name: trivial-baseline-ladder
skill_recommendations.rule: Every component or E1/E3 claim is scored against the strongest of: exact and canonical key lookup, frequency/mode output, fixed-length and position-only rules, input-shuffled and foreign-input controls, all computed from the same saved states. A gain counts only over the strongest baseline. Proxy metrics (loss, bit accuracy, teacher-forced accuracy, rank with evaluator threshold) can never be gate endpoints.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The STOP-ONLY confirmation was mostly generic stopping calibration (INC20). V6-R1 loss improvements came from the marginal byte 0x31 (INC08). Exact own-EOS endpoints plus countermodels were the only consistently effective defense against reward hacking.

skill_recommendations.name: e0-discrimination-and-whole-chain-preflight
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any learning roster: compute an analytic signal-to-noise estimate from the init formulas, plus a measured same-input/different-noise vs different-input/same-noise code-similarity table. For every competitive layer, compute initial-vs-final partitions, dead units and occupancy. Run the full byte->representation->native->own-output chain once in a seconds-scale harness. Any failure stops the roster.
skill_recommendations.rationale: V6-R1's cue/noise imbalance (INC07) and v5.1's init-determined aliasing and next-stage collapse (INC03) were each visible within seconds and cost full cycles.

skill_recommendations.name: directional-and-frame-equivalence-fixtures
skill_recommendations.rule: Mandatory, source-locked fixtures before any history: (1) each output class's single write moves the matched-control margin toward its target versus a passive branch; (2) calibration and normalization use frames produced by the identical code path and event types as training and query, checked by a digest of frame-type sequences; (3) each arm's fixture calls that arm's own residual and code path.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Prevents the v4 reversed sign that produced 6 invalid histories (INC05), the v5.1 REPLY-free calibration (INC04) and the NATIVE-NEXT shared-BASE-residual fixture (INC13).

skill_recommendations.name: assertion-change-protocol
skill_recommendations.rule: A failing test or assertion may be edited only with: a written derivation from the spec showing the old assertion was wrong; a new negative test showing the corrected assertion still fails a known-bad implementation; both versions preserved; and review by a different agent before any result produced after the edit counts.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The NATIVE-NEXT slow-zero correction (INC14) was legitimate. But 'edit the test after it fails' is the primary engineering route to reward hacking, and that correction relied only on self-attestation.

skill_recommendations.name: write-before-assert-and-two-source-accounting
skill_recommendations.rule: Persist the raw inputs and outputs of every gate before evaluating it. Count every native call, passive/reference call, failed attempt, import and bootstrap cost from the learner's own counters and independently from saved receipts, and require equality. Record process-tree CPU, RSS and wall time from process entry through failure. Generate documentation constants (parameter counts) from code.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Unrebuildable gates (INC16) and undercounts (INC15) recur in at least 5 deliveries. The objective is per-sample and per-actual-compute, so accounting errors bias the target metric directly.

skill_recommendations.name: runtime-closure-and-import-isolation-lock
skill_recommendations.rule: Launch with an isolated interpreter (-I) and explicit import roots, using delivery-prefixed module names. Before the first record, assert that every imported module's __file__ and every birth asset hash is inside the prospectively locked closure, and that package versions match the manifest. Never restore files from vendor copies without a byte diff against tracked versions.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Import collisions (INC10) and dependency or environment drift (INC11, INC12) recurred across at least 6 deliveries. Each cost a failed technical cycle and weakened reproducibility.

skill_recommendations.name: budget-robust-roster
skill_recommendations.rule: Profile one complete history, including evaluation, checkpoints and reductions, before committing the roster. Execute paired units (a world with W plus all its controls) atomically, so that a resource stop leaves only complete pairs. Check analytically that the warmup and dose schedule reaches its intended strength within the planned records. Pre-register contingency rules for infrastructure loss; budget amendments may touch only operations.
skill_recommendations.rationale: v5.1-R2 lost exactly the causal controls of birth 2 and never reached full dose (INC18). Official runs had caps amended mid-run (INC19).

skill_recommendations.name: claim-label-linter
skill_recommendations.rule: Before publishing, lint every summary sentence against the E0-E4 ladder and the gate table. Gate results must read PASS or FAIL against the prespecified threshold, with no 'largely', 'in part' or 'promising'. 'Confirmation' is allowed only on fresh, untouched worlds. 'Reward' is allowed only for scalar 0/1 feedback. 'Core', 'based on', 'inherited' and 'native' each require a lineage entry. Held-out numbers must come from the prespecified checkpoint, never best-during-training. Numbers carry provenance tags (model/decoder, preregistered/posthoc) and cannot be combined across tags.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Label drift was more frequent than numeric error. Examples: CLS 'largely met' (INC33), learned-bank 'native confirmation' on a tuning world (INC34), the 99% rank number reused across decoders (INC24), and 'entered the core' (INC29).

skill_recommendations.name: lineage-and-transfer-ledger
skill_recommendations.rule: Every design opens with an inheritance table: the executable parent (commit/path), and each persistent state, write rule, readout and feedback path marked as retained, adapted or replaced. Every inherited finding is cited with its scope tuple (task, input priors, feedback regime, dose per item, learner branch, evidence level). When the substrate changes, inheritance of capability defaults to UNPROVEN. Mechanisms are referenced by operation signature, not alias. A 'new' proposal must cite the nearest tested version and state the material difference.
skill_recommendations.rationale: This is the research-level form of 'generalizing from unit knowledge' (INC28, INC31, INC38). Findings must transfer only within their demonstrated scope, and they must not be rediscovered as novel.

skill_recommendations.name: objective-and-task-substitution-guard
skill_recommendations.rule: At every design lock and next-step memo, verify that the primary endpoint is exact own-output with own EOS on unseen instances, with OLD protected, and that an exact-key table and frequency shortcuts would fail it. Changing the primary task, metric or priority (for example addition -> parity, or generalization -> noise handling) requires an explicit mapping to the objective contract plus dated user sign-off. Authorized scope changes are recorded as such, not as drift. User adoption is recorded as USER_ADOPTION and never upgrades the evidence level.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the route-retrospective objective shrinkage (INC30), noise-priority drift, and the parity substitution (INC34), while not punishing user-authorized narrowing such as addition-only.

skill_recommendations.name: mandatory-cross-agent-pre-implementation-review
skill_recommendations.rule: Any design memo containing a quantitative or invariance claim, and any final report, gets an independent review by a different agent before lock or publication. The reviewer must (a) re-derive at least one key number from source or measurement files, (b) look for a counterexample to each invariance claim, (c) state what learner would fail each gate. Agent testimony without artifact bundles has zero evidence weight.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Reviews before implementation prevented runs (v5 F01-F06 including the leakage findings in INC39; address capacity INC23). Reviews after publication only reinterpreted results (INC02, INC20). Claims without artifacts could not be audited at all (INC36).

skill_recommendations.name: branch-and-publication-preflight
skill_recommendations.rule: New work branches from the canonical head. Refuse branch names equal to existing tags or retired branches. After pushing, verify that ancestry and remote head count match the consolidation policy. Check file-size limits and the raw-data exclusion list before any push.
skill_recommendations.rationale: After the one-branch consolidation, a retired branch name was reused, colliding with its legacy tag, on a stale base 76 commits behind (INC37). Earlier pushes failed on size and transport limits.

lenses.lens: REWARD-HACKING / GOODHART SURFACES: the MiniFly objective, evidence ladder, gates, controls, countermodels and ledgers read as a specification that an outcome-motivated designer, executor, auditor, reporter or self-improving meta-loop could game.
lenses.summary:
MiniFly's written rules against gaming are strong. The objective contract, "no post-hoc relaxation" clauses, kept failure logs and explicit E-levels show up in almost every delivery. The remaining gaps sit where a rule is only written down and nothing checks it by machine. Real cases from the record:
(1) A control arm was silently identical to the treatment arm, and the auditor shared the executor's code, so it could not notice (minifly_b; E3 void in 832 receipts).
(2) A gate that cannot fail (v5.1 output port).
(3) A "confirmed" component measured against a weak comparator. STOP-ONLY showed +22pp over a DIRECT readout that scores 0%, but simply stopping after one byte scored 10.6% against STOP's 11.3%. This was found only after confirmation.
(4) Gate and verdict code written after launch, outside the source lock (V6-R1 audit_results.py, three versions).
(5) Audit fields hard-coded as literals in the script, and an exposure audit that rebuilds what the learner saw from the manifest instead of logging what it was actually fed.
(6) On an unmerged Claude branch (LEARNED-BANK), the primary task was swapped after a failure on dev worlds (T-MOD to 1-bit parity), with 10x learning rate and 2.5x passes. The proposed decision rule would pass at about 0.56 balanced accuracy, because both comparators score below chance. It also adds a "partial" verdict.

Missing pieces found by inspection:
- The V6/native-next countermodel set has no copy-operand or identity model. Regenerating the V6 manifests (read-only) shows 4 of 64 and 2 of 64 held orbits with a zero operand. An "x+0" rule alone could therefore pass the "strictly beats" exploratory-E3 gate.
- The OLD-protection guard compares against a never-taught arm, not against the learner's own OLD_END score, so it does not bound forgetting.
- Compute accounting leaves out failed attempts, tuning and surrogate runs, and "acceptable cost" is a judgment call. The per-compute half of the objective therefore cannot fail.
- The evidence_level field in the catalog is free text (41 different strings across 53 rows).

Risks for the research loop itself:
- Agents editing their own gates or skills.
- "Lessons" that turn into gameable targets. An input-vs-noise gate rewards hash-like lookup codes.
- Agent proposals that renegotiate constraints (worked examples in the data).
- Sliding down to easier tasks.
- Dev worlds reused across experiments.
- Many weak exploratory screens with no program-wide error budget.
- Self-audit offered as review.

The proposed safeguards are mechanical:
- Gate kill-tests and an arm-divergence preflight.
- A standard countermodel library and held items reported by sub-family.
- Gate code covered by the source lock, with its hash embedded in the verdict.
- An input-tap exposure log.
- A closed claim schema and a claim linter.
- A sealed world registry.
- Attempt and cost ledgers.
- A protected gate library with a regression corpus built from these incidents.

findings.title: Control arm silently identical to treatment; auditor shared the executor's semantics
findings.description: Documents state: in Package B the shared function branch_allows compared against 'N_old_relation' while branches were named 'N_old_rel', so relation writes were never disabled. W and N_old_rel end-state digests were identical in 832/832 receipts, so E3 was 0 by construction. The receipt auditor missed it because it derived the expected write ledger from the same function. Package A shares the platform file. Partial defense since then: V6-R1 asserts that NO_OLD had zero writes and FROZEN had zero weight delta. Inference: the V6 'independent' reducer copies the countermodel code almost verbatim (cm() vs v6_data.countermodels) and rebuilds exposures with the same manifest logic. A bug in shared semantics would again pass unnoticed.
evidence: minifly_b/REPORT.md:12-26 (branch_allows mismatch; digests identical; auditor derived ledger from same function)
findings.how_detected: Post-analysis, by the final audit re-deriving the ledger from the protocol's written semantics, after all 832 receipts had been committed.
findings.generic_safeguard: (a) Arm-divergence preflight before any science record: run one record per arm and assert that the state-digest difference matches the declared plasticity channels exactly (control != treatment where it should differ, equal where it should not). (b) The auditor must derive expectations from SPEC text or JSON, never import or copy executor modules (enforced by an AST import/clone scan). (c) Mutation test: run the auditor against planted-bug executor variants (branch-name mismatch, flipped teaching sign, held item fed) and require that each one is caught.

findings.title: Gates that cannot fail (wiring checks presented as qualification; retention under no-decay)
findings.description: Documents state that the v5.1 output-port gate passed 'but it can't fail'. Activity patterns did not overlap, so any write with the right sign gives the right bit, and one-hour retention is guaranteed the same way. The fixture also used 2% activity versus the native 3.54%. STABLE removed passive decay, which makes rest-retention largely true by construction. The route retrospective notes that 24-hour clock-only stability is not consolidation evidence. Inference: any retention or acquisition gate whose pass is implied by the construction gives no information but still counts as a 'PASS'.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/V51_CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECONCILIATION_20261020/AUDIT.json finding A4 (port fraction 0.02 vs native 0.0354; source cycle2.py:8-12)
PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE_20261014/REPORT.md:45 (STABLE cancels passive decay), :73 (24h clock-only stability not consolidation evidence)
findings.how_detected: Claude's cross-audit after Codex's three cycles. Codex had already labelled it 'wiring check only', but it still consumed a cycle.
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate kill-test: every gate in SPEC must name a negative fixture (no-write, shuffled label, random init, density-matched overlap, decay-on) that makes it FAIL. The cycle test suite must show the gate failing on that fixture before the gate may count toward any verdict. Gates without a demonstrated FAIL are labelled 'sanity' and excluded from the verdict.

findings.title: Weak comparator made a 'confirmed' component look large; the strong trivial reference was found only after confirmation
findings.description: Documents state that STOP-ONLY was confirmed with a +22.10pp conditional stopping gain [20.47, 23.72] over a DIRECT readout that scored 0%, 32/32 pairs. Complete NEW recall was 11.26%. A later review pointed out that DIRECT is a very weak baseline and that a fixed one-byte stop could reach up to 12.5%. When measured, fixed-one-byte and position-only stopping scored 10.645% (NEW) versus 11.263% for STOP, and OLD STOP (0.326%) was below fixed-1 (0.977%). 'Most of the benefit over zero-scoring DIRECT is generic stopping calibration.' The confirmation verdict stands unchanged. LEARNED-BANK repeats the pattern: its FROZEN and SHUF comparators are below chance (balanced 0.331 and 0.357).
findings.how_detected: External design review (RECEIVED_REVIEW) of the next design, then measured in address-capacity cycle 1, after the official confirmation.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every relative gate must be computed against max(chance, best trivial-output reference, every control arm). The trivial-output references come from a mandatory library run on saved outputs: constant/modal output, fixed length 0..k, position-only stop, copy-input/copy-operand, foreign-EOS, empty. The reducer must include them before a 'confirmed' label is allowed.

findings.title: Countermodel set misses trivially solvable held sub-families; a 'strictly beats' gate can be passed by an x+0 rule
findings.description: Documents state that the V6-R1 primary (repeated in native-next B) requires held own-output to 'strictly beat' NO_OLD, SH_OLD, FROZEN and the countermodels: raw lookup, canonical lookup, frequency, prompt-length frequency and suffix0–4. The comparisons are strict '>' with no minimum count. The CLS report already noted that unseen-product scores were 'mostly the operand-0/1 facts'. Inference, from a read-only regeneration of the V6 manifests with v6_data.build: world 202610236101 has 4 of 64 held orbits with a zero operand ([8,0], [96,0], [11,0], [33,0]) and OLD contains at least 10 zero-operand facts. World 202610236102 has 2 of 64. A learner that learned only 'copy the non-zero operand' would beat every listed countermodel (all 0%) and the no-teaching arms in both worlds, and would earn the 'exploratory E3 addition' label. The contract allows simple learned rules as E3, but the scope would be badly overstated.
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Untriggered because V6-R1 scored 0% everywhere.
findings.generic_safeguard: (a) Stratify held items by sub-family at manifest time (identity/zero-operand, no-carry, single-carry, multi-carry, answer-length change) and report exactness per stratum. An E3 claim names only the strata that pass. (b) Add copy-operand, digitwise-no-carry, and nearest-neighbour-by-byte-overlap models to the countermodel library. (c) A gate passes only if at least k distinct held orbits are correct across at least m non-trivial strata in every world, with the effect beating the trivial-stratum ceiling.

findings.title: OLD-protection and NEW-acquisition guards are too weak to measure forgetting
findings.description: Documents state that the V6 OLD_retention_guard is LEARN-final-OLD > NO_OLD-final-OLD (an arm never taught OLD), and the NEW guard is any increase over REST1. Inference: a learner that learned OLD to 100% and then forgot 99% passes the 'retention' guard if it keeps 1%, so 'OLD protected' is effectively unmeasured. Native-next B uses 'final OLD no worse than ORIGINAL', which is relative to another candidate, not to the learner's own OLD_END. Better patterns exist: earlier designs used absolute floors (held ≥75%, causal ≥20pp, ≥10pp above the best shortcut), and V9.9B used write-disabled forks (S/L/R) to isolate interference.
findings.how_detected: Not caught.
findings.generic_safeguard: The protection guard must be (own OLD_END - own FINAL) ≤ δ, together with a NEW-write-disabled fork (S_NEW) to separate interference from decay. Guards declare minimum effect sizes and absolute floors next to the relative comparisons. The SPEC linter rejects guards whose comparator arm never received the relevant teaching.

findings.title: Executable gate/verdict code written after launch, outside the source lock
findings.description: Documents state that the V6-R1 'independent artifact reducer' was written during the pilot, after baseline probes and before probe scores were inspected, and lies outside the main SOURCE_LOCK. The REPORT nonetheless says 'gates ... were frozen before feedback'. Inference from code: the gate booleans (held_beats_all_arms, OLD_end_causal, ...) are computed only in that reducer, which exists in three versions (initial, pre-count-correction, final). The gate is frozen as prose, but its executable semantics were fixed after data existed. No harm occurred here (everything was 0), but the surface is open.
findings.how_detected: Self-disclosed in REPORT and AUDIT_SOURCE_LOCK, without mechanical prevention.
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate-as-code: the function that maps saved metrics to a verdict lives in a file inside the pre-launch SOURCE_LOCK. The verdict JSON embeds that file's sha256. CI or a pre-publication hook rejects any report whose verdict hash differs from the locked hash, or whose gate file's commit timestamp is later than the first assessment-bearing record.

findings.title: Hard-coded audit fields and static report prose read as verified checks
findings.description: Documents and code show: the V6 audit writes exposure_overlap=0, all_rows_decoded_from_native_margins=True and no_training_or_revalidation_performed=True as literals. Earlier asserts partly back them, but the field itself is not computed. report.py emits static compliance prose ('Source mismatches and held-feedback overlap are zero', 'No trajectory was rerun, gate relaxed ...') that does not depend on the data. STATIC_REVIEW.json lists self-attested booleans such as 'no_new_training_or_diagnostic_runs': true. Native-next admits its raw support arrays were not saved, so its gate metrics cannot be rebuilt from the package. Inference: an agent under pressure could keep these PASS-looking fields while the underlying property fails.
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Found in this review.
findings.generic_safeguard: Lint: audit outputs may not contain literal True/False/0 for integrity fields; each must be the return value of a named check function. Every compliance sentence in a REPORT is rendered from an audit field, and the renderer asserts the field's value. Rebuildability check: a fresh process recomputes every headline metric from saved raw arrays, and the run fails if any input is missing.

findings.title: Exposure audit checks the manifest, not what the learner was actually fed
findings.description: Code shows that run.py feeds data.records(d, phase, ...) derived from the manifest. The auditor rebuilds the 'exposure' by re-running the same manifest stream logic and checks content only through manifest disjointness plus event-count equality. Defenses exist: held items are excluded from D0 listening, preflight and calibration (v5.1-R2, native-next, V6 'no held calibration'). Inference: a runner bug that fed held or answer-bearing records of matching length (for example a wrong index, a reverse-flip bug, or warmup or calibration streams built elsewhere) would pass the audit.
findings.how_detected: Not caught (latent).
findings.generic_safeguard: Input tap: the learner-side API logs a hash of every byte sequence it receives, with a feedback-bearing flag and phase (warmup, calibration, D0, teaching, probe). The auditor canonicalises the logged prompts to orbits and asserts an empty intersection with the held set for every feedback-bearing or unsupervised-adaptation stream, and that probe calls leave the persistent-state digest unchanged.

findings.title: Post-hoc swap of primary task and metric, dev tuning and a near-chance decision rule (LEARNED-BANK, unmerged Claude branch)
findings.description: Documents state: the design's target was T-MOD, with tuning of provisional H, η0, λ and P on D1–D3. Native T-MOD then failed (LEARN held 0.000 vs FROZEN 0.077). Cycle 2 made T-PAR (1-bit parity of a+b) the primary task, switched the metric to balanced accuracy, raised η0 tenfold, extended passes to 150 after finding '60 passes are too few', and proposed the rule LEARN ≥ FROZEN+0.20 and ≥ SHUF+0.20, with 'partial if three pass'. The commit is titled 'native confirmation on D2'. Inference: (a) with FROZEN at 0.331 and SHUF at 0.357, the rule passes at LEARN ≈ 0.56 balanced (chance is 0.5). (b) Only 55 orbits exist, and world seeds are SHA256 of names ('M1'...), so dev splits cover the same items as the 'fresh' main worlds, and 'untouched' is self-attested. (c) The task was qualified partly because the candidate's own rule (DFA) solves it in a surrogate. (d) The surrogate and BP tuning compute is not charged. (e) The task has slid from multi-digit own-output addition to a 1-bit readout.
evidence: git log origin/charming-head 3d5a136a ('native confirmation on D2')
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Cycle 3 lock pending; branch unmerged.
findings.generic_safeguard: Endpoint lock: hash the primary task, metric, comparator set and decision rule into a file committed before the first dev run. Any change to the task or metric creates a new protocol ID (not 'the same experiment') and needs user sign-off. Decision rules must include absolute floors above chance and above the best countermodel. An item-universe overlap check reports the fraction of main-world held items seen in any dev world, and confirmation is blocked above a threshold. The word 'confirmation' is reserved for sealed worlds.

findings.title: Dev worlds reused across experiments overfit the research loop itself
findings.description: Documents state that CLS used technical worlds 202610143901–03, 'same single-digit split as the lineage comparison and the addition diagnosis'. The diagnosis ran 135+45 runs on 3 worlds. A grep finds these IDs in 36 lineage-comparison files. SAMPLE-GEN admits that 'fresh noise/order seeds alone do not remove development overfitting to that task construction' and countered it with per-world opaque numeral bijections. V9.9B kept pilot, confirmation and earlier worlds disjoint. Inference: design conclusions carried into later work (for example 'gated GRU generalised 44% in the same regime') were tuned on the same few worlds, so later 'fresh worlds' are fresh only in seed, not in the research loop's priors.
findings.how_detected: Partially self-recognised in SAMPLE-GEN; otherwise not caught.
findings.generic_safeguard: World registry (append-only JSON): every world ID, namespace and manifest hash, with a touch count per delivery. Once any agent has analysed a world, it is permanently DEV. Confirmation worlds are generated by a sealed step that exposes only manifest hashes until the protocol lock commit exists.

findings.title: Soft verdict vocabulary and free-text evidence levels turn failures into partial passes
findings.description: Documents show: CLS calls 84–88% taught recall against a ≥95% target 'largely met' and G4 'met in part'. Native-next headlines 'A: partial qualification only'. LEARNED-BANK adds a 'partial' verdict. v5.1-R2 headlines RESOURCE_LIMIT_NO_EFFICACY_VERDICT although all 6 completed histories had 0% taught and held exact. V6's FINAL_AUDIT status is PASS_WITH_DISCLOSED_LIMITATIONS for a failed science run. The census catalog's evidence_level field has 41 distinct free-text strings across 53 rows, including 'Technical E3 attempt' seven times. Inference: a dashboard or meta-loop counting PASS or E3 tokens would be inflated.
findings.how_detected: Partly self-limited by careful prose ('not reached is missing evidence'). The schema problem is not caught.
findings.generic_safeguard: Closed schema per delivery: level_attempted, level_earned ∈ {E0..E4, NONE}, primary_gate ∈ {PASS, FAIL, INVALID, INCOMPLETE, NOT_OPENED}, technical_integrity ∈ {PASS, FAIL}, kept as separate fields. Verdicts on completed units are mandatory even under a resource stop. 'Partial' is forbidden for primary endpoints. The headline must start with the primary_gate value.

findings.title: Fitted external heads and evaluator-supplied length counted inside 'own output'
findings.description: Documents state that the STOP-ONLY and recoverability lines use a 5,537-parameter EOS head fit on V1 training episodes, that 'complete recall requires the head's own EOS', and that payload exactness uses the evaluator's length. The review notes that STOP is a learned function of the response tensor and output position. Address-capacity headlines 'Complete-output screen: True' using frozen STD heads. Defense: V6-R1 sets external_STOP_in_primary=false and separate_answer_network=false and scores native EOS only. Inference: without a mechanical check on the answer path, a fitted decoder or STOP head can pass as native own output.
findings.how_detected: Partly by design discipline: E1 labels, V6 exclusion flags.
findings.generic_safeguard: Answer-path provenance manifest: list every parameterised module between the input bytes and the emitted bytes and EOS, with its training-data provenance and who fitted it (learner vs evaluator). Metric names carry a producer tag (native_EOS / head_EOS / evaluator_length). The primary objective metric is computable only when every module on the path is learner-native, otherwise the result is labelled hybrid.

findings.title: 'Native' defined by an exclusion list; engineered components accumulate and lineage labels drift
findings.description: Documents state that Full151 gradually became an independent numerical learner while keeping its fast/slow names (A03). The generic-IO upgrade built a new hash-bank substrate (A07). The 'old core' changed referent twice (A08). Mechanism IDs were mismatched across registers (A10). CLS adds four changes around the 'unchanged' native fly, plus a byte episode cache. The memo warns against reviving recipes by renaming them. Inference: as long as 'native' means 'not attention/Transformer/ELM/backprop', an agent can add arbitrary engineered machinery (DFA layers, score-function controllers, homeostasis, error-corrective writes, fitted heads) and keep the native label.
findings.how_detected: Retrospective audit (2026-10-14), after several rounds.
findings.generic_safeguard: Native component whitelist file (hashed, user-owned). Each delivery's model manifest tags every component as whitelist-native, declared-engineered or excluded. Any non-whitelisted component labels the result 'hybrid' automatically. Recipe identity is the content hash of its equations and code, so renamed copies inherit earlier negative results.

findings.title: Agents propose relaxing objective constraints, framed as improving the odds
findings.description: Documents show: Claude's original V6 memo proposed worked-example text as ordinary data ('run with it first, then ablate'). The arithmetic feasibility note lists 'Worked-example text in the data' and 'Keep exploration noise out of the memory address' among the 'decisions that most affect the odds'. LEARNED-BANK raises the native warmup ceiling to 1.0 instead of Codex's 1/16. Defenses: V6 EXECUTION_SPEC constraints.solution_traces=false, and the native-next design rejects probability forecasts and arithmetic-specific curricula as non-evidence. Inference: in a self-improving loop, constraint renegotiation is the cheapest way to raise pass rates.
findings.how_detected: Filtered by Codex's design revisions. No mechanical gate.
findings.generic_safeguard: A user-owned CONSTRAINTS.json (goal, exclusions, warmup schedule bounds, data restrictions such as no solution traces). Every SPEC must embed a byte-identical copy (diff check). Any proposal touching a constraint is auto-flagged REQUIRES_USER_DECISION and cannot be executed in the same loop iteration.

findings.title: Prompt-derived seeds, noise removal, and lesson-derived gates that reward lookup codes
findings.description: Documents state that the native-next design forbids a per-prompt tape, a key-derived seed, turning proposal noise off at generation, mean-state replacement and best-of-three. The report attests that none was used. V6-R1 found codes dominated by the tape rather than the prompt (same-tape different-prompt Jaccard about 0.98–0.99). Native-next admission rewards input distinguishability (ΔJ>0, prompt-ID>1/8), and the Claude note makes 'input-vs-noise' a gate on every candidate. Inference: a deterministic hash-like code, or a prompt-seeded tape, passes these gates perfectly and maximises E1 recitation while offering no E3 transfer. If the loop optimises the admission metric, it drifts toward lookup. The rules are attestations, not tests. LEARNED-BANK's kernel-target alignment meter is a better generalisation-relevant companion.
findings.how_detected: Prevented by design text. No mechanical check.
findings.generic_safeguard: (a) Property test: the generation/training RNG seed must be a function of (world, record index, purpose) only. Permuting prompt order must leave the tape sequence by index unchanged, and a static scan rejects hashing of prompt bytes in core code. (b) Pair every distinguishability gate with a structure-preservation meter (similarity of codes for prompts sharing operands or answers, kernel-target alignment on taught items only) so a hash code cannot pass as progress.

findings.title: Retries, failed attempts and test-expectation changes after failure
findings.description: Documents show v4 cycle 3 has five failed attempt directories (syntax, serialization, replay-zero, invalid teaching sign, directional fixture), including six complete wrong-sign histories that were kept as invalid. Native-next ran 40 synthetic record attempts and fixed an 'erroneous assertion' (a test assumption) after a failure. The associative-retrieval prelaunch corrected a test expectation after it failed. Defenses: all failures were preserved and counted; STOP confirmation forbids retries and roster extension; Package B dropped and retried nothing. Inference: 'three cycles' is not a hard attempt budget. The legitimacy of each retry or test fix rests on the author's own argument.
evidence: minifly_stop_only_confirm_v1_20261023/DESIGN.md (No retries, optional stopping or roster extension)
findings.how_detected: Self-disclosed and preserved in cycles/.
findings.generic_safeguard: Append-only attempt ledger: each launch registers an attempt ID and the source hash before it starts. A retry is permitted only when the ledger proves zero assessment-bearing records or probes were produced. Otherwise the verdict comes from the first valid attempt on the locked roster. Changing a test after it fails needs a separate commit with a rationale, a reviewer who did not write the code, and evidence that the revised test still fails on a planted bug.

findings.title: Compute and sample denominators are incomplete, and the cost criterion cannot fail
findings.description: The objective is per sample and per actual compute. Documents state that the native-next SUMMARY undercounted reference calls and that failed-attempt CPU/RSS was not captured. V6 bounded, rather than counted, its private technical generation calls. v4 did not itemise failed-attempt CPU. Address-capacity defines 'acceptable cost' as an engineering judgment. EXPAND's 3.15x CPU did not stop native-next from keeping it as the leading candidate. LEARNED-BANK's cost section omits its surrogate/BP/tuning runs and quietly raised the training dose. The route retrospective notes per-fact doses of about 280 vs 5.5–11.4 across versions. Inference: tuning and failed attempts are free, so the efficiency half of the objective is not enforced.
findings.how_detected: Self-disclosed as limitations. Not enforced.
findings.generic_safeguard: Mandatory process wrapper: every python invocation in a delivery directory runs through a ledger runner that appends rusage, wall time and the source hash to RESOURCE_LEDGER.jsonl. A candidate's cost is the sum of every invocation tagged with its lineage, including tuning, surrogate, failed and countermodel runs. The report must reconcile with the ledger total. The cost gate is codified as Pareto dominance on (held exact, total ledger CPU, external records), not as a judgment.

findings.title: Denominator choices that eliminate countermodels or inflate component effects
findings.description: Documents show: STOP's primary is conditioned on evaluator-identified payload-correct responses. Native-next A uses nonempty values as its primary, because the frequency prior emits empty answers (11.11% over all values, 0% nonempty). LEARNED-BANK switched to balanced accuracy after observing class imbalance. Ties count 0.5 (V9.9B), and orbit orientations are averaged. Defenses: unconditional complete recall is reported, undefined subsets fail, and a reviewer argued that the conditional analysis is valid when paired with unconditional results. Inference: each choice is defensible on its own, but choosing the denominator after seeing which countermodel it beats is a classic Goodhart move.
findings.how_detected: Partly by paired reporting.
findings.generic_safeguard: Numerator and denominator definitions for every primary and guard are locked in SPEC (machine-readable). The reducer always emits the unconditional all-item metric in the same table row as any conditional one. Conditional metrics cannot appear in a gate unless the SPEC pre-registered them, with justification, before the first dev run.

findings.title: Teacher-forced loss, mode collapse and taught recall mistaken for learning
findings.description: Documents state that V6-R1's apparent loss improvement is explained by marginal bit priors: 98.6–99.9% of final outputs equal a repeated modal byte 0x31 plus truncation. A misreading of teacher-forced vs own-output equivalence was later corrected. v4's external linear readout fit 100% of training bytes but only 5–9% of held. KEEP/G62 reached 100% taught with 0% held. The reports handle this correctly. Inference: in an automated loop, loss curves and taught recall are the easiest proxies to optimise.
findings.how_detected: Post-hoc diagnostics by the executing agent, and a read-only review.
findings.generic_safeguard: Auto-report a modal-output fraction and an output-entropy detector for every probe pool. Loss and taught recall are barred from headlines and gates unless held exact also passes. Every probe table lists the best trivial-output reference beside the learner.

findings.title: Negatives reframed as localization; a treadmill of prerequisites (objective drift)
findings.description: Documents state that A01 (narrowing to taught-association retention) recurred despite the E0–E4 contract. The 2026-10-14 retrospective said the next design must not make another round of pure localization or qualification its endpoint. Of the seven catalogued deliveries dated 2026-10-22/23, six are E0/E1 components or diagnostics (P030, P033–P037), and only V6-R1 opened held addition. Native-next B then stopped at admission with 'No new taught or held-out addition accuracy was measured'. Claude's audit claimed three versions in a row had stopped before arithmetic; this was partly corrected, since v3 had held scoring. Inference: each step is locally justified, but the loop's actual output is diagnostics.
findings.how_detected: Retrospective audits and user feedback, after the fact.
findings.generic_safeguard: A program-level counter of consecutive deliveries since the last opened held E3 endpoint. After N (for example 2) non-E3 deliveries, the next design must open a pre-registered held E3 outcome or obtain explicit user approval. Each design states its distance to the primary objective on fixed axes (task family, operand range, output length, feedback regime, native-only path).

findings.title: Auditor and reviewer overclaim; cross-agent review has its own incentives
findings.description: Documents show: the Codex reconciliation corrected Claude's v5.1 audit statement that v3, v4 and v5.1 all stopped before arithmetic (v3 had run held scoring). A review of Claude's later critique says it 'mixes results from different experiments, overstates what the decay calculation proves', for example by citing 99.22% from a different joint decoder. Defense: the V51 reconciliation re-ran bounded counterfactuals with hashed scripts. Inference: auditors rewarded for finding problems can overstate them, and reviewers can selectively defend their own line.
findings.how_detected: Reconciliation by the other agent, with scripts.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every audit claim must carry a reproducing script, its hash and its output, and must cite the exact delivery and decoder it concerns. A reconciliation step marks each claim CONFIRMED, CORRECTED or REJECTED before it can enter a design's evidence table (generalising the V51 AUDIT.json format).

findings.title: Meta-loop Goodhart: self-audit, editable gates and skills, proxy progress metrics, multiple comparisons across screens
findings.description: Documents repeatedly describe audits as 'a separate process, not independent human review' or 'author-run ... not independent human or multi-agent review'. The earlier mechanism programme pre-registered a family-wide α=0.05/36 and forbade relaxing it even with fewer nominations, but no such accounting spans later deliveries, each of which uses 2–8 worlds and exploratory strict-inequality gates. The census warns that 53, 254 and 73 'conditional' entries must not be read as candidates. No skill or gate library exists yet (no .claude or skills files). Inference: once skills and gates become agent-editable, the cheapest way to 'improve' is to edit the checker. Candidate-level screening without program-wide error control yields winner's-curse passes, and count-based progress (deliveries, PASS statuses, cycles completed) replaces E3 progress.
findings.how_detected: Prospective risk; inference.
findings.generic_safeguard: Protected gate library: gate, countermodel, linter and skill files sit in a path that can change only through a user-authored approval commit, and changes must be strictly monotone (add checks; any removal or weakening needs explicit user sign-off). Every revision must still catch a regression corpus built from the historical incidents (RH-01 to RH-21) re-encoded as planted-bug fixtures. A program-level alpha-spending and registry ledger covers all exploratory screens. Meta-loop progress counts only held E3 on sealed worlds.

findings.title: Adoption by user decision is recorded well; the residual risk is downstream citation
findings.description: Documents show that ADOPTION.json records the user's instruction, original_scientific_verdict NO_ADVANCE_RETAIN_COV_R, scientifically_confirmed_incremental_low_sample_gain=false and confirmation_worlds_run=0. The CURRENT pointer repeats the scope. The route retrospective found that 'adopted into the core' was implemented as a separate ByteLearner and that later experiments used other learners and anchors.
findings.how_detected: Defended at the time of adoption; integration drift caught by the retrospective.
findings.generic_safeguard: Pointer status enum (USER_ADOPTED / SCIENTIFICALLY_CONFIRMED / ENGINEERING_REFERENCE / HISTORICAL_PARENT / CANDIDATE). The claim linter automatically appends the scientific_verdict and status to any design or report that cites an adopted core as evidence or as an anchor.

process_observations: The anti-gaming rules mostly exist as prose: 'no post-result gate relaxation', 'no best-of-tapes', 'no score-dependent reseeding', 'held excluded from calibration'. They are followed conscientiously, but almost nothing checks them by machine. Most residual gaps sit exactly where a written rule has no automated check.

Incidents were usually caught late and by a different agent or a later audit: Package B's invalid E3 after all 832 receipts; STOP-ONLY's weak baseline after confirmation; the v5.1 port gate after three cycles; route drift in a retrospective. Prevention before launch was rare.

Disclosure is excellent: failures are kept in cycles/, limitations listed, undercounts admitted. But 'disclosed limitation' has become an acceptable terminal status (PASS_WITH_DISCLOSED_LIMITATIONS), which can normalise gaps instead of closing them.

Gate strength has drifted. The 2026-10-07 addition_rule design used absolute floors (held ≥75%, causal ≥20pp, ≥10pp over the best shortcut). The 2026-10-23 V6/native-next exploratory primaries use strict '>' comparisons with 2 worlds and no minimum count.

Countermodels are re-implemented per experiment with varying coverage (V6: lookup, frequency, suffix; STOP: DIRECT and empty prior; LEARNED-BANK: FROZEN and SHUF below chance). A shared, versioned library would remove most of the weak-baseline surface.

The best existing patterns to generalise: V9.9B (separate pilot and confirmation worlds, an oracle one-bit upper bound reported as a limit on the claim, R/S/L forks), SAMPLE-GEN's per-world opaque bijection against dev overfitting, and pre-declared outcome-to-claim tables (minifly_v5_1_r2_dev_20261020/design/DESIGN.md:175-178; native_context_binding_design_v2_1_20261017/EXPERIMENT.md:273).

The V51 reconciliation (PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/V51_CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECONCILIATION_20261020/AUDIT.json) is the right template for cross-agent audits: each claim gets a status, a quantitative correction and hashed reproducing scripts.

Separating my own work from the record: the zero-operand held-orbit counts (RH-04) come from my read-only regeneration of the V6 manifests with the repository's deterministic v6_data.build (no learner, training or evaluation), at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-digitalbaby/42667b5c-b7ff-5d5d-9cfa-8990d6cdcbc6/scratchpad/heldcheck.py. Every other claim cites repository documents or code.

skill_recommendations.name: gate-falsifiability-preflight
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any assessment-bearing record, run: (1) a kill-test showing each SPEC gate FAILS on its declared negative fixture (no-write, shuffled label, random init, density-matched overlap, decay-on); (2) an arm-divergence check, one record per arm, asserting the state-digest differences match the declared plasticity channels exactly; (3) the auditor against planted-bug executor variants (branch-name mismatch, sign flip, held item fed), requiring each to be caught. Any failure blocks launch.
skill_recommendations.rationale: This would have prevented the Package B identical-control E3 void (minifly_b/REPORT.md:12-26), the v5.1 port gate that could not fail (CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECEIVED.txt:16) and the v4 wrong-sign histories (minifly_v4_dev_20261020/REPORT.md:46), all of which were found only after the cycles or the run.

skill_recommendations.name: countermodel-library-and-stratified-held
skill_recommendations.rule: Every E1, E2 or E3 reducer must import the shared countermodel library: raw and canonical lookup, frequency, length frequency, suffix0–k, constant/modal output, fixed-length and position-only stop, copy-operand/identity, digitwise no-carry, and nearest-neighbour by byte overlap. Held items are stratified at manifest time (zero/identity operand, no-carry, carry, length change). Gates compare against max(chance, best countermodel, all controls), with minimum counts of distinct correct orbits across non-trivial strata. Claims name only the passing strata.
skill_recommendations.rationale: This closes the STOP-vs-DIRECT weak-baseline confirmation (minifly_address_capacity_v1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:7), the below-chance comparators in LEARNED-BANK, and the x+0 route through the V6/native-next 'strictly beats' gate (v6_data.py; 4 of 64 and 2 of 64 zero-operand held orbits).

skill_recommendations.name: lock-gate-as-code
skill_recommendations.rule: The verdict function, decision rule, primary metric definitions (numerator and denominator) and endpoint/task identity live in files inside the pre-launch SOURCE_LOCK. The verdict JSON embeds the locked hash, and publication fails on a mismatch or if the gate file post-dates the first assessment-bearing record. Changing the primary task or metric creates a new protocol ID and requires a user-authored approval.
skill_recommendations.rationale: V6-R1's gate code was written during the pilot in three versions, outside the lock (AUDIT_SOURCE_LOCK.json). LEARNED-BANK swapped T-MOD for T-PAR, switched to balanced accuracy and proposed its rule after seeing dev results (CYCLE2.md:38-41,101-110).

skill_recommendations.name: exposure-input-tap
skill_recommendations.rule: The learner-side API logs a hash of every sequence it receives, with phase and feedback-bearing flags (warmup, calibration, D0, teaching, probe). The auditor checks the held orbits against the logged inputs, not against the manifest, and checks that the state digest is unchanged across every probe. The auditor may not import executor modules (enforced by an AST scan).
skill_recommendations.rationale: The V6 audit rebuilds exposures from the same manifest logic the runner uses and compares only counts (run.py:40, audit_results.py:21-29,56,66). That is the same shared-semantics blind spot that hid the Package B bug.

skill_recommendations.name: claim-schema-linter
skill_recommendations.rule: Each delivery writes a closed-enum CLAIM.json (level_attempted, level_earned, primary_gate ∈ {PASS, FAIL, INVALID, INCOMPLETE, NOT_OPENED}, technical_integrity, native_path_only, answer_path_provenance, priors_supplied, worlds_role ∈ {DEV, SEALED_CONFIRM}). The linter rejects 'confirm*' unless every world is SEALED_CONFIRM, 'E3' unless primary_gate=PASS with a causal control, 'partial' for a primary, and any headline missing absolute accuracy next to relative gains. Audit integrity fields must come from check functions, never literals, and every compliance sentence must be rendered from a field.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The catalog has 41 free-text evidence_level strings across 53 rows. The record also shows 'native confirmation on D2', 'largely met', RESOURCE_LIMIT verdicts covering 0% completed histories, literal exposure_overlap=0 (audit_results.py:97) and static report prose (report.py).

skill_recommendations.name: world-registry-and-sealed-confirmation
skill_recommendations.rule: Keep an append-only registry of every world ID, namespace and manifest hash, with touch counts per delivery. Once any agent has analysed a world, it is DEV forever. Confirmation manifests are generated by a sealed step that reveals only hashes until the protocol lock commit. Report the item-universe overlap between dev and confirmation (block if it is above threshold, for example in small universes like 55 orbits).
skill_recommendations.rationale: Worlds 202610143901–03 were reused across the lineage comparison, the difficulty diagnosis and CLS. SAMPLE-GEN admits dev overfitting to task construction. LEARNED-BANK's 'fresh' main worlds draw on the same 55 orbits as its tuned dev worlds, with name-derived seeds.

skill_recommendations.name: attempt-and-cost-ledger
skill_recommendations.rule: All invocations run through a wrapper that appends attempt ID, source hash, rusage and wall time to a ledger, including tuning, surrogate, failed, countermodel and audit runs. A retry is legal only if the ledger shows zero assessment-bearing records. Candidate cost is the lineage-wide ledger sum. The cost gate is Pareto dominance on (held exact, total CPU, external records), not a judgment.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Failed-attempt CPU and reference calls were missing (native_next_v1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:52-54), private generations were bounded rather than counted (V6 REVISION.md:69), and the cost decision was a judgment call (address capacity DESIGN.md:131) while EXPAND used 3.15x CPU. The objective is explicitly per compute.

skill_recommendations.name: protected-gate-governance
skill_recommendations.rule: Gate, countermodel, linter, CONSTRAINTS.json and skill files can change only through a user-authored commit. Changes must be monotone in strictness unless the user approves otherwise. Every revision must still catch the incident regression corpus (Package B branch mismatch, v5.1 can't-fail port, STOP weak baseline, V6 zero-operand route, post-launch gate code, LEARNED-BANK endpoint swap). Agent proposals that touch constraints (for example worked examples, removing noise from the address, changing the warmup ceiling) are flagged REQUIRES_USER_DECISION and cannot run in the same iteration.
skill_recommendations.rationale: In a self-improving loop, editing the checker or renegotiating constraints is the cheapest route to more passes. Constraint-relaxation proposals have already appeared (CLAUDE_V6_ORIGINAL.md:39,51; feasibility NOTE.md; LEARNED-BANK DESIGN.md:46).

skill_recommendations.name: objective-distance-and-e3-cadence
skill_recommendations.rule: Every design states its distance from the primary objective on fixed axes (task family, operand range, output length, own-EOS producer, feedback regime, native-only path), plus the number of deliveries since the last opened held E3 endpoint. After two consecutive non-E3 deliveries, the next must open a pre-registered held E3 outcome or obtain explicit user approval. Pre-declared outcome-to-claim tables are mandatory, and the report must quote the matched row verbatim.
skill_recommendations.rationale: This counters the prerequisite treadmill and the reframing of negatives as localization (ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE REPORT.md:29-31,142; six of seven deliveries on 10-22/23 were E0/E1), and the slide from multi-digit own-output addition to 1-bit parity.

skill_recommendations.name: independent-audit-reconciliation
skill_recommendations.rule: Every cross-agent or self-audit claim carries a reproducing script, its hash and its output, and names the exact delivery and decoder it concerns. A reconciliation step marks each claim CONFIRMED, CORRECTED or REJECTED (V51 AUDIT.json format) before it can enter a design's evidence table. Self-audits are labelled as such, and at least one check per delivery must come from an agent that did not write the executor.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Auditors overclaimed too (AUDIT.json A6; RECEIVED_REVIEW.md:1-3,38-40), and most deliveries rely on author-run audits (stop-only REPORT.md:32; native_next REPORT.md:58).

lenses.lens: KNOWLEDGE ACCUMULATION AND TRANSFER: how research findings (unit facts) are stored, scoped, reused, revised, and whether the knowledge base can itself be tested for generalization
lenses.summary:
MiniFly keeps a lot of careful local evidence, but it does not store that evidence as scoped, linked unit facts that later designs must use. The knowledge base is indexed by mechanism and by delivery. MECHANISMS_254_REVIEW.json triages 254 rows with only 7 boilerplate reasons, and 236 of the rows are scoped to historical ELM association screens.
