EXPERIMENT_CATALOG.json uses a free-text result and 40 distinct evidence-level strings across 53 rows. It has no fields for substrate, priors, dose, comparator strength, or superseded_by. In practice, designs check the register defensively: they tick through 254 rows, mark them "not excluded", and stop there. The register does not feed predictions. As a result:
(1) The same class of input-conditioning/address failure came back at least 5 times. It shows up in the contract (2026-09-26, line 39), the order probe (10-17), the suffix conflict (10-15), v4 G0 (10-20), v5.1 aliasing (10-20), V6-R1 cue/noise (10-23) and native_next B (10-23). The v4 coverage gate and the contract's KC-code check were not carried into V6, so the gate had to be worked out again after V6 failed.
(2) When a fact is narrowed, the summaries do not pick it up. STOP's +22.10pp was measured against DIRECT, which scores 0. A fixed one-byte stop rule gets 10.645% vs STOP's 11.263%. CATALOG P036 and the MEMO still quote only +22pp.
(3) No mechanism scores predictions. learning_spectrum (10-01) had a fail-closed launch gate that required a quantitative forecast, and nothing reused it. Claude designs include "Predictions (to be locked)". Codex revisions delete them as "ungrounded" (V6 revised DESIGN l.21, REVIEW l.11, native_next DESIGN l.16). No report anywhere scores a prediction.
(4) Agents misremember prior facts: v3 history, the register's coverage of gating, STOP magnitude, tally caveats. These errors are caught only by manual cross-agent review.
(5) The Claude branch has no PROJECT_DOCUMENTS. 93 files point to /Users/pencilbard paths. The only native E3 positives (V9.9A/B) exist only locally.
There are real strengths to build on: Evidence→Consequence tables in designs; cheap saved-data reanalyses; and several correct prunings (joint decoder→STOP-ONLY, native_next birth gate, common-mode auditor lesson, learning_spectrum analytic preflight).
Recommended structure: a UNIT_FACTS register with scope fields and narrowed_by links; a mandatory design block listing the fact IDs relied on, the failure classes addressed, and hashed numeric or probabilistic predictions; post-run scoring that updates fact status; and a periodic blinded retrodiction test of the knowledge base.

findings.title: Input-conditioning / answer-time address failure recurred at least 5 times; the gates that would have caught it existed and were dropped
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE a chain. The contract (09-26) told designers to first measure whether label-preserving byte variants change the KC code before learning. 10-15: native suffix-conflict continuation 2/4. 10-17: native FE barely encodes order. 10-20: v4 G0 coverage readout failed (held 5-9%); the v4 revision ordered future gates as port -> representation -> coverage on frozen learned codes -> consolidation. 10-20: v5.1 identity aliasing fixed at birth, and Claude noted 'the failure was visible from the random starting values in about a second'. The V6 revised design's qualification list (DESIGN.md:129-135) checks interfaces, the estimator, no-write behavior and birth hashes, but has no prompt-vs-noise or coverage check. V6-R1 then failed with cue effects 70-90x weaker than noise, measured already at BIRTH. Only afterwards did NEXT_DESIGN add birth sensitivity, at first 'not a tuned efficacy threshold'. native_next turned it into a stop gate that closed the rescaled candidate for about 2 CPU-s. The Claude LEARNED-BANK design then cites it as a 'V6 lesson'. INFERENCE: the knowledge existed in at least four documents, but nothing turns a recognised failure class into a standing preflight for every new front end, so it was re-derived through a full 34,816-record run.

findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a failure-class library (FC-ADDR etc.), each class with a seconds-scale check. Any design that changes the encoder/front end must run all applicable checks at birth before teaching: same-input/different-noise vs different-input/same-noise; leave-one-tape-out prompt ID > chance; frozen-code coverage readout on held items. The design document must cite the failure-class IDs.

findings.title: No mechanism requires a design to state predictions from prior facts and score them later; a working precedent was abandoned and forecasts are actively deleted
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE the following. The required design block in the objective contract has 5 items (claim/level, exposure audit, recitation countermodel, causal controls, promotion rule/cost). None of them is 'prior facts relied upon' or 'predicted outcome'. learning_spectrum (10-01) implemented a fail-closed launch gate: launch_gate.py raises 'no quantitative total forecast' when the prediction field is absent, and that blocked a run. No later delivery reuses it; a grep finds it only in learning_spectrum. Claude designs carry 'Predictions (to be locked before running)' (v4 original l.174; v5 l.151; V6 memo l.45-47; LEARNED-BANK sec.7). The Codex-frozen versions drop them: v4 DESIGN.md has none; V6 revised l.21 'Remove V6's numerical forecasts'; REVIEW.md l.11 'Delete ungrounded ... forecasts'; native_next l.16 'probability forecasts ... are not evidence'. No report contains post-run prediction scoring. Several implicit predictions could have been scored and were not: NEXT_DESIGN called the rescale 'a falsifiable first correction', and native_next falsified it, but it was recorded only as 'candidate closed'. The RECEIVED_REVIEW 12.5% ceiling for FIXED_1 was later measured at 10.645%. Claude's v5.1 audit said 'fixing only the byte stage guarantees another NO_ADVANCE'; R2 birth 2 then had one occupied class and no verdict. INFERENCE: removing forecasts protects against overclaiming but removes any calibration signal, so the program cannot tell whether its knowledge generalises to new designs.

findings.title: Fact narrowings do not propagate to the summary layer (STOP +22pp, CREDIT null)

findings.title: Weak comparators, unfalsifiable gates and inert manipulations recur and are found only after the run
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE several cases. v5.1 port gate 'passes, but it can't fail' (disjoint activity patterns; fixture at 2% vs native 3.54% activity). STOP compared with DIRECT, which scores 0, before FIXED_1 was tried. CREDIT changed updates by about 0.3-1.3%. Package B's N_old_rel was bit-identical to W, so E3 was 0 by construction. The converse also occurs: LEARNED-BANK's primary T-MOD gate could not be passed even by exact BP. The contract item 4 asks for 'a positive control known to solve the task', but no standing rule asks for evidence that each gate can fail, that the treatment actually differs from the control, or that the comparator includes the cheapest trivial policy. INFERENCE: this is one failure class (a gate that is not sensitive) that re-appears in new forms, because each lesson is stored only in the delivery where it occurred.

(d) The trivial-policy panel (constant, mode, FIXED_k, position-only, frequency) is always among the comparators. (e) The auditor must not import the code under test.

findings.title: E3-targeted native runs repeatedly fail at E0/E1 prerequisites; the prerequisite ladder is written down but not enforced
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE the following. Native taught acquisition was near zero in N151/C151/RC151 (10-15) and NATIVE-BIND V1 (10-16). v5.1 stopped at identity, R2 hit its resource limit with a one-class collapse, and V6-R1 had OLD/NEW/held all 0. The contract (l.39-41) and the v4 revision (l.58) both give a gate order. Claude's feasibility note says 'every full run failed an earlier prerequisite'. Over this period the base rate of native E3 attempts that passed acquisition is 0/6+. INFERENCE: a register-based base-rate forecast would have rated V6-R1's full roster very unlikely to clear acquisition, which would have justified a cheap acquisition or birth gate first. native_next is the first design to fail closed at that step.

findings.title: Transferable generalisation levers from reference learners are neither adopted nor explicitly rejected in native designs
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE that Claude's GRU diagnosis found the following. Data suffice: an additive fit predicts all held answers. Generalisation peaks early and is then overwritten. A generic simplicity pressure (weight decay) gave +38pp, and counting-as-data +11 to +21pp; the diagnosis calls it 'an inductive-bias problem, not a data problem'. The V6 learning rule states 'There is no weight decay ... in this initial candidate' without referencing this fact. No native design records held-out peak timing as a planned diagnostic tied to it. INFERENCE (not proof that it would transfer to local native rules): there is no step where a design must list the known generalisation levers and justify including or excluding each, so research-level transfer from reference learners to the native line happens only by chance (LEARNED-BANK does include weight decay).

findings.title: Engineering-error lessons are stored per delivery; the class 'fixture/lock differs from the production path' recurs
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE the following. The v5.1 port fixture used activity 0.02 vs native 0.0354, and calibration omitted the REPLY transition. v4 had a replay [-0:] bug and a reversed teaching sign that a parity check had not covered. The V6-R1 source lock covered vendor copies, not actual asset locations, and had an evaluator import collision. native_next's EOS fixture used BASE's residual for all arms, omitted boundaries, and contained a false slow-zero assertion. NATIVE-BIND v2.1 checkpoints were not bound to cursor/resource. Some lessons were carried into the next design (V6 NEXT_DESIGN l.43 'Resolve actual imported asset paths'; native_next design l.76 'Do not accept only agreement between two reducers importing the same decoder'). There is no cross-delivery checklist; each lesson lives in that delivery's cycles/ REVIEW files (39 cycles dirs).

findings.title: Strength: several correct knowledge-driven prunings, plus local Evidence->Consequence tables that a fact register could attach to
findings.description: DOCUMENTS STATE these cases. RECOVERABILITY V1's 'joint head damages payload' led directly to a STOP-ONLY arm that preserves native payload signs, which was then confirmed, and to repeated 'do not enlarge the decoder' rules. V6-R1's cue/noise diagnosis led to native_next's fail-closed birth gate, which saved the 43,520-record roster. Package B's common-mode auditor led to later rules requiring independent reconstruction that does not import the learner or decoder. learning_spectrum's analytic formation prediction rejected a candidate before any fresh world. v4 G0 stopped the large P3/G2 run. U034 was removed from scheduling ('do not rerun under a new name'). The register corrected Claude's false 'no gating' claim. Designs carry Evidence->Consequence tables (v6 revised l.11-17; R2 design l.11-13; native_next l.11-16). The census memo's priority table conditions each mechanism family's re-entry on the current failure locus. Cheap saved-data reanalyses settled interpretations without retraining (V51 reconciliation about 27 CPU-s; ADDRESS-CAPACITY cycle 1).

findings.generic_safeguard: Keep these patterns and formalise them: each Evidence->Consequence row cites a fact ID; each pruning is recorded as a fact-derived prediction ('fact F implies candidate C fails gate G') and scored when the gate is run.

process_observations: Workflow asymmetry: Claude (claude/* branches) writes conceptual designs that include forecasts and 'Predictions (to be locked)'. Codex (committing as Pencilbard) revises, freezes and runs them, and systematically strips forecasts as ungrounded. This protects against overclaiming, but it means no agent ever receives calibration feedback.

The objective contract's 'recitation countermodel' (item 3) is the only institutionalised prediction. It is a predicted shortcut ceiling, computed after the run from observed prefixes. It is a natural place to add 'predicted candidate performance' alongside 'predicted shortcut performance'.

The convention 'family_wide_exclusion: false / not a survivor count' prevents over-pruning but also blocks principled deprioritisation. The register cannot say 'family X has failed k times under conditions Y; base rate p'. A fact register with scope fields would allow a calibrated base rate without claiming impossibility.

Base rate visible from the documents (my tally, inference): native byte-addition E3 attempts since 10-15 (N151/C151/RC151, NATIVE-BIND V1, NATIVE-BIND V2.1 tech, v3, v5.1-R2, V6-R1, native_next B) show 0 that cleared both taught acquisition and the held causal gate. A register-only forecaster would have predicted most of the recent outcomes. This is a cheap first benchmark for knowledge-base generalisation.

Fact definitions need units: the same V6 cue/noise fact appears as 1:37 (analytic per-neuron content RMS vs noise SD, NEXT_DESIGN.md:7) and as 1/70-1/87 (measured hidden-distance ratio, REVISION.md:43-48; MEMO.md:42). Both are correct, but they could be confused without a stored metric definition.

Proposed structure for Q4, testing the KB for generalisation. (a) UNIT_FACTS.jsonl with scope fields and status links. (b) PREDICTIONS/<design>.json written before freeze and hashed into SOURCE_LOCK; it includes derived_from fact IDs and a register-only base-rate forecast as the null forecaster. (c) PREDICTION_SCORES.json at post-audit (hit/miss, interval coverage, Brier/log score per agent). A fact used in a failed cross-substrate prediction gets a 'transfer_failed@substrate' annotation; a fact with at least 2 successful cross-substrate predictions earns a 'transferable' tag. (d) At each census, a blinded retrodiction test: freeze the KB at date T, have a fresh agent predict the outcomes of deliveries after T from the KB alone, and score it against actuals. KB versions that do not beat the base-rate forecaster indicate facts that are not generalising.
Cycles directories (39) preserve sources, failures and reviews for provenance, but there is no aggregation step that lifts recurring errors into a cross-delivery checklist.

The route retrospective's own diagnosis (REPORT.md:7,130: local reports state limits accurately, but the limits are not carried into the next design or oral summaries) is confirmed by the newer evidence: STOP narrowing, the address-gate loss between v4 and V6, and orphaned D1-D3/U047.

skill_recommendations.name: unit-fact-register
skill_recommendations.rule: After every delivery's post-audit, add or update rows in a canonical UNIT_FACTS register. Each row has: id, claim, evidence level E0-E4, learner/substrate identity, supplied priors, feedback regime, dose, comparator AND the best trivial baseline, effect+CI, independent units, scope limits, source path:line, status (active/narrowed/superseded/refuted), and narrowed_by/supersedes links. CATALOG/MEMO tables are generated from the register, never hand-edited. A linter fails if a summary quotes a narrowed fact without its comparator.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-00, KT-01 and KT-04: facts currently live in free text, and narrowings (STOP vs FIXED_1, CREDIT inert) are lost in summaries.

skill_recommendations.name: design-prior-facts-and-predictions-block
skill_recommendations.rule: Every design must add a sixth block to the contract's required design block. It lists the fact IDs relied on, the failure-class IDs addressed, and the generalisation levers considered (adopt/reject/test). It gives numeric point+interval or probability predictions for each primary and guard endpoint, plus a register-only base-rate forecast. The block is hashed into SOURCE_LOCK before any feedback. The launcher fails closed if it is missing, as learning_spectrum/src/launch_gate.py did. Reviewers may mark predictions as ungrounded but may not delete them.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-03 and KT-10: the precedent existed (learning_spectrum) and was abandoned; forecasts are currently deleted, so there is no calibration signal.

skill_recommendations.name: prediction-scoring-post-audit
skill_recommendations.rule: In the post-run audit, score every registered prediction (hit/miss, interval coverage, Brier/log score). Record the result in PREDICTION_SCORES.json. Update each fact the prediction was derived from with a transfer_ok or transfer_failed annotation for the new substrate. Report per-agent calibration in each census. A falsified 'first correction' (e.g., the V6 rescale) must be recorded as a failed prediction of hypothesis H, not only as 'candidate closed'.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-03: implicit predictions (rescale fix, FIXED_1 ceiling, v5.1 one-class collapse) were never scored, so the knowledge base cannot tell which facts generalise.

skill_recommendations.name: failure-class-preflight-library
skill_recommendations.rule: Maintain FAILURE_CLASSES with a seconds-scale check and incident list for each class. At minimum: FC-ADDR (same-input/different-noise vs different-input/same-noise; leave-one-out prompt ID > chance; frozen-code coverage readout on held items), FC-ACQ (small taught-acquisition preflight before any E3 roster), FC-GATE (gate must fail a negative control and pass an oracle), FC-INERT (treatment-vs-control update/state digest differs by a pre-stated minimum), FC-WEAKCOMP (the trivial-policy panel of constant/mode/FIXED_k/position/frequency is always a comparator), FC-COMMONMODE (the auditor does not import the code under test), FC-FIXTURE (fixture parameters and locks read from the actual production path). Any change to front end, learner or readout must run every applicable check at birth and cite the class IDs.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-02, KT-05, KT-09 and KT-11: the address failure recurred at least 5 times, and gate-insensitivity recurred in 5 forms, because lessons stayed delivery-local.

skill_recommendations.name: claim-citation-linter
skill_recommendations.rule: Before any design, memo or review is committed, flag every numeric or historical claim about prior work that lacks a fact ID. Check the quoted value, comparator and scope caveats against the register. Block claims that drop a recorded caveat (e.g., 'tally 98-100%' without 'removes composition') or that mix results from different decoders or substrates.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-06: Claude misremembered v3 history, register coverage and STOP magnitude, and these were caught only by manual cross-agent review.

skill_recommendations.name: hypothesis-lifecycle-and-pointer-staleness
skill_recommendations.rule: Keep a HYPOTHESES ledger (proposed/active/tested/retired/transferred). Each design names the hypothesis IDs it tests or retires. On a substrate change, every active hypothesis must be explicitly transferred or retired, with reasons. A session-start check flags any CURRENT_* or priority file older than the newest delivery in its track, and any README that calls a stale file 'current decision'.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-08: U047 PRIORITY_DESIGN and D1-D3 PRIORITY_HYPOTHESIS were orphaned, and CURRENT_ARITHMETIC (10-15) is stale.

skill_recommendations.name: kb-sync-and-link-check
skill_recommendations.rule: Every agent branch must contain the canonical KB directory (contract, unit facts, failure classes, hypotheses, census). A session-start hook verifies it is present and current. A link checker fails on absolute /Users/... paths or relative links with missing targets. Facts with local-only sources are tagged UNVERIFIABLE_IN_REPO and cannot serve as the sole basis of a design decision.
skill_recommendations.rationale: KT-07: the Claude branch lacks PROJECT_DOCUMENTS, 93 files use local absolute paths, and the only native E3 positives (V9.9A/B) are not in the repo.

skill_recommendations.name: kb-generalization-benchmark
skill_recommendations.rule: At each census, freeze the KB at date T and give a fresh agent only the KB. Have it predict the outcomes of all deliveries after T (taught acquisition, held E3, gate verdicts). Score it against actuals and against a base-rate forecaster. Demote facts whose predictions repeatedly fail; promote facts that predict correctly across substrates as 'transferable'. Run as a meta-task with no new experiments.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Q4: this makes 'generalisation from unit learned knowledge' measurable at the research level, using only existing documents.

lenses.lens: Cross-agent review and the current Claude branch (LEARNED-BANK V1 on origin/charming-head plus its continuation origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850; Claude<->Codex reviews for v4, v5, v5.1 and v6)
lenses.summary:
Note on branches: origin/charming-head stops at cycle 2. Amendment A1, LOCK.json, check_lock, CYCLE3 and the main-run start live on origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850 (commits 1ce1eadb and 84c530d4).

(a) LEARNED-BANK V1 has several practices worth turning into skills. The strongest is a testbed audit. On the same inputs and splits, evaluator-only BP, DFA and FROZEN learners showed that T-MOD cannot test the hypothesis (even exact gradient got held 0.00/0.11), while parity can. Other good practices: an ORACLE plumbing arm, a SHUF control rebuilt so binary labels do not become anti-parity, balanced accuracy, a surrogate calibrated against the native store, a code-hash lock enforced in run.py, a dress rehearsal with the identical command, and unit checks that carry over earlier incidents (the v4 sign and passive-adaptation bugs, the V6 identity gate).

It also has risks:
- The task was swapped away from addition.
- The design has no E-level or objective-contract block.
- A1 (task, metric, a 10x learning rate, 2x passes, a 0.20 margin) was written after the native D2 results were seen. The only check between A1 and the main worlds was a rehearsal on a world already used for tuning.
- summarize.py fails open. Missing arms count as passing gates, and any number of worlds can yield "supported". The rehearsal's SUMMARY.json already says "supported" for one dev world.
- The lock does not hash the native stores.
- A planned native-parity check was dropped without a note.
- Nothing measures retention of old facts, even though learned-bank codes drift (Jaccard 0.04 between checkpoints).
- The main run started 1.7 minutes after the lock, with no outside review and no authorization record.

(b) Reviews that re-ran code worked; reviews that re-read claims did not.
- Claude's read-only review of v4 introduced a wrong dose number. Codex traced it to a coefficient on one source line.
- Codex's v5.1 audit only re-checked artifacts, and it called the port "qualified". Claude's short re-execution showed three things: the port test cannot fail, the byte grouping was already fixed at birth, and the next stage collapses even with a perfect upstream.
- Codex then re-ran Claude's audit. It corrected Claude's counts and history claims and found two new defects. Its own verdict was "Artifact reproducibility checks were insufficient as design and integration validation".
- Codex removed unsupported claims and an authorization overreach from Claude's v6. But its own V6-R1 design locked an initialization that buried the input under noise (roughly 70x). Its static check only verified counts, so the problem showed up only after 8 histories all scored 0%. The next delivery added a pre-run gate and saved a 43,520-record roster. That is a lesson that transferred.

Every Claude design (v4, v5, v6, LEARNED-BANK) leaves out the contract's E-level block, and every Codex revision adds it back.

findings.title: Testbed discriminability audit proved T-MOD could not test the hypothesis (good practice)
findings.description: Document states: before blaming the local rule, cycle 2 ran an evaluator-only one-hidden-layer network on the identical FE-PERM traces and splits with three credit modes: FROZEN (random features), BP (exact gradient) and DFA (the candidate's rule). MOD held accuracy was 0.00/0.11 even with BP, so 'T-MOD tells us nothing about local learning'. CARRY/CMP were solved by FROZEN, so they cannot show feature learning. PAR was failed by FROZEN (0.22-0.24) and solved by both BP and DFA (1.00/1.00). Inference: this is the most reusable practice on the branch. A task is admissible for a mechanism claim only if an unconstrained ceiling passes, the no-learning floor fails, and the candidate's rule can close the gap in a cheap surrogate.
findings.how_detected: Author's own cycle-2 audit, after the native T-MOD dev run showed LEARN 0.000 held (CYCLE2.md lines 5-15)
findings.generic_safeguard: Before any candidate run, require a task-admissibility table on identical inputs and splits: ceiling learner (unconstrained, evaluator-only) must pass; frozen/random floor must fail; candidate rule in a surrogate must be able to pass. If any cell fails, the task cannot test the claim, and its result may not be read as evidence for or against the mechanism.

findings.title: Task substitution from addition (T-MOD) to parity (T-PAR), with no E-level or objective-contract block
findings.description: Document states: Amendment A1 makes parity of a+b (a one-bit answer) the primary task and drops T-MOD from the main run. Codex's V6-R1 review had warned 'No parity/modulo/recall success replaces that endpoint'. The objective contract requires every design to state its claim level (E0-E4), exposure audit, recitation countermodel, causal controls and promotion rule. A grep of LEARNED-BANK DESIGN.md and CYCLE1-3.md for E0-E4, 'recitation', 'contract', 'intervening' and 'retention' returns nothing. Inference: the substitution is honestly motivated by LB-01. But a positive PAR verdict ('condition 1 supported') could be read as progress toward E3 addition. The task-level distance from the objective (single-digit, one bit, no own EOS, no intervening learning) is never stated.
evidence: minifly_v6_revised_design_20261023/REVIEW.md line 14 ('No parity/modulo/recall success replaces that endpoint')
git grep -E '\bE[0-4]\b|recitation|contract|intervening|retention' on LEARNED-BANK docs: no matches (exit 1)
findings.how_detected: Not caught. No reviewer saw LEARNED-BANK before the main run. Found in this analysis.
findings.generic_safeguard: Any amendment that changes the primary task must re-derive the contract block: claim level, distance from the program objective (which E3 properties are dropped), and the follow-up experiment that would reconnect to the objective. A design linter refuses DESIGN.md files without the five contract headings.

findings.title: Amendment A1 adopted after native dev evidence; only a tuned dev world checked it before the main worlds
findings.description: Document states: the D2 native confirmation (LEARN 0.824 vs FROZEN 0.331 and SHUF 0.357) was seen in cycle 2. The 0.20 margin, eta0 = 0.03 (10x the provisional value), 150 passes, the balanced metric and the new SHUF were proposed in the same document and adopted at the cycle-3 lock. The rehearsal ran on D3, which had been used for surrogate tuning, and CYCLE3 calls it 'a second native development confirmation, not evidence'. Inference: the protections are that M1-M4 are fresh and that tuning was confined to dev worlds, as DESIGN.md section 7 required. But no untouched validation world sat between the amendment and the main run. The margin was set after the observed effect size (about 0.47-0.49) was known. Also, 'fresh worlds' are new splits of the same 100-prompt universe, so every M-world held prompt was taught and tuned on in some D world.
evidence: origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/cycles/CYCLE2.md lines 59-70 (settings chosen; D2 native table), lines 101-112 (proposed rule)
origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/data.py lines 38-53 (worlds differ only by split and seed over the same 55 orbits)
findings.how_detected: Partly disclosed by the author (CYCLE3.md line 46). The timing risk was not caught.
findings.generic_safeguard: Amendment rule: list every result seen before the amendment, and set margins from a priori variance (for example, a dev-world spread) rather than the observed effect. Require one untouched validation world run under the lock after the amendment, or declare in the lock that the main worlds are the first independent test.

findings.title: Locked decision reducer fails open: missing arms pass gates, any world count can yield 'supported', and a dev world is already labelled 'supported'
findings.description: Document states (code): a missing ORACLE or COPY history gives a gate value of None, and gates_ok uses 'is not False', so a missing arm passes. A world without LEARN/FROZEN/SHUF is silently skipped. overall = 'supported' if n_ok == len(verdict), with no check that len(verdict) is 4. That contradicts the locked rule 'supported if 4/4'. The spec says 'a failed gate makes that world uninformative', but the code counts it as non-supporting. The rehearsal's results/c3_rehearsal/SUMMARY.json reports overall 'supported' (1/1) for development world D3. The CYCLE3 audit only recomputed balanced accuracy by hand on the happy path, so it missed these.
evidence: origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/summarize.py lines 76-101 (skip at 76; gate None at 87, 91; 'is not False' at 92-93; overall at 99-100)
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Found in this analysis by reading the locked summarize.py against LOCK.json.
findings.generic_safeguard: Mutation-test every verdict reducer before the lock on fixtures that must not pass: a missing arm, a missing world, a failed gate, a borderline margin, and a dev-world tag. The denominator is read from LOCK.json; None means fail closed and is reported as 'uninformative'. Any output from a non-main world is stamped DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE instead of a verdict word.

findings.title: Lock hash closure is incomplete, and main-world blindness is enforced only in run.py
findings.description: Document states (code): make_lock.py hashes lb1.py, data.py, run.py, summarize.py, main.sh and fastmem.py. fastmem.py imports bootstrap.py, which puts minifly_a_v3/src on the path and imports stores (the native equations). Neither bootstrap.py nor stores.py is hashed, and neither is checks.py. check_lock runs only in run.py. data.make_world, surrogate.py and diag_mlp.py accept any world name, including M1-M4, with no guard or access ledger. Inference: the claim that M1-M4 were never touched rests on the author's statement and the absence of M worlds in the committed logs. A change to the native stores would not trip the lock.
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Found in this analysis.
findings.generic_safeguard: Build the lock from the runtime import closure (hash every file in sys.modules that sits under the repo after a dry import), plus checks and the data generator. Put the held-out guard inside the world generator itself: refuse main-world names without a valid lock, and append every access (caller, time) to a ledger committed with the results.

findings.title: Planned native-parity unit check dropped silently; identity gate run only on D1's birth
findings.description: Document states: DESIGN.md section 9 cycle 1 lists 'native parity of a bank with homeostasis off' as a unit check. checks.py has no such check, and CYCLE1.md neither lists nor explains its absence (34/34 'pass'). The design also lists an 'input-identity gate at birth' (section 6, a V6 lesson). checks.py runs it only for world D1's model seed, and run.py has no per-world birth gate, so the M1-M4 births are never identity-gated. Inference: the 'N/N checks pass' summary hides the gap between planned and implemented checks.
evidence: origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/DESIGN.md line 99 (planned native parity) and line 77 (identity gate, V6 lesson)
origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/checks.py lines 25-104 (world D1 only; no parity check)
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Found by grepping 'parity' across the design, cycles and checks.
findings.generic_safeguard: Keep a check manifest: each check promised in DESIGN.md gets an ID, and checks.py must report each ID as pass, fail or explicitly DROPPED with a reason. Birth-time gates (identity, input-vs-noise) run inside the main runner for every world, not once in a unit test.

findings.title: Decision rule is relative to a below-chance FROZEN arm, has no absolute floor, and has no retention clause despite near-total code drift
findings.description: Document states: FROZEN balanced held is 0.331 on D2 (below chance), and the rule needs LEARN >= FROZEN + 0.20 and >= SHUF + 0.20. The kernel clauses only need 'final > birth'. LEARN's learned-bank codes for taught prompts drift almost completely between checkpoints (min_drift_L 0.044 on D2 PAR) while taught accuracy stays 1.0, because the store re-learns. Inference: a LEARN score near 0.55-0.70 could pass whenever controls are anti-correlated. The 'final > birth' clauses are met by almost any drift. Address drift of this size would destroy old knowledge in the program's continual setting (old knowledge protected), yet no retention or intervening-learning probe is in the rule.
evidence: minifly_b/package/DOCS/MINIFLY_OBJECTIVE_CONTRACT.md line 19 (E3 requires delayed and intervening-learning probes)
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Drift was noted as a meter (CYCLE1.md line 15; CYCLE2.md lines 77-80) but not put in the rule.
findings.generic_safeguard: Every relative clause gets an absolute companion: a floor above chance or majority class, plus the best exposure-only countermodel. Monotone clauses ('above birth') need a minimum effect. Any learner whose addresses move must include an old-fact retention probe after intervening learning in the primary rule.

findings.title: Provenance and authorization: pre-registration not verifiable, rationale off-repo, main run launched 1.7 minutes after the lock with no outside review
findings.description: Document states: DESIGN.md says it was 'written before any code'. Yet the cycle-1 commit, 6 minutes after the design commit, adds 1,001 lines of code plus run results. The motivating 'condition 1 from the emergence discussion' is not in any committed file. There is no AUTHORIZATION record for the main run (about 11 CPU-hours). The lock commit is 03:34:11 and the main-run-started commit is 03:35:53. By contrast, Codex's V6-R1 SPEC.json carries a machine-readable authorization block (design true; implementation, training and adoption false), and verify_design.py asserts it. Inference: commit timing cannot prove design-before-code, and self-authorization from the design text ('After the lock: run the main worlds') skipped the cross-agent review that caught real defects in every earlier version.
evidence: git log origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850: 4d8952c3 01:41:18 (design), 0b80d02a 01:47:39 (11 files, 1001 insertions), 1ce1eadb 03:34:11 (lock), 84c530d4 03:35:53 (main run started)
findings.how_detected: Not caught. Found from git history in this analysis.
findings.generic_safeguard: Pre-registration means the design is pushed with its hash before any code commit, and the code commit names that hash. Rationale from chat must be written into the repo. A long run needs AUTHORIZATION.json naming the human approval and its scope, plus one external review of the lock and the reducer.

findings.title: Read-only review introduced a wrong quantitative premise; caught only by tracing the number to source code
findings.description: Document states: Claude's v4 review ('Read-only review; nothing re-run') said one native teaching event moves an output by about 0.01-0.02 and derived v5 doses from that. Codex's v5 review traced the figure to port_baseline.py line 8, where the coefficient was (tanh(z/2)-target)/32, an attenuated write. A separate full-strength fixture had measured -0.16411. Claude later conceded: 'I misread the v4 measurement'. Codex also corrected overstatements in Claude's retrospective, such as 'no segments ever formed'.
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent review (Codex review of v5, which traced the source line)
findings.generic_safeguard: Any number a reviewer or designer carries from another experiment must cite the producing code line and the exact coefficients and conditions. A reviewer must re-measure it, or label it UNVERIFIED and keep it out of dose or design derivations.

findings.title: The author's artifact audit passed a gate that could not fail; executing review exposed it in seconds
findings.description: Document states: Codex v5.1 declared the native output port 'qualified' (100% exact; matched no-write 0%), and its FINAL_AUDIT was an 'Independent artifact reduction, no learner execution' that accepted it. Claude's executing review showed three things. (1) The port test 'passes, but it can't fail': the activity patterns don't overlap, so any write with the right sign gives the right bit. (2) The byte-stage grouping was set by the random starting values; it is computable from the initial weights in about a second. (3) A counterfactual run of Codex's unchanged context-class code on a perfect upstream collapsed to one class, so fixing only the byte stage would 'guarantee another NO_ADVANCE'. Codex's reconciliation concluded: 'Artifact reproducibility checks were insufficient as design and integration validation'.
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent executing review (Claude), confirmed by the author's reconciliation (Codex)
findings.generic_safeguard: Gate-falsifiability rule: every qualification gate must show a constructed input it rejects (for example, overlapping patterns for a port, or noise-only input for an identity gate). Before fixing stage k, run stage k+1 unchanged on an oracle (perfect) upstream so the next blocker is found in the same cycle.

findings.title: Audit-of-the-audit corrected the reviewer's own overclaims and found new defects
findings.description: Document states: Codex re-ran each Claude claim with scripts under a CPU cap. A1 was 'CONFIRMED_WITH_QUANTITATIVE_CORRECTION': 6 of 8 settings kept the birth partition, not Claude's 7, and reconstruction MSE fell 0.69-0.75, so 'not literally zero learning'. A3 re-ran the shared-cell risk at the actual native activity fraction 0.0354 instead of Claude's 2%. New defects: A4 (the port fixture hard-codes 0.02, against the lock's native fraction) and A5 (calibration omits the REPLY transition). A6 corrected Claude's history claim: v3 did run full addition histories, with held 0%. v5.1-R2 then adopted the actual masks, frames matched to REPLY, and farthest-first initialization. Inference: reviewers overclaim too. Effective reconciliation re-executes the reviewer's claims with the author's real parameters and keeps a status taxonomy plus a scope limit for each finding.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/V51_CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECONCILIATION_20261020/context/check_context.py lines 1-20 (RLIMIT_CPU 30 s; author code loaded unchanged via AST)
findings.how_detected: Author's reconciliation of a cross-agent audit (Codex)
findings.generic_safeguard: Reconciliation protocol: for each received finding, re-execute it with the author's actual parameters and assign CONFIRMED, CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION, REFUTED, NEW_DEFECT or SCOPE_LIMITED, with the numbers that differ. Only then change the design.

findings.title: Codex's revision of Claude's v6 removed unsupported claims and an authorization overreach
findings.description: Document states: Claude's v6 memo said the 254-mechanism register 'has no entries for sequential state ... gating'. It called one-step local credit '(approved)', listed AuGMEnT as a candidate, gave sample-count forecasts, and treated toy non-arithmetic tasks as allowed first steps. Codex's REVIEW responded point by point. It found context routing and learned encoders in the full register. It ruled that 'A prior memo's word approved is not human authorization', that AuGMEnT 'explicitly includes attention-related feedback', and that the forecasts were ungrounded and deleted. It also ruled that no parity/modulo success replaces the endpoint. Claude's original was kept verbatim, with its git blob SHA checked by verify_design.py.
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent design review (Codex)
findings.generic_safeguard: Design review checklist: (1) every historical or negative claim about the ledger is checked against the full register; (2) any 'approved' or 'allowed' must cite a human message; (3) each borrowed method is checked against the hard constraints using its primary paper, not its gist; (4) forecasts without a derivation are deleted.

findings.title: Static design verification missed an operating-regime defect; the lesson then turned into a pre-run gate that saved a roster
findings.description: Document states: Codex's V6-R1 SPEC locked nonbias init std 0.05/sqrt(348), assuming about 348 active inputs, while the byte input is one-hot. verify_design.py asserts counts, hashes and links only. R1 ran 8 histories with 0% everywhere, including taught OLD. Post-hoc, same-prompt/different-tape distances were about 70-90x larger than different-prompt/same-tape distances, so the state carried noise, not input. Claude's feasibility note turned this into 'Input-vs-noise gate on every recurrent candidate ... V6-R1 failed this by about 70x undetected'. NATIVE-NEXT V1 applied an input-state admission gate before launch: INPUT_STATE_NOT_ADMITTED, and the 43,520-record roster was not launched. Inference: this is a clean example of research-level transfer, from incident to cheap pre-run gate. It also shows that design-time checks must cover signal-to-noise and scale, not only arithmetic consistency.
evidence: minifly_v6_r1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md lines 9-18; REVISION.md lines 43-50; NEXT_DESIGN.md line 7
findings.how_detected: Author's post-run diagnosis (Codex), generalized by Claude, and applied as a pre-run gate by Codex in the next delivery

findings.title: Author's own bugs found only after histories ran: parity checks did not test direction, and the directional fixture was confounded
findings.description: Document states: in Codex's v4 implementation, Python [-0:] replayed the full 32-record ring when zero replay was requested. A source-to-port audit found the bit wrapper's teaching sign reversed after six complete wrong-sign histories had run: 'The earlier native-event parity check had not tested the new wrapper's directional learning'. The first directional fixture then confused teaching with passive adaptation and needed a matched no-write control. LEARNED-BANK V1's checks.py carries these lessons over. It checks that two teaching records move every margin toward the target, that a zero coefficient equals a passive event (state-hash equal), and that probes leave the state hash unchanged.

process_observations: origin/charming-head is stale for this lens. The amendment, LOCK.json, check_lock, CYCLE3 and main-run start are only on origin/claude/charming-clarke-u9g850 (1ce1eadb, 84c530d4). Any skill that audits 'the current Claude branch' should resolve the newest descendant commit first.

LEARNED-BANK V1 went from design commit to main-run start in about 1 h 54 min (01:41 to 03:35) across three self-run cycles. Codex deliveries show the opposite failure: Claude's v5.1 audit counted 119 files and 28.5k lines against 173 CPU-s of accepted compute (CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECEIVED.txt line 42). One agent under-reviews and the other over-qualifies. A skill should fix review depth by stake (main run vs dev), not by agent habit.

The most effective reviews took seconds of execution: computing byte groupings from the initial weights, running the author's unchanged next stage on an oracle upstream, or tracing a quoted number to a coefficient on one source line. The least effective was a careful read-only review that inherited a mis-scaled number (CLAUDE_REVIEW_V4.md).

Cross-agent review has caught a substantive defect in every reviewed round (v4 claims treated as facts; v5 dose and reference; v5.1 unfalsifiable port, birth-fixed aliasing and next-stage collapse; v6 authorization and history overclaims). LEARNED-BANK V1 is the first recent delivery to reach a main run with no outside review.

Research-level transfer is visible and works when a lesson becomes a cheap check. Examples: v4 sign/passive bugs became LEARNED-BANK directional and zero-coefficient checks; the V6-R1 noise failure became the NATIVE-NEXT input-state gate, which saved a 43,520-record roster. Transfer fails when a lesson stays prose (the E0-E4 contract existed but recurred as drift: ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE REPORT.md line 31).
Machine-readable verdict files can outrank prose caveats. The rehearsal SUMMARY.json says 'supported' while CYCLE3.md says 'not evidence'. Downstream agents usually read the JSON.
Codex's reconciliation schema (status taxonomy, scope_limit for each finding, hashes of received text, CPU-capped scripts that load author code unchanged) is ready to template as a skill.
No main-world results for LEARNED-BANK exist yet on any branch. The birth checkpoints in main_run.log are the only main-world data, so the findings here concern protocol, not outcome.

skill_recommendations.name: task-admissibility-audit
skill_recommendations.rule: Before a candidate experiment, run evaluator-only learners on the identical inputs and splits: an unconstrained ceiling (e.g., BP), a frozen/random-feature floor, and the candidate's own rule in a calibrated surrogate. Admit the task only if ceiling passes, floor fails and the candidate can pass. If the task changes as a result, log it as TASK_SUBSTITUTION, re-derive the E-level and state which program-objective properties are lost.
skill_recommendations.rationale: LEARNED-BANK cycle 2 showed T-MOD was untestable even for BP and that CARRY/CMP were solved by frozen features (CYCLE2.md lines 17-36). The same audit enabled a substitution away from addition that no one reviewed (DESIGN.md section 11; V6 REVIEW.md line 14).

skill_recommendations.name: verdict-reducer-mutation-tests
skill_recommendations.rule: Every locked summarize or verdict script must pass fixture tests that remove an arm, remove a world, fail each gate, sit exactly on a margin, and use a dev-world tag. The denominator comes from LOCK.json; a None gate value fails closed as 'uninformative'; non-main worlds print DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE instead of a verdict.
skill_recommendations.rationale: LEARNED-BANK summarize.py lines 76-101 treat missing ORACLE/COPY as passing and return 'supported' for any world count. The rehearsal SUMMARY.json already says 'supported' for one dev world.

skill_recommendations.name: lock-import-closure-and-heldout-guard
skill_recommendations.rule: Build LOCK.json from the runtime import closure (all repo files in sys.modules after a dry import), plus checks and data generators. Put the held-out or main-world guard inside the world generator, and log every access to a committed ledger.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The LEARNED-BANK lock omits bootstrap.py and minifly_a_v3 stores (make_lock.py line 12; bootstrap.py lines 11-14). Only run.py enforces the lock; surrogate.py and diag_mlp.py accept M worlds.

skill_recommendations.name: executing-cross-review
skill_recommendations.rule: A review of another agent's delivery must (1) re-execute each gate on a constructed input it should reject; (2) run the next stage unchanged on an oracle upstream; (3) trace every quoted number to its producing code line and coefficients; (4) commit its scripts with repo-relative paths and CPU caps. Read-only findings are labelled UNVERIFIED.
skill_recommendations.rationale: The read-only v4 review propagated a mis-scaled dose (REVIEW.md F05). The executing v5.1 review found an unfalsifiable port, birth-fixed aliasing and next-stage collapse in seconds (CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECEIVED.txt lines 16-34), all missed by the author's artifact-only FINAL_AUDIT.

skill_recommendations.name: reconcile-received-review
skill_recommendations.rule: When receiving a review, re-run each claim with the author's actual parameters and record a status for each finding (CONFIRMED / CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION / REFUTED / NEW_DEFECT / SCOPE_LIMITED), with differing numbers and a scope limit, before changing the design.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Codex's reconciliation corrected Claude's 7/8 to 6/8 and 'no learning' to an MSE drop of 0.69-0.75, re-measured at the native density 0.0354 instead of 2%, and found two new defects (AUDIT.json A1-A7).

skill_recommendations.name: amendment-after-evidence-protocol
skill_recommendations.rule: Any amendment written after seeing dev results lists every result seen, sets margins from a priori variance rather than the observed effect, and is followed by one untouched validation world under the lock, or the lock states explicitly that the main worlds are the first independent test.
skill_recommendations.rationale: A1 (task, metric, 10x eta0, 2x passes, 0.20 margin) followed the D2 native result. The only check before the main run was a rehearsal on surrogate-tuned D3 (CYCLE2.md lines 59-70; CYCLE3.md line 46).

skill_recommendations.name: contract-block-lint
skill_recommendations.rule: Refuse to lock or launch unless DESIGN.md and LOCK.json contain the objective contract's five fields: claim level E0-E4, exposure audit, recitation and exposure-only countermodel, causal and positive controls, promotion and stop rule. Relative clauses need an absolute floor, and drifting-address learners need an old-fact retention clause.
skill_recommendations.rationale: Claude designs v4/v5/v6/LEARNED-BANK contain zero E-level mentions, while Codex revisions add them (3-5 each). LEARNED-BANK's rule compares against a below-chance FROZEN (0.331) and ignores code drift at Jaccard 0.044.

skill_recommendations.name: regime-preflight-registry
skill_recommendations.rule: Keep a cross-experiment registry of named admission gates derived from past incidents (input-vs-noise contrast, actual activity density, shared support at the decision frame, teaching direction against a matched passive control, zero-count edge cases). Every new design runs all applicable gates on its real births before any learning run, and each new incident adds a gate.
skill_recommendations.rationale: V6-R1's roughly 70x noise dominance passed static verification and cost 8 null histories (REVISION.md lines 43-50). Turned into a gate, the same lesson stopped NATIVE-NEXT before a 43,520-record roster (REPORT.md lines 14-29). The v4 sign and replay bugs became LEARNED-BANK checks (checks.py lines 83-104).

skill_recommendations.name: check-manifest-and-authorization-record
skill_recommendations.rule: Every check promised in the design gets an ID that checks.py reports as pass, fail or DROPPED with a reason. A main run requires AUTHORIZATION.json citing the human approval and its scope, and one external review of the lock and reducer. Rationale from chat is committed before the design hash is taken.
skill_recommendations.rationale: LEARNED-BANK's planned native-parity check vanished silently (DESIGN.md line 99 vs checks.py). The main run began 1.7 minutes after the lock with no authorization record, and its motivating 'emergence discussion' is not in the repo.

lenses.lens: What the "three cycles" actually change: classification of every recorded cycle revision (ops / test-fixture / measurement-reducer / learner-implementation bug / scientific parameter-mechanism / gate-criterion / scope / world), whether it was informed by outcome data, whether it was preregistered, whether tests were weakened, and whether "3 cycles" is the right unit
lenses.summary:
I sampled 36 of the 39 cycle-bearing deliveries, dated 2026-10-07 to 10-24 (Codex and Claude, addition, arithmetic, MiniFly and native lines, plus minifly_learned_bank_v1 on origin/charming-head). By my own count of about 140 revisions, roughly 76% are engineering: ops 28%, measurement/reducer 29%, test fixtures 14%, learner-implementation bugs 6%. Scientific parameter/mechanism changes are about 9%, gate changes 3%, scope 5%, world changes 7%. The cycles are mostly staged technical qualification. In 13 of 36 deliveries they never looked at the scientific endpoint, and the official runs that followed (240–492 jobs each) were mostly negative. That is 10 of 12 official runs; one adoption rests on engineered priors, and one STOP-ONLY "confirmation" turned out, one delivery later, to be about equal to a fixed-length stopping baseline.

I found no case where a scientific gate was loosened until it passed, and no case where dev worlds were later counted as official evidence. The documents are unusually honest about failures (63 failure artifacts preserved). The real problems are elsewhere:
- Within-cycle mechanism swaps: addition_rule tried three designs in sequence and reported the winner on fresh worlds with an engineered ordinal prior. The route retrospective (A03/A04) names this as a drift node.
- Endpoint or task amendments after seeing dev outcomes: observation_content_core, gated_feedback Cstar, and the learned_bank switch from MOD to PAR.
- Vacuous tests that cannot fail, accepted as qualification: the v5.1 port test, mechanism_transfer's tamper suite, the SHUF derangement control, the native_next EOS fixture.
- A negated teaching sign in v4 that survived two cycles.
- The same defect classes re-found again and again: import collisions in at least 10 deliveries, JSON tuple/list round-trips, fly_id equality.
- Cycle 3 often stands in for the official run, on 1–2 worlds.

Of 168 cycle notes, 81 carry "no parameter changed" disclaimers. None states a researcher-level falsifiable prediction (the "预测" hits refer to the model's own byte predictions).

My judgement is that a fixed count of three is the wrong unit. It pads some exercises (identical AUDIT.md in all three cycles; whole cycles that only rerun after an import fix). It truncates others ("no fourth cycle" while a signal is promising). And it lets staged prerequisite failures each cost a full cycle. Cycles should instead be bounded by exit criteria. Each should produce:
- a prediction written before the run;
- caught seeded bugs;
- a revision ledger tagged by category and by whether the outcome informed it, with world IDs;
- the endpoint checked against the strongest trivial baseline;
- an explicit decision: continue, revise, stop or escalate.

A cheap "cycle 0" should come first: check that the testbed can test the claim, then run the whole chain end to end.

findings.title: Cycles are mostly engineering qualification; the scientific endpoint is often never examined before large official runs
findings.description: Documents state: many technical cycles are explicitly blind to science ('Scientific jobs: 0', 'No DEV or confirmation science ran'), and cycle summary files carry no held-out/accuracy fields. Hundreds of official jobs then followed and were negative. By my classification of about 140 revisions across 36 deliveries, about 76% are ops/measurement/test-fixture/implementation fixes and about 9% are scientific changes. Cycles use about 4–12% of a delivery's records. Inference: blinding cycles to the endpoint guards against tuning, but it also removes any cheap go/no-go signal. v6_r1 shows the cost: 34,816 records ran with taught OLD at 0% in every arm, which a cheap E1 acquisition check would have caught.

findings.generic_safeguard: Every cycle reports the primary endpoint and a cheap taught-acquisition (E1) check on its dev worlds, against a range declared before the run. This viability check may only STOP or ESCALATE; it may not tune knobs. An official run is admitted only if the last cycle shows taught acquisition above a stated floor and held signal above the strongest shortcut, or the design states why it expects the official run to differ.

findings.title: Sequential mechanism swaps inside the cycles act as a hidden multi-design search; the winner carries an engineered task-shaped prior
findings.description: Documents state: in addition_rule, cycle 1 scored 0% held-out, so the input topology was changed to role-partitioned banks. Cycle 2 still scored 0%, so the candidate's content operation was replaced by a single ordinal scalar with an 'engineered ordinal output prior'. Cycle 3 on fresh worlds scored 87.5% held-out. The protocol had pre-authorised 'one explicit common structure or content operation' per documented failure and forbade a fourth cycle, and fresh worlds were used, so these mitigations existed. The route retrospective later found that this is where the native Full151 learner was replaced by an engineered numeric learner that 'did not execute native Full151 write equations', and that the result was later loosely called an 'original MiniFly core upgrade'. Inference: three sequential designs were tried and the best is reported. The prior chosen after failure makes addition linear in the representation, so the designer supplied the function class. That is specification gaming at the design level, even with fresh-world evaluation.

findings.how_detected: Disclosed in the cycle docs at the time. Recognised as drift only by the route retrospective (2026-10-14), a week later.
findings.generic_safeguard: Tag each revision SCI/GATE/SCOPE/WORLD/OPS/TEST/MEAS/IMPL with an informed_by_outcome flag and the world IDs that informed it. A SCI revision informed by outcome (a) increments a visible designs-tried counter k, reported as 'best of k'; (b) forces a learner lineage rename when the operative learning equations change; (c) is checked against a declared allowed-inductive-bias list, where task-shaped priors such as ordinal or additive outputs or role slots demote the claim. Cap SCI revisions per exercise.

findings.generic_safeguard: An endpoint amendment protocol. Amendments are allowed only for candidate-blind reasons: ceiling, testbed invalidity shown with oracle/BP/frozen arms, or a measurement defect. Never for the candidate's relative profile. Every amendment goes into LOCK.json with the path to the evidence that motivated it, keeps the original endpoint reported as co-primary, and states its effect on the E-level claim and its distance from the program objective. Normalisers such as compute caps must come from a rule fixed before the run and computed on reference arms only.

findings.title: Tests that cannot fail were accepted as qualification; most were caught late, one only by an external auditor
findings.description:
Documents state several cases:
- v5.1 cycle 2: the port test 'passes, but it can't fail' because the activity patterns don't overlap and decay cannot flip a sign. The fixture also hard-coded activity 0.02 where the specification said native 0.0354, and calibration omitted the REPLY transition. The Claude audit found these, not the cycles.
- mechanism_transfer cycle 2: the tamper rejections were vacuous because even the genuine receipt failed the disk audit (tuple/list round-trip).
- v3: the cycle-1 derivative check used zero input, so it was trivially satisfied; it was repaired in cycle 3.
- memory_channel: parity with an empty state was 'weak'.
- native_next: the EOS fixture used BASE's residual for every arm, so the arms were identical.
- learned_bank: a SHUF derangement of binary labels teaches anti-parity, a fully structured control that LEARN would beat for free.
- core_lineage: a selection fixture expected one control value to erase a group effect.
Inference: a passed check is treated as evidence without first showing that the check can fail.

findings.generic_safeguard: Mutation-tested qualification: every check ships with at least one seeded fault it must reject (wrong sign, collapsed slots, identical arms, wrong label), and runs the positive control first (a genuine artifact must pass before tamper rejections count). Fixtures must use representative state: nonzero state, overlapping patterns, the declared density. A mechanical diff checks that every spec parameter equals the fixture value.

findings.title: Negated teaching sign survived two cycles; six complete wrong-sign histories ran before a directional check existed
findings.description: Documents state: in v4 the port residual was negated relative to the native signed-write convention. Six complete invalid histories (432 record applications) and 16 records of a seventh ran before a new directional audit in cycle 3 detected it. The report says 'Event parity did not by itself qualify the new teaching port'. The same cycle also hit a Python [-0:] replay bug, which replayed 32 records when zero were requested, and a directional fixture that compared mismatched passive states. Cycle 3 needed five failed attempts and two technical-world changes before acceptance. Inference: cycles 1–2 tested equation parity of the native kernel but not the property that matters, namely that teaching moves the output toward the target compared with a matched no-write event.

findings.generic_safeguard: A mandatory cycle-1 check for any new learner or teaching port: (a) one teaching event moves the target margin in the target direction compared with a matched no-write event at identical time and activity, for both signs; (b) a zero-dose event equals the passive event; (c) zero replay or zero dose yields zero applications. learned_bank checks.py already includes these, so they should become a shared library rather than a per-delivery reinvention.

findings.title: The same engineering defect classes are re-discovered across deliveries; whole cycles are consumed by them
findings.description:
Documents state:
- Module or import name collisions with inherited modules occur in at least 10 deliveries.
- Treating fly_id identity as a scientific equality field was fixed twice.
- JSON tuple/list round-trip broke audits on consecutive days (observation_support on 10-11, mechanism_transfer on 10-12).
- A NumPy bool_ value broke JSON packaging.
In v6_r1, cycle 2 is explicitly a rerun of cycle 1 after an import collision ('Rerun the bounded technical suite as cycle 2'). Inference: no cross-delivery incident ledger or preflight lint exists, so knowledge does not transfer even at the engineering level. Cycle budgets are spent rediscovering known faults.
evidence: minifly_v6_r1_dev_20261023/cycles/01_REVIEW.md:7-9 (import data resolved to inherited module; 'Rerun the bounded technical suite as cycle 2')
findings.how_detected: Each one was self-detected locally at run time. The pattern across deliveries was never noted in any document I found.
findings.generic_safeguard: A shared known-defect preflight lint that runs before cycle 1. It covers: a unique package namespace with sys.path isolation and an import-origin assertion for every module; JSON round-trip equality of world plans and receipts; identity fields excluded from value equality; NumPy scalar serialisation; slice-boundary tests for zero limits. Every preserved failure gets one line appended to a repo-level incident ledger that design reviews must cite.

findings.title: Official confirmation of a proxy gate later shown to be roughly matched by a trivial fixed-length baseline
findings.description: Documents state: STOP-ONLY was designed in recoverability v1-r2 cycles after a post-hoc diagnosis on the v1 evaluation pairs. Its official confirmation passed 32/32 pairs, with a conditional stopping gain of 0.221 (95% CI [0.205, 0.237]) relative to DIRECT, a readout that scores 0% complete. Whole-output recall was 0.33% OLD and 11.26% NEW. It was the largest run in the sample (225,792 native record applications). One delivery later, address_capacity cycle 1 re-scored the official checkpoints. A fixed endpoint at length 1 reached 10.645% NEW against STOP's 11.263% (+0.62pp), and on OLD reached 0.977% against STOP's 0.326%. The report notes that 'the official historical confirmation is unchanged'. Inference: the gate was compared against the weakest internal reference and conditioned on payload being correct, so it could pass without meaningful memory. The strongest trivial countermodel was missing from the preregistered gate.

minifly_recoverability_v1_dev_20261022/cycles/CYCLE3_REVIEW.md:9 (post-hoc diagnosis → 'Propose one smaller EOS-only learned correction'); cycles/BYPASS_POSTHOC.log, DIAGNOSE.log
minifly_recoverability_v1_r2_dev_20261023/REPORT.md (A: gate conditioned on evaluator-only native payload correctness)
findings.how_detected: Caught after the official run by the next delivery's cycle 1 re-analysis (address_capacity, 2026-10-23). The cycles that designed the gate did not catch it.
findings.generic_safeguard: A strongest-trivial-baseline rule. Every primary gate must beat a sweep of trivial countermodels: constant, fixed length 0–8, marginal or frequency, position-only, FROZEN, SHUF. A gate that only compares against an internal reference is not enough. Metrics conditioned on correctness may not be primary. Before any confirmation, run the baseline sweep on dev data and require a margin that rests on candidate-blind reasoning.

findings.title: Cycle 3 often stands in for the official run: verdicts rest on 1–2 development or engineering worlds
findings.description: Documents state: in addition_rule, v3, v4, v5.1-R2, v6_r1, memory_channel, recoverability v1/r2, address_capacity, transformer_external_memory and earned_authority, the delivery verdict comes from cycle 3's fixed roster, typically 1–2 worlds, with no separate confirmation. Most such verdicts are negative or 'NO_ADVANCE', so the false-positive risk is limited. The one positive E3 signal (addition_rule, 87.5%, 2 worlds) followed directly from in-cycle mechanism selection (C2). In autonomous_observation, cycle 2 failed on one world (unchanged keys 75% < 85%). Cycle 3 then passed on the preregistered equal-weight mean of 4 new worlds. That was legitimate, but a mean gate can absorb a failing world. Inference: the program's 'test run x3 → official run' sequence collapses in practice to 'cycle 3 = result'. Null pilots are seldom accompanied by a power statement.
evidence: minifly_v6_r1_dev_20261023/cycles/03_PRE_RUN_REVIEW.md:3 and REPORT.md:3 (cycle 3 is the fixed roster; verdict)
findings.how_detected: Not caught; the delivery reports do label these as engineering or development evidence.
findings.generic_safeguard: Label cycle-3 outcomes as pilot results with n stated and a minimum detectable effect. A positive pilot cannot be reported as a delivery verdict without a frozen-design confirmation on untouched worlds. Mean gates also require a per-world floor, or report the worst world as a co-gate.

findings.title: The fixed count of three cycles pads some exercises, truncates others, and makes staged prerequisite failures expensive
findings.description:
Documents state:
- Padding: AUDIT.md is byte-identical across all three multimechanism cycles; CYCLE_REPORT is templated in feedback_rule_v2 and stream_transfer; v5.1-R2's DESIGN_REVIEW is one line; v6_r1's cycle 2 reruns cycle 1; representation_learning's cycle 3 repeats cycle 2's technical world.
- Truncation: addition_rule says 'No fourth cycle', and observation_content_core says '不追加第四轮', even though both exercises end with a partial signal.
- Expensive staging: in v5.1 the cycles were staged prerequisites and stopped at the first failure. The Claude audit notes that 'the failure was visible from the random starting values in about a second, yet it cost a full cycle plus a design revision' and that this was 'the third version in a row' to stop before the arithmetic hypothesis. Codex corrected this for v3.
- learned_bank notes: task validity was tested only after a full native T-MOD run, and should be a cheap cycle 0.
Inference: the number 3 is a budget, not a stopping rule. It also works as an unstated budget of design alternatives (see C2).
evidence: git show origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/NOTES_FOR_SKILLS_SESSION.md §3 ('Task validity was tested too late… cheap cycle 0')
findings.how_detected: External Claude audit of v5.1 (2026-10-20) and the learned_bank notes (2026-10-24). The other cases are not flagged.
findings.generic_safeguard:
Replace 'three cycles' with an exit-criteria contract:
- Cycle 0 (minutes, not hours) checks that the testbed can test the claim: BP or oracle learns, frozen or shortcut fails. It also runs the whole chain on tiny data.
- Every later cycle must produce a pre-run prediction, at least one seeded bug caught, a categorised revision ledger, and an explicit decision: continue, revise, stop or escalate.
- The exercise ends on a decision, not a count, with a declared maximum on SCI revisions and on compute.

findings.title: Post-hoc diagnosis on evaluation worlds steers the next design toward component proxies
findings.description:
Documents state:
- recoverability v1 cycle 3: after every cell failed, post-hoc DIAGNOSE and BYPASS analyses on the same pairs led to the EOS-only STOP design, which went on to R2 and the official run.
- earned_authority: the gating rule was revised after a read-only census of the existing official 48-world ERROR data, labelled exploratory and 'rather than claiming fresh evidence'.
- address_capacity: cycle 1 re-scored the official STOP-ONLY worlds.
- learned_bank: D3 was used for surrogate tuning and then for the native dress rehearsal, recorded as development only.
Each was disclosed, and later evaluation used fresh worlds. Inference: the main risk is not leakage but proxy-chasing. Every redesign targets the component the last diagnosis lit up (stopping, then address capacity). The E3 endpoint did not move: whole-output OLD stays near 0%, and none of the later designs stated how the change would raise unseen-addition accuracy.
evidence: earned_authority_v1_20261007/cycles/cycle2/DESIGN_AUDIT_REVISION.md:3,9 (inert halving; revised-rule census on 48-world ERROR data, exploratory)
git show origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/cycles/CYCLE3.md ('D3 … is therefore a second native development confirmation, not evidence')
findings.how_detected: The world-reuse items were self-disclosed. The proxy-chasing pattern was not flagged anywhere I found.
findings.generic_safeguard: Hypotheses derived after the fact carry a tag naming the worlds they came from, and may be tested only on fresh worlds. Each new design states its predicted effect on the program-level E3 endpoint, not only on the diagnosed component. Two consecutive component-only advances with a flat E3 endpoint force an escalation review of the route.

findings.title: Cycle reviews are self-audits; independent review is rare, and it catches what the cycles miss
findings.description: Documents state: cycle plans record 'review': 'self-audit'. Reports say 'self-audits plus a separate reducing process, not independent reviewer approval' and 'author-run … not independent human or multi-agent review'. The cross-agent Claude audit of v5.1 found three defects the cycles missed (A3–A5). In the learned_bank notes, Claude records Codex catching its earlier overclaims, and its own near miss: writing 'balanced accuracies recomputed by hand and match' before running that check. Inference: within-cycle 'audit' is mostly the same agent re-reading its own work, and claims in notes can run ahead of the evidence.
evidence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/V51_CLAUDE_AUDIT_RECONCILIATION_20261020/AUDIT.json (verdict MAIN_DIAGNOSIS_SUPPORTED_R1_INCOMPLETE; A3–A5; interpretation.process 'Artifact reproducibility checks were insufficient as design and integration validation')
git show origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/NOTES_FOR_SKILLS_SESSION.md §1 ('A claim written before its check'; 'An independent reviewer (Codex) caught them')
findings.how_detected: Cross-agent audits (Claude on Codex v5.1; Codex on Claude summaries) and Claude's own notes.
findings.generic_safeguard: At least one adversarial reviewer from a different agent signs off each cycle against a red-team checklist covering vacuous tests, trivial baselines, amendment motives and lineage changes. Every sentence in a cycle note that claims a check passed must cite an artifact whose timestamp precedes the note; enforce this mechanically.

findings.title: Practices that worked and should be kept as skill primitives
findings.description:
Documents state these good patterns:
- transformer_external_memory cycle 1 includes a seeded positive control: 'Deliberately collapsed slots give 100%, so the measurement detects the intended failure'. Each cycle plan was hash-locked, with PLAN_LOCKED_BEFORE_EXECUTION.
- addition_efficiency found at cycle 3 that 'even a perfect candidate has less than the frozen 5pp headroom' and kept the result instead of changing the endpoint.
- associative_retrieval's cycle-3 design was 'written before full development results are inspected'.
- mechanism_transfer adopted 'genuine receipt passes before tamper rejection is credited'.
- Failed worlds were never restarted: fresh technical worlds were used after failures (sample_gen 835008; v4 4451/4452 and 4461/4462).
- learned_bank's run.check_lock refuses main worlds unless every hash and setting matches LOCK.json, and it uses a mechanical decision rule.
- 63 failure artifacts are preserved across cycle directories.
Inference: these are the reusable elements. The weak point is that they appear inconsistently, one delivery at a time.
evidence: git show origin/charming-head:minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/NOTES_FOR_SKILLS_SESSION.md §2 (lock guard, arm set, mechanical rule)
findings.how_detected: Not applicable (positive practices).
findings.generic_safeguard: Make these mandatory and shared rather than optional: a hash-locked plan per cycle, a seeded positive and negative control per metric, positive-before-tamper ordering, no restarting of a failed world, a lock guard on evaluation worlds, and a mechanical decision script.

process_observations: Sample: 36 of 39 cycle-bearing deliveries, from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-24. That is 35 on the main checkout plus minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024 on origin/charming-head. Main-branch commits are authored 'Pencilbard', so authorship is mostly inferred from each delivery's own wording. Not covered: arithmetic_source_derived_kernel, addition_observation_support (only its failure dirs were inspected), r_center_compact_ablation.

Revision tally, my classification and approximate, about 140 revisions:
- measurement/reducer: 40 (29%)
- ops/infrastructure: 39 (28%)
- test-assumption/fixture: 19 (14%)
- learner-implementation bug: 8 (6%)
- scientific parameter/mechanism: 13 (9%)
- world/seed change: 10 (7%, almost all fresh technical worlds after a failed attempt)
- scope reduction/deferral: 7 (5%)
- gate/criterion change: 4 (3%)
Engineering (ops + test + measurement + implementation) is about 76%; science + gate + scope is about 17%.

Scientific endpoint coverage in the cycles: never examined in 13 of 36 (for example mechanism_transfer, representation_learning, value_interaction, feedback_efficiency, sample_gen, multimechanism, uncertainty_restoration, schedule_context, native_bind v1/v2.1, r_center_core, v5.1, native_next). Examined only in cycle 3 in about 14 of 36. Examined every cycle in about 5 (addition_rule, value_retention, observation_content_core, autonomous_observation, transformer_external_memory).

About 11 deliveries end with cycle 3 as the verdict and have no separate official run. Of the cycle-3 outcomes where the endpoint was measured, the only positive held-out E3 signal is addition_rule (87.5%, 2 worlds, engineered ordinal prior). The rest are null or hold.

Revisions made after seeing endpoint outcome data: about 10 instances across 8 deliveries (addition_rule ×2, observation_content_core ×2, earned_authority, autonomous_observation, v4 scope, recoverability v1 redesign, memory_channel EOS pooling, learned_bank amendment). Subsequent evaluation used fresh worlds in all but three world-reuse cases: earned_authority's census of existing official data, address_capacity's re-analysis of the official worlds, and learned_bank's D3 tuning followed by rehearsal. All three were disclosed as non-evidence.

Preregistration: revision policy was preregistered in only a few cases (addition_rule EXPERIMENT.md:21; autonomous_observation's 4-world cycle-3 mean; v5.1's ordered calibration grid). The specific scientific changes were not preregistered. Per-cycle hash-locked plans exist only in the 10-22/23 Claude-era style deliveries (memory_channel, transformer_external_memory) and in learned_bank's LOCK.json.

Fix-until-pass: I found no case of a scientific gate loosened until it passed. Engineering fix-until-pass is common, the extreme being v4 cycle 3 with 5 failed attempts and 2 world changes. I found 7 tests that would have passed regardless of correctness, or were mis-specified, all detected one cycle or more later (C4).

Cycle-note language: of 168 cycle .md files, 81 contain 'no parameter changed / not selected on scores' disclaimers. 48 mention tamper or negative controls. None contains a researcher-level falsifiable prediction; the 12 'predict/预测' hits all refer to the model's byte predictions. Templated or identical per-cycle docs appear in at least 4 deliveries.

Failures: 63 failure artifacts are preserved under cycles/ directories. Import or module-name collision appears in at least 10 deliveries, and fly_id, JSON tuple/list and numpy-type defects recur. These are knowledge that does not transfer across deliveries.

Effort judgement: cycles mostly buy pipeline correctness (receipts, checkpoints, tamper suites, resume) rather than scientific information. The science they yield is either absent (blind cycles) or arrives as a single pilot at cycle 3. Research-level transfer between experiments shows up only in prose design citations and occasional cross-agent audits; I found no machine-readable findings ledger except the one proposed in the learned_bank notes.

skill_recommendations.name: cycle-exit-contract
skill_recommendations.rationale: There is no falsifiable prediction in any of 168 cycle notes. Templated or identical cycle docs (C9), cycles spent rerunning import fixes, and 'no fourth cycle' truncation all show that the count is a budget, not a stopping rule.

skill_recommendations.name: cycle-zero-testbed-and-chain-smoke
skill_recommendations.rule:
Before the design is frozen, run a cycle 0 in minutes:
(a) Testbed validity on the exact split and code. An oracle or exact-gradient learner must succeed, and frozen-random-features, shortcut and constant baselines must fail. Otherwise the task cannot test the claim.
(b) Whole-chain smoke on tiny data through every stage (encoder → classes → address → port → teaching → generation), with progress curves at each stage.
(c) A cheap taught-acquisition (E1) floor.
Failing (a) or (c) blocks the design. A failure there is information, not a result.
skill_recommendations.rationale: learned_bank showed that T-MOD was unlearnable even by BP and that CARRY/CMP are solved by frozen features (C3). In v5.1 the failure was visible in about 1 second but cost a full cycle (C9). v6_r1 ran 34,816 records with taught accuracy at 0% (C1).

skill_recommendations.name: revision-ledger-and-forking-budget
skill_recommendations.rationale: addition_rule's three sequential designs with an engineered prior became a drift node (C2). observation_content_core changed its primary endpoint to a dimension favouring B after B failed protection (C3). learned_bank itself calls amendments the main drift channel.

skill_recommendations.name: mutation-tested-qualification
skill_recommendations.rule: Every qualification check must ship with at least one seeded fault it rejects: wrong sign, identical arms, collapsed slots, wrong label, structured shuffle. Run the positive control first, so that a genuine artifact passes before any tamper rejection counts. Use representative state: nonzero state, overlapping patterns, the declared activity density.
